explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.OreLocalization.ore_right_cancel: If two elements multiplied by a common factor from a submonoid are equal, then there exists another factor such that multiplying it by the first element yields the same result as multiplying it by the second element.

explanatories.Submonoid.smul_def: The action of scalar multiplication by an element of a submonoid is equivalent to the same scalar multiplication by that element regarded as a member of the underlying monoid.
explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.

OreLocalization.oreEqv.fullDefinition: def oreEqv : Setoid (X × S) where   r rs rs' := ∃ (u : S) (v : R), u • rs'.1 = v • rs.1 ∧ u * rs'.2 = v * rs.2   iseqv := by     refine ⟨fun _ => ⟨1, 1, by simp⟩, ?_, ?_⟩     · rintro ⟨r, s⟩ ⟨r', s'⟩ ⟨u, v, hru, hsu⟩; dsimp only at *       rcases oreCondition (s : R) s' with ⟨r₂, s₂, h₁⟩       rcases oreCondition r₂ u with ⟨r₃, s₃, h₂⟩       have : r₃ * v * s = s₃ * s₂ * s := by         -- Porting note: the proof used `assoc_rw`         rw [mul_assoc _ (s₂ : R), h₁, ← mul_assoc, h₂, mul_assoc, ← hsu, ← mul_assoc]       rcases ore_right_cancel (r₃ * v) (s₃ * s₂) s this with ⟨w, hw⟩       refine ⟨w * (s₃ * s₂), w * (r₃ * u), ?_, ?_⟩ <;>         simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, Submonoid.smul_def, ← hw]       · simp only [mul_smul, hru, ← Submonoid.smul_def]       · simp only [mul_assoc, hsu]     · rintro ⟨r₁, s₁⟩ ⟨r₂, s₂⟩ ⟨r₃, s₃⟩ ⟨u, v, hur₁, hs₁u⟩ ⟨u', v', hur₂, hs₂u⟩       rcases oreCondition v' u with ⟨r', s', h⟩; dsimp only at *       refine ⟨s' * u', r' * v, ?_, ?_⟩ <;>         simp only [Submonoid.smul_def, Submonoid.coe_mul, mul_smul, mul_assoc] at *       · rw [hur₂, smul_smul, h, mul_smul, hur₁]       · rw [hs₂u, ← mul_assoc, h, mul_assoc, hs₁u]

OreLocalization.expand.description: The fraction formed by an element from a type divided by an element from a submonoid can be expressed as the product of an arbitrary factor with the same fraction, provided that the product of the factor and the submonoid element remains in the submonoid.

Fractions which differ by a factor of the numerator can be proven equal if
those factors expand to equal elements of `R`.

OreLocalization.liftExpand.fullDefinition: def liftExpand {C : Sort*} (P : X → S → C)     (hP : ∀ (r : X) (t : R) (s : S) (ht : t * s ∈ S), P r s = P (t • r) ⟨t * s, ht⟩) :     X[S⁻¹] → C :=   Quotient.lift (fun p : X × S => P p.1 p.2) fun (r₁, s₁) (r₂, s₂) ⟨u, v, hr₂, hs₂⟩ => by     dsimp at *     have s₁vS : v * s₁ ∈ S := by       rw [← hs₂, ← S.coe_mul]       exact SetLike.coe_mem (u * s₂)     replace hs₂ : u * s₂ = ⟨_, s₁vS⟩ := by ext; simp [hs₂]     rw [hP r₁ v s₁ s₁vS, hP r₂ u s₂ (by norm_cast; rwa [hs₂]), ← hr₂]     simp only [← hs₂]; rfl
OreLocalization.liftExpand.description: A function defined on a type and a submonoid can be extended to the Ore localization of that type if it remains unchanged when elements are multiplied on the left by elements from the monoid.

OreLocalization.liftExpand_of.description: The expansion of a lift through a function on an Ore division yields the same result as applying the function directly to the original element and the submonoid element.

OreLocalization.lift₂Expand.code:
OreLocalization.lift₂Expand.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} [Monoid R] {S : Submonoid R} [OreSet S] {X : Type u_3}
  [MulAction R X] {C : Sort u_2} (P : X → ↥S → X → ↥S → C)
  (hP :
    ∀ (r₁ : X) (t₁ : R) (s₁ : ↥S) (ht₁ : t₁ * ↑s₁ ∈ S) (r₂ : X) (t₂ : R) (s₂ : ↥S) (ht₂ : t₂ * ↑s₂ ∈ S),
      P r₁ s₁ r₂ s₂ = P (t₁ • r₁) ⟨t₁ * ↑s₁, ht₁⟩ (t₂ • r₂) ⟨t₂ * ↑s₂, ht₂⟩) :
  OreLocalization S X → OreLocalization S X → C
OreLocalization.lift₂Expand.comment:
A version of `liftExpand` used to simultaneously lift functions with two arguments
in `X[S⁻¹]`.

explanatories.OreLocalization.liftExpand: A function defined on a type and a submonoid can be extended to the Ore localization of that type if it remains unchanged when elements are multiplied on the left by elements from the monoid.
explanatories.OreLocalization.liftExpand_of: The expansion of a lift through a function on an Ore division yields the same result as applying the function directly to the original element and the submonoid element.

OreLocalization.lift₂Expand.fullDefinition: def lift₂Expand {C : Sort*} (P : X → S → X → S → C)     (hP :       ∀ (r₁ : X) (t₁ : R) (s₁ : S) (ht₁ : t₁ * s₁ ∈ S) (r₂ : X) (t₂ : R) (s₂ : S)         (ht₂ : t₂ * s₂ ∈ S),         P r₁ s₁ r₂ s₂ = P (t₁ • r₁) ⟨t₁ * s₁, ht₁⟩ (t₂ • r₂) ⟨t₂ * s₂, ht₂⟩) :     X[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] → C :=   liftExpand     (fun r₁ s₁ => liftExpand (P r₁ s₁) fun r₂ t₂ s₂ ht₂ => by       have := hP r₁ 1 s₁ (by simp) r₂ t₂ s₂ ht₂       simp [this])     fun r₁ t₁ s₁ ht₁ => by     ext x; induction' x with r₂ s₂     dsimp only     rw [liftExpand_of, liftExpand_of, hP r₁ t₁ s₁ ht₁ r₂ 1 s₂ (by simp)]; simp
OreLocalization.lift₂Expand.description: This definition describes a method for expanding functions with two arguments in the context of Ore localization, which allows for the simultaneous lifting of these functions from a type to its Ore localization.

OreLocalization.lift₂Expand_of.description: The result establishes that when expanding a certain operation defined on elements of a type divided by a submonoid element, the outcome is equivalent to performing the operation directly on the original elements, under a specific condition relating their scaled representations.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def smul'' (r : R) (s : S) : X[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] :=   liftExpand (smul' r s) fun r₁ r₂ s' hs => by     rcases oreCondition r s' with ⟨r₁', s₁', h₁⟩     rw [smul'_char _ _ _ _ _ _ h₁]     rcases oreCondition r ⟨_, hs⟩ with ⟨r₂', s₂', h₂⟩     rw [smul'_char _ _ _ _ _ _ h₂]     rcases oreCondition (s₁' : R) (s₂') with ⟨r₃', s₃', h₃⟩     have : s₃' * r₁' * s' = (r₃' * r₂' * r₂) * s' := by       rw [mul_assoc, ← h₁, ← mul_assoc, h₃, mul_assoc, h₂]       simp [mul_assoc]     rcases ore_right_cancel _ _ _ this with ⟨s₄', h₄⟩     have : (s₄' * r₃') * (s₂' * s) ∈ S := by       rw [mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc r₃', ← h₃]       exact (s₄' * (s₃' * s₁' * s)).2     rw [OreLocalization.expand' _ _ (s₄' * s₃'), OreLocalization.expand _ (s₂' * s) _ this]     simp only [Submonoid.smul_def, Submonoid.coe_mul, smul_smul, mul_assoc, h₄]     congr 1     ext; simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, ← mul_assoc]     rw [mul_assoc (s₄' : R), h₃, ← mul_assoc]

OreLocalization.smul.fullDefinition: protected def smul : R[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] :=   liftExpand smul'' fun r₁ r₂ s hs => by     ext x     induction' x with x s₂     show OreLocalization.smul' r₁ s x s₂ = OreLocalization.smul' (r₂ * r₁) ⟨_, hs⟩ x s₂     rcases oreCondition r₁ s₂ with ⟨r₁', s₁', h₁⟩     rw [smul'_char _ _ _ _ _ _ h₁]     rcases oreCondition (r₂ * r₁) s₂ with ⟨r₂', s₂', h₂⟩     rw [smul'_char _ _ _ _ _ _ h₂]     rcases oreCondition (s₂' * r₂) (s₁') with ⟨r₃', s₃', h₃⟩     have : s₃' * r₂' * s₂ = r₃' * r₁' * s₂ := by       rw [mul_assoc, ← h₂, ← mul_assoc _ r₂, ← mul_assoc, h₃, mul_assoc, h₁, mul_assoc]     rcases ore_right_cancel _ _ _ this with ⟨s₄', h₄⟩     have : (s₄' * r₃') * (s₁' * s) ∈ S := by       rw [← mul_assoc, mul_assoc _ r₃', ← h₃, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, mul_assoc]       exact mul_mem (s₄' * s₃' * s₂').2 hs     rw [OreLocalization.expand' (r₂' • x) _ (s₄' * s₃'), OreLocalization.expand _ _ _ this]     simp only [Submonoid.smul_def, Submonoid.coe_mul, smul_smul, mul_assoc, h₄]     congr 1     ext; simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, ← mul_assoc]     rw [mul_assoc _ r₃', ← h₃, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc]

OreLocalization.universalMulHom.fullDefinition: def universalMulHom : R[S⁻¹] →* T where   -- Porting note(#12129): additional beta reduction needed   toFun x :=     x.liftExpand (fun r s => ((fS s)⁻¹ : Units T) * f r) fun r t s ht => by       simp only [smul_eq_mul]       have : (fS ⟨t * s, ht⟩ : T) = f t * fS s := by         simp only [← hf, MonoidHom.map_mul]       conv_rhs =>         rw [MonoidHom.map_mul, ← one_mul (f r), ← Units.val_one, ← mul_right_inv (fS s)]         rw [Units.val_mul, mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc _ (fS s : T), ← this, ← mul_assoc]       simp only [one_mul, Units.inv_mul]   map_one' := by beta_reduce; rw [OreLocalization.one_def, liftExpand_of]; simp   map_mul' x y := by     -- Porting note: `simp only []` required, not just for beta reductions     beta_reduce     simp only [] -- TODO more!     induction' x with r₁ s₁     induction' y with r₂ s₂     rcases oreDivMulChar' r₁ r₂ s₁ s₂ with ⟨ra, sa, ha, ha'⟩; rw [ha']; clear ha'     rw [liftExpand_of, liftExpand_of, liftExpand_of, Units.inv_mul_eq_iff_eq_mul, map_mul, map_mul,       Units.val_mul, mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc (fS s₁ : T), ← mul_assoc (fS s₁ : T), Units.mul_inv,       one_mul, ← hf, ← mul_assoc, ← map_mul _ _ r₁, ha, map_mul, hf s₂, mul_assoc,       ← mul_assoc (fS s₂ : T), (fS s₂).mul_inv, one_mul]
OreLocalization.universalMulHom.description: This definition describes a universal morphism that extends a given homomorphism from a monoid to another while ensuring that elements from a submonoid map to units in the target monoid.

OreLocalization.universalMulHom_apply.description: Applying a universal multiplication homomorphism to a fraction in the Ore localization results in the product of the inverse of the associated homomorphism value for the submonoid element and the homomorphism value of the original element.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def add' (r₂ : X) (s₂ : S) : X[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] :=   (--plus tilde       Quotient.lift       fun r₁s₁ : X × S => add'' r₁s₁.1 r₁s₁.2 r₂ s₂) <| by     -- Porting note: `assoc_rw` & `noncomm_ring` were not ported yet     rintro ⟨r₁', s₁'⟩ ⟨r₁, s₁⟩ ⟨sb, rb, hb, hb'⟩     -- s*, r*     rcases oreCondition (s₁' : R) s₂ with ⟨rc, sc, hc⟩     --s~~, r~~     rcases oreCondition rb sc with ⟨rd, sd, hd⟩     -- s#, r#     dsimp at *     rw [add''_char _ _ _ _ rc sc hc (sc * s₁').2]     have : sd * sb * s₁ = rd * rc * s₂ := by       rw [mul_assoc, hb', ← mul_assoc, hd, mul_assoc, hc, ← mul_assoc]     rw [add''_char _ _ _ _ (rd * rc : R) (sd * sb) this (sd * sb * s₁).2]     rw [mul_smul, ← Submonoid.smul_def sb, hb, smul_smul, hd, oreDiv_eq_iff]     use 1     use rd     simp only [mul_smul, smul_add, one_smul, OneMemClass.coe_one, one_mul, true_and]     rw [this, hc, mul_assoc]

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def add : X[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] → X[S⁻¹] := fun x =>   Quotient.lift (fun rs : X × S => add' rs.1 rs.2 x)     (by       rintro ⟨r₁, s₁⟩ ⟨r₂, s₂⟩ ⟨sb, rb, hb, hb'⟩       induction' x with r₃ s₃       show add'' _ _ _ _ = add'' _ _ _ _       dsimp only at *       rcases oreCondition (s₃ : R) s₂ with ⟨rc, sc, hc⟩       rcases oreCondition rc sb with ⟨rd, sd, hd⟩       have : rd * rb * s₁ = sd * sc * s₃ := by         rw [mul_assoc, ← hb', ← mul_assoc, ← hd, mul_assoc, ← hc, mul_assoc]       rw [add''_char _ _ _ _ rc sc hc (sc * s₃).2]       rw [add''_char _ _ _ _ _ _ this.symm (sd * sc * s₃).2]       refine oreDiv_eq_iff.mpr ?_       simp only [Submonoid.mk_smul, smul_add]       use sd, 1       simp only [one_smul, one_mul, mul_smul, ← hb, Submonoid.smul_def, ← mul_assoc, and_true]       simp only [smul_smul, hd])

explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_eq_of_eq_mk: This theorem asserts that if the underlying elements of a subtype and another element are equal, then the subtype itself is equal to the constructed element from that value.

explanatories.Submonoid.smul_def: The action of scalar multiplication by an element of a submonoid is equivalent to the same scalar multiplication by that element regarded as a member of the underlying monoid.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.Semigroup.mul_assoc: This theorem states that in a semigroup, the multiplication operation is associative, meaning the grouping of the elements does not affect the product.
explanatories.OreLocalization.universalMulHom: This definition describes a universal morphism that extends a given homomorphism from a monoid to another while ensuring that elements from a submonoid map to units in the target monoid.
explanatories.RingHom.toMonoidHom: This defines a way to view a ring homomorphism as a monoid homomorphism between two non-associative semirings.
explanatories.RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe: This theorem asserts that for any ring homomorphism between non-associative semirings, viewing it as a monoid homomorphism yields a consistent identity.
explanatories.OneHom.toFun_eq_coe: This theorem asserts that the function associated with a homomorphism in a structure with a multiplicative identity is equal to its coerced version.
explanatories.MonoidHom.toOneHom_coe: This theorem states that the function associated with a monoid homomorphism can be represented identically whether viewed through its coercion or its direct form.
explanatories.OreLocalization.universalMulHom_apply: Applying a universal multiplication homomorphism to a fraction in the Ore localization results in the product of the inverse of the associated homomorphism value for the submonoid element and the homomorphism value of the original element.
explanatories.MonoidHom.coe_coe: This theorem states that there are no assertions being made in this case.

explanatories.RingHom.map_add: This theorem indicates that a ring homomorphism maintains the property of addition by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.RingHom.map_mul: This theorem states that ring homomorphisms maintain the multiplication structure by ensuring the image of a product equals the product of the images.
explanatories.Units.val_mul: The value of the product of two unit elements in a monoid is equal to the product of their corresponding representation values.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.mul_left_inv: This theorem states that in a group, the product of an element and its inverse equals the identity element.

OreLocalization.universalHom.fullDefinition: def universalHom : R[S⁻¹] →+* T :=   { universalMulHom f.toMonoidHom fS hf with     map_zero' := by       simp only [RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe, OneHom.toFun_eq_coe, MonoidHom.toOneHom_coe]       rw [OreLocalization.zero_def, universalMulHom_apply]       simp     map_add' := fun x y => by       simp only [RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe, OneHom.toFun_eq_coe, MonoidHom.toOneHom_coe]       induction' x with r₁ s₁       induction' y with r₂ s₂       rcases oreDivAddChar' r₁ r₂ s₁ s₂ with ⟨r₃, s₃, h₃, h₃'⟩       rw [h₃']       clear h₃'       simp only [RingHom.toMonoidHom_eq_coe, smul_eq_mul, universalMulHom_apply, MonoidHom.coe_coe,         Submonoid.smul_def]       simp only [mul_inv_rev, MonoidHom.map_mul, RingHom.map_add, RingHom.map_mul, Units.val_mul]       rw [mul_add, mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc _ (f s₃), hf, ← Units.val_mul]       simp only [one_mul, mul_left_inv, Units.val_one]       congr 1       rw [← mul_assoc]       congr 1       norm_cast at h₃       have h₃' := Subtype.coe_eq_of_eq_mk h₃       rw [← Units.val_mul, ← mul_inv_rev, ← fS.map_mul, h₃']       rw [Units.inv_mul_eq_iff_eq_mul, Units.eq_mul_inv_iff_mul_eq, ← hf, ← hf]       simp only [map_mul] }

  {motive : (a a_1 : R) → RingConGen.Rel r a a_1 → Prop} :
  ∀ {a a_1 : R} (t : RingConGen.Rel r a a_1),
    (∀ (x y : R) (a : r x y), motive x y ⋯) →
      (∀ (x : R), motive x x ⋯) →
        (∀ {x y : R} (a : RingConGen.Rel r x y), motive x y a → motive y x ⋯) →
          (∀ {x y z : R} (a : RingConGen.Rel r x y) (a_2 : RingConGen.Rel r y z),
              motive x y a → motive y z a_2 → motive x z ⋯) →
            (∀ {w x y z : R} (a : RingConGen.Rel r w x) (a_2 : RingConGen.Rel r y z),
                motive w x a → motive y z a_2 → motive (w + y) (x + z) ⋯) →
              (∀ {w x y z : R} (a : RingConGen.Rel r w x) (a_2 : RingConGen.Rel r y z),
                  motive w x a → motive y z a_2 → motive (w * y) (x * z) ⋯) →
                motive a a_1 t

TwoSidedIdeal.mk'.fullDefinition: def mk' (carrier : Set R)     (zero_mem : 0 ∈ carrier)     (add_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → x + y ∈ carrier)     (neg_mem : ∀ {x}, x ∈ carrier → -x ∈ carrier)     (mul_mem_left : ∀ {x y}, y ∈ carrier → x * y ∈ carrier)     (mul_mem_right : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → x * y ∈ carrier) : TwoSidedIdeal R where   ringCon :=     { r := fun x y ↦ x - y ∈ carrier       iseqv :=       { refl := fun x ↦ by simpa using zero_mem         symm := fun h ↦ by simpa using neg_mem h         trans := fun {x y z} h1 h2 ↦ by           simpa only [show x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) by abel] using add_mem h1 h2 }       mul' := fun {a b c d} (h1 : a - b ∈ carrier) (h2 : c - d ∈ carrier) ↦ show _ ∈ carrier by         rw [show a * c - b * d = a * (c - d) + (a - b) * d by rw [mul_sub, sub_mul]; abel]         exact add_mem (mul_mem_left h2) (mul_mem_right h1)       add' := fun {a b c d} (h1 : a - b ∈ carrier) (h2 : c - d ∈ carrier) ↦ show _ ∈ carrier by         rw [show a + c - (b + d) = (a - b) + (c - d) by abel]         exact add_mem h1 h2 }
TwoSidedIdeal.mk'.description: A two-sided ideal can be constructed by specifying an underlying set along with proofs that it contains the zero element and is closed under addition, additive negation, and multiplication from either side.

Ideal.iSup_iInf_eq_top_iff_pairwise.code:
Ideal.iSup_iInf_eq_top_iff_pairwise.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] {t : Finset ι}
  (h : t.Nonempty) (I : ι → Ideal R) : ⨆ i ∈ t, ⨅ j ∈ t, ⨅ (_ : j ≠ i), I j = ⊤ ↔ (↑t).Pairwise fun i j => I i ⊔ I j = ⊤
Ideal.iSup_iInf_eq_top_iff_pairwise.comment:
A finite family of ideals is pairwise coprime (that is, any two of them generate the whole ring)
iff when taking all the possible intersections of all but one of these ideals, the resulting family
of ideals still generate the whole ring.

For example with three ideals : `I ⊔ J = I ⊔ K = J ⊔ K = ⊤ ↔ (I ⊓ J) ⊔ (I ⊓ K) ⊔ (J ⊓ K) = ⊤`.

When ideals are all of the form `I i = R ∙ s i`, this is equivalent to the
`exists_sum_eq_one_iff_pairwise_coprime` lemma.

Ideal.iSup_iInf_eq_top_iff_pairwise.description: A finite family of ideals is pairwise coprime if and only if the supremum of the infimums of all but one ideal equals the whole ring.

IsCoprime.code: IsCoprime.{u} {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (x y : R) : Prop
IsCoprime.comment:
The proposition that `x` and `y` are coprime, defined to be the existence of `a` and `b` such
that `a * x + b * y = 1`. Note that elements with no common divisors are not necessarily coprime,
e.g., the multivariate polynomials `x₁` and `x₂` are not coprime.
IsCoprime.fullDefinition: def IsCoprime : Prop :=   ∃ a b, a * x + b * y = 1
IsCoprime.description: Two elements are defined as coprime if there exist coefficients such that their linear combination equals one.

This is the bundled version of `Set.rangeFactorization`.

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.NonUnitalRingHom.mem_srange_self: The output of a non-unital ring homomorphism applied to an element from its domain is always included in the range of that homomorphism.
explanatories.NonUnitalRingHom.codRestrict: The restriction of a non-unital ring homomorphism to a non-unital subsemiring of its codomain is defined under a condition that ensures the image of each element lies within that subsemiring.

  (ha : a ∈ closure s) (hb : b ∈ closure s) (Hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, p x y) (H0_left : ∀ (x : R), p 0 x)
  (H0_right : ∀ (x : R), p x 0) (Hneg_left : ∀ (x y : R), p x y → p (-x) y) (Hneg_right : ∀ (x y : R), p x y → p x (-y))
  (Hadd_left : ∀ (x₁ x₂ y : R), p x₁ y → p x₂ y → p (x₁ + x₂) y)
  (Hadd_right : ∀ (x y₁ y₂ : R), p x y₁ → p x y₂ → p x (y₁ + y₂))
  (Hmul_left : ∀ (x₁ x₂ y : R), p x₁ y → p x₂ y → p (x₁ * x₂) y)
  (Hmul_right : ∀ (x y₁ y₂ : R), p x y₁ → p x y₂ → p x (y₁ * y₂)) : p a b

HahnSeries.ofIterate.fullDefinition: def ofIterate {Γ' : Type*} [PartialOrder Γ'] (x : HahnSeries Γ (HahnSeries Γ' R)) :     HahnSeries (Γ ×ₗ Γ') R where   coeff := fun g => coeff (coeff x g.1) g.2   isPWO_support' := by     refine Set.PartiallyWellOrderedOn.subsetProdLex ?_ ?_     · refine Set.IsPWO.mono x.isPWO_support' ?_       simp_rw [Set.image_subset_iff, support_subset_iff, Set.mem_preimage, Function.mem_support]       exact fun _ ↦ ne_zero_of_coeff_ne_zero     · exact fun a => by simpa [Function.mem_support, ne_eq] using (x.coeff a).isPWO_support'
HahnSeries.ofIterate.description: This defines a transformation that converts a Hahn series with coefficients in another Hahn series into a new Hahn series based on the lexicographic product of the two partially ordered sets.

HahnSeries.addOppositeEquiv.comment:
`addOppositeEquiv` is an additive monoid isomorphism between
Hahn series over `Γ` with coefficients in the opposite additive monoid `Rᵃᵒᵖ`
and the additive opposite of Hahn series over `Γ` with coefficients `R`.

explanatories.AddOpposite.unop: This definition describes a function that retrieves the original element from its representation in the additive opposite type.

HahnModule.code:
HahnModule.{u_5, u_6, u_7} (Γ : Type u_5) (R : Type u_6) (V : Type u_7) [PartialOrder Γ] [Zero V] [SMul R V] :
  Type (max u_5 u_7)
HahnModule.comment:
We introduce a type alias for `HahnSeries` in order to work with scalar multiplication by
series. If we wrote a `SMul (HahnSeries Γ R) (HahnSeries Γ V)` instance, then when
`V = HahnSeries Γ R`, we would have two different actions of `HahnSeries Γ R` on `HahnSeries Γ V`.
See `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Module` for more discussion on this problem.
HahnModule.fullDefinition: def HahnModule (Γ R V : Type*) [PartialOrder Γ] [Zero V] [SMul R V] :=   HahnSeries Γ V
HahnModule.description: A Hahn module is a type that allows for scalar multiplication in the context of Hahn series, helping to address the complications that arise from defining these operations with the same series type.

  HahnSeries Γ V ≃ HahnModule Γ R V
HahnModule.of.comment: The casting function to the type synonym.

explanatories.Equiv.refl: This definition states that every type is self-equivalent, meaning it has an equivalence relation to itself.

HahnModule.of.fullDefinition: def of (R : Type*) [SMul R V] :     HahnSeries Γ V ≃ HahnModule Γ R V := Equiv.refl _
HahnModule.of.description: There exists an equivalence between Hahn series and Hahn modules defined over a partially ordered set and a vector space.

  [AddCommMonoid V] [SMul R V] [Zero R] (x : HahnSeries Γ R) (y : HahnModule Γ R V) (a : Γ) :
  ((of R).symm (x • y)).coeff a = ∑ ij ∈ addAntidiagonal ⋯ ⋯ a, x.coeff ij.1 • ((of R).symm y).coeff ij.2

explanatories.HahnSeries.smul_coeff: The coefficient of a Hahn series scaled by a scalar is equal to the scalar times the coefficient of the series at that index.

HahnSeries.addVal.comment:
The additive valuation on `HahnSeries Γ R`, returning the smallest index at which
a Hahn Series has a nonzero coefficient, or `⊤` for the 0 series.

explanatories.AddValuation: The type of additive valuations on a ring is defined as those valuations that take values in a specified ordered additive monoid with a top element.
explanatories.WithTop: This definition creates a new type that extends a given type by adding a greatest element.
explanatories.AddValuation.of: An alternate constructor for an additive valuation on a ring provides a way to define it in terms of its behavior on zero, one, and the operations of addition and multiplication without relying on a multiplicative structure.
explanatories.if_pos: If a condition is true, then the result of a conditional expression evaluating that condition will equal the first option.
explanatories.if_neg: If a condition is proven to be false, then the result of a conditional expression will yield the alternative value.
explanatories.one_ne_zero: This theorem demonstrates that one is not equal to zero in any type that supports both one and zero.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.HahnSeries.order_of_ne: The order of a nonzero Hahn series equals the minimum of the values of its supporting indices.
explanatories.HahnSeries.support_nonempty_iff: The support of a Hahn series is nonempty if and only if the series itself is not the zero series.
explanatories.not_false_iff: The statement establishes that the negation of falsehood is logically equivalent to truth.
explanatories.HahnSeries.isWF_support: The support of a Hahn series is a well-founded set, meaning there are no infinite descending sequences within it.
explanatories.WithTop.coe_min: This theorem shows that the minimum of two elements in a linear order can be obtained by taking the minimum of their boxed representations.
explanatories.WithTop.coe_le_coe: This theorem shows that the comparison of two values in an optional type corresponds directly to the comparison of the original values in their inherent order.
explanatories.HahnSeries.min_order_le_order_add: The minimum order of two Hahn series is less than or equal to the order of their sum, provided that the sum is not zero.
explanatories.mul_ne_zero: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.WithTop.coe_add: The coercion of the sum of two elements in a type with addition is equal to the sum of their respective coercions.
explanatories.WithTop.coe_eq_coe: This theorem states that two elements represented in a type that includes a greatest element are equal if and only if their corresponding original elements are equal.
explanatories.HahnSeries.order_mul: The order of the product of two non-zero Hahn series is equal to the sum of their individual orders.
explanatories.Set.Subset.trans: The transitive property of set inclusion states that if one set is included in a second set, and that second set is included in a third set, then the first set is also included in the third set.

HahnSeries.addVal.fullDefinition: def addVal : AddValuation (HahnSeries Γ R) (WithTop Γ) :=   AddValuation.of (fun x => if x = (0 : HahnSeries Γ R) then (⊤ : WithTop Γ) else x.order)     (if_pos rfl) ((if_neg one_ne_zero).trans (by simp [order_of_ne]))     (fun x y => by       by_cases hx : x = 0       · by_cases hy : y = 0 <;> · simp [hx, hy]       · by_cases hy : y = 0         · simp [hx, hy]         · simp only [hx, hy, support_nonempty_iff, if_neg, not_false_iff, isWF_support]           by_cases hxy : x + y = 0           · simp [hxy]           rw [if_neg hxy, ← WithTop.coe_min, WithTop.coe_le_coe]           exact min_order_le_order_add hxy)     fun x y => by     by_cases hx : x = 0     · simp [hx]     by_cases hy : y = 0     · simp [hy]     dsimp only     rw [if_neg hx, if_neg hy, if_neg (mul_ne_zero hx hy), ← WithTop.coe_add, WithTop.coe_eq_coe,       order_mul hx hy]
HahnSeries.addVal.description: The additive valuation for Hahn series yields the least index with a nonzero coefficient or indicates that the series is zero by returning a top element.

HahnSeries.SummableFamily.embDomain.fullDefinition: def embDomain (s : SummableFamily Γ R α) (f : α ↪ β) : SummableFamily Γ R β where   toFun b := if h : b ∈ Set.range f then s (Classical.choose h) else 0   isPWO_iUnion_support' := by     refine s.isPWO_iUnion_support.mono (Set.iUnion_subset fun b g h => ?_)     by_cases hb : b ∈ Set.range f     · dsimp only at h       rw [dif_pos hb] at h       exact Set.mem_iUnion.2 ⟨Classical.choose hb, h⟩     · simp [-Set.mem_range, dif_neg hb] at h   finite_co_support' g :=     ((s.finite_co_support g).image f).subset       (by         intro b h         by_cases hb : b ∈ Set.range f         · simp only [Ne, Set.mem_setOf_eq, dif_pos hb] at h           exact ⟨Classical.choose hb, h, Classical.choose_spec hb⟩         · simp only [Ne, Set.mem_setOf_eq, dif_neg hb, zero_coeff, not_true_eq_false] at h)

HahnSeries.SummableFamily.powers.fullDefinition: def powers (x : HahnSeries Γ R) (hx : 0 < addVal Γ R x) : SummableFamily Γ R ℕ where   toFun n := x ^ n   isPWO_iUnion_support' := isPWO_iUnion_support_powers hx   finite_co_support' g := by     have hpwo := isPWO_iUnion_support_powers hx     by_cases hg : g ∈ ⋃ n : ℕ, { g | (x ^ n).coeff g ≠ 0 }     swap; · exact Set.finite_empty.subset fun n hn => hg (Set.mem_iUnion.2 ⟨n, hn⟩)     apply hpwo.isWF.induction hg     intro y ys hy     refine       ((((addAntidiagonal x.isPWO_support hpwo y).finite_toSet.biUnion fun ij hij =>                     hy ij.snd ?_ ?_).image                 Nat.succ).union             (Set.finite_singleton 0)).subset         ?_     · exact (mem_addAntidiagonal.1 (mem_coe.1 hij)).2.1     · obtain ⟨hi, _, rfl⟩ := mem_addAntidiagonal.1 (mem_coe.1 hij)       rw [← zero_add ij.snd, ← add_assoc, add_zero]       exact         add_lt_add_right (WithTop.coe_lt_coe.1 (lt_of_lt_of_le hx (addVal_le_of_coeff_ne_zero hi)))           _     · rintro (_ | n) hn       · exact Set.mem_union_right _ (Set.mem_singleton 0)       · obtain ⟨i, hi, j, hj, rfl⟩ := support_mul_subset_add_support hn         refine Set.mem_union_left _ ⟨n, Set.mem_iUnion.2 ⟨⟨j, i⟩, Set.mem_iUnion.2 ⟨?_, hi⟩⟩, rfl⟩         simp only [and_true_iff, Set.mem_iUnion, mem_addAntidiagonal, mem_coe, eq_self_iff_true,           Ne, mem_support, Set.mem_setOf_eq]         exact ⟨hj, ⟨n, hi⟩, add_comm j i⟩

ideal.quotient.ring_con.fullDefinition: protected def ringCon (I : Ideal R) : RingCon R :=   { QuotientAddGroup.con I.toAddSubgroup with     mul' := fun {a₁ b₁ a₂ b₂} h₁ h₂ => by       rw [Submodule.quotientRel_r_def] at h₁ h₂ ⊢       have F := I.add_mem (I.mul_mem_left a₂ h₁) (I.mul_mem_right b₁ h₂)       have : a₁ * a₂ - b₁ * b₂ = a₂ * (a₁ - b₁) + (a₂ - b₂) * b₁ := by         rw [mul_sub, sub_mul, sub_add_sub_cancel, mul_comm, mul_comm b₁]       rwa [← this] at F }

Ideal.Quotient.quotient_ring_saturate.code:
Ideal.Quotient.quotient_ring_saturate.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (s : Set R) :
  ⇑(mk I) ⁻¹' (⇑(mk I) '' s) = ⋃ x, (fun y => ↑x + y) '' s
Ideal.Quotient.quotient_ring_saturate.comment:
If `I` is an ideal of a commutative ring `R`, if `q : R → R/I` is the quotient map, and if
`s ⊆ R` is a subset, then `q⁻¹(q(s)) = ⋃ᵢ(i + s)`, the union running over all `i ∈ I`.

Ideal.modulePi.fullDefinition: instance modulePi : Module (R ⧸ I) ((ι → R) ⧸ I.pi ι) where   smul c m :=     Quotient.liftOn₂' c m (fun r m => Submodule.Quotient.mk <| r • m) <| by       intro c₁ m₁ c₂ m₂ hc hm       apply Ideal.Quotient.eq.2       rw [Submodule.quotientRel_r_def] at hc hm       intro i       exact I.mul_sub_mul_mem hc (hm i)   one_smul := by     rintro ⟨a⟩     convert_to Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _ = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _     congr with i; exact one_mul (a i)   mul_smul := by     rintro ⟨a⟩ ⟨b⟩ ⟨c⟩     convert_to Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _ = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _     congr 1; funext i; exact mul_assoc a b (c i)   smul_add := by     rintro ⟨a⟩ ⟨b⟩ ⟨c⟩     convert_to Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _ = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _     congr with i; exact mul_add a (b i) (c i)   smul_zero := by     rintro ⟨a⟩     convert_to Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _ = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _     congr with _; exact mul_zero a   add_smul := by     rintro ⟨a⟩ ⟨b⟩ ⟨c⟩     convert_to Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _ = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _     congr with i; exact add_mul a b (c i)   zero_smul := by     rintro ⟨a⟩     convert_to Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _ = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.pi ι) _     congr with i; exact zero_mul (a i)

ideal.basis_span_singleton.fullDefinition: noncomputable def basisSpanSingleton (b : Basis ι R S) {x : S} (hx : x ≠ 0) :     Basis ι R (span ({x} : Set S)) :=   b.map <|     LinearEquiv.ofInjective (Algebra.lmul R S x) (LinearMap.mul_injective hx) ≪≫ₗ         LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _           (by             ext             simp [mem_span_singleton', mul_comm]) ≪≫ₗ       (Submodule.restrictScalarsEquiv R S S (Ideal.span ({x} : Set S))).restrictScalars R

explanatories.Ideal.gc_map_comap: There exists a Galois connection between the image of an ideal under a ring homomorphism and its preimage, indicating a relationship between these two constructions.
explanatories.Ideal.le_comap_map: An ideal is contained in the preimage of its image under a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.GaloisConnection.monotone_l: The theorem asserts that if two functions form a Galois connection, then the first function is monotone, meaning it preserves the order of inputs in its output.
explanatories.GaloisConnection.monotone_u: The theorem states that if two functions form a Galois connection, then the function mapping from the second set to the first is monotone, preserving the order of the elements.
explanatories.Ideal.map_comap_of_surjective: The image of the preimage of an ideal under a surjective ring homomorphism is equal to the original ideal.
explanatories.GaloisInsertion.monotoneIntro: This definition provides a method to establish a Galois insertion between two ordered sets given certain properties of the functions relating them, including monotonicity and specific order conditions.

Ideal.giMapComap.description: The mapping and preimage under a ring homomorphism form a Galois insertion, meaning they are adjoint operations that satisfy the identity when composed.

RingHom.liftOfRightInverseAux.fullDefinition: def liftOfRightInverseAux (hf : Function.RightInverse f_inv f) (g : A →+* C)     (hg : RingHom.ker f ≤ RingHom.ker g) :     B →+* C :=   { AddMonoidHom.liftOfRightInverse f.toAddMonoidHom f_inv hf ⟨g.toAddMonoidHom, hg⟩ with     toFun := fun b => g (f_inv b)     map_one' := by       rw [← map_one g, ← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub g, ← mem_ker g]       apply hg       rw [mem_ker f, map_sub f, sub_eq_zero, map_one f]       exact hf 1     map_mul' := by       intro x y       rw [← map_mul g, ← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub g, ← mem_ker g]       apply hg       rw [mem_ker f, map_sub f, sub_eq_zero, map_mul f]       simp only [hf _] }

RingHom.liftOfRightInverse.comment:
`liftOfRightInverse f hf g hg` is the unique ring homomorphism `φ`

* such that `φ.comp f = g` (`RingHom.liftOfRightInverse_comp`),
* where `f : A →+* B` has a right_inverse `f_inv` (`hf`),
* and `g : B →+* C` satisfies `hg : f.ker ≤ g.ker`.

See `RingHom.eq_liftOfRightInverse` for the uniqueness lemma.

```
   A .
   |  \
 f |   \ g
   |    \
   v     \⌟
   B ----> C
      ∃!φ
```

RingHom.liftOfRightInverse.fullDefinition: def liftOfRightInverse (hf : Function.RightInverse f_inv f) :     { g : A →+* C // RingHom.ker f ≤ RingHom.ker g } ≃ (B →+* C) where   toFun g := f.liftOfRightInverseAux f_inv hf g.1 g.2   invFun φ := ⟨φ.comp f, fun x hx => (mem_ker _).mpr <| by simp [(mem_ker _).mp hx]⟩   left_inv g := by     ext     simp only [comp_apply, liftOfRightInverseAux_comp_apply, Subtype.coe_mk]   right_inv φ := by     ext b     simp [liftOfRightInverseAux, hf b]
RingHom.liftOfRightInverse.description: The construction associates a unique ring homomorphism from the image of a given ring homomorphism to a target ring, conditioned on the existence of a right inverse for the original homomorphism and the kernel inclusion.

ring_hom.lift_of_right_inverse.code:
RingHom.liftOfRightInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} {C : Type u_3} [Ring A] [Ring B] [Ring C]
  (f : A →+* B) (f_inv : B → A) (hf : Function.RightInverse f_inv ⇑f) : { g // ker f ≤ ker g } ≃ (B →+* C)
ring_hom.lift_of_right_inverse.comment:
`liftOfRightInverse f hf g hg` is the unique ring homomorphism `φ`

* such that `φ.comp f = g` (`RingHom.liftOfRightInverse_comp`),
* where `f : A →+* B` has a right_inverse `f_inv` (`hf`),
* and `g : B →+* C` satisfies `hg : f.ker ≤ g.ker`.

See `RingHom.eq_liftOfRightInverse` for the uniqueness lemma.

```
   A .
   |  \
 f |   \ g
   |    \
   v     \⌟
   B ----> C
      ∃!φ
```

Ideal.pointwiseMulSemiringAction.comment:
The action on an ideal corresponding to applying the action to every element.

This is available as an instance in the `Pointwise` locale.

explanatories.Ideal.map: The image of an ideal under a function from one semiring to another is defined as the span of the images of the elements in the ideal.
explanatories.MulSemiringAction.toRingHom: This definition associates each element of a monoid with a semiring homomorphism that acts on a semiring.
explanatories.RingHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two ring homomorphisms are equal if they yield the same output for every input from the domain.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Ideal.map_id: The image of an ideal under the identity homomorphism is equal to the original ideal itself.
explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.Ideal.map_map: The image of an ideal under the composition of two ring homomorphisms is equal to the image of the ideal under the inner function followed by the outer function.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Ideal.map_bot: The image of the zero ideal under any ring homomorphism is the zero ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.map_sup: The image of the sup of two ideals under a ring homomorphism is equal to the sup of the images of each ideal under the same homomorphism.
explanatories.Ideal.one_eq_top: The ideal generated by the multiplicative identity in a commutative semiring is equal to the entire ring.
explanatories.Ideal.map_top: The image of the top ideal under a function from one semiring to another is again the top ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.map_mul: The image of the product of two ideals under a ring homomorphism is equal to the product of the images of each ideal under that homomorphism.
explanatories.RingEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a ring isomorphism as another ring isomorphism between the respective rings.

Ideal.pointwiseMulSemiringAction.fullDefinition: protected def pointwiseMulSemiringAction : MulSemiringAction M (Ideal R) where   smul a := Ideal.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom _ _ a)   one_smul I :=     congr_arg (I.map ·) (RingHom.ext <| one_smul M) |>.trans I.map_id   mul_smul a₁ a₂ I :=     congr_arg (I.map ·) (RingHom.ext <| mul_smul _ _) |>.trans (I.map_map _ _).symm   smul_one a := by simp only [Ideal.one_eq_top]; exact Ideal.map_top _   smul_mul a I J := Ideal.map_mul (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom _ _ a) I J   smul_add a I J := Ideal.map_sup _ I J   smul_zero a := Ideal.map_bot
Ideal.pointwiseMulSemiringAction.description: The pointwise multiplication semiring action of a monoid on an ideal is defined by applying the action to each element of the ideal.

Ideal.pointwise_smul_def.description: The action of a monoid on an ideal can be expressed as the image of the ideal under the semiring homomorphism associated with the monoid element acting on the ideal.

Ideal.smul_mem_pointwise_smul.code:

Ideal.smul_mem_pointwise_smul.description: If an element belongs to an ideal, then multiplying that element by a monoid element results in a product that belongs to the ideal generated by the action of the monoid on the ideal.

Ideal.mem_pointwise_smul_iff_inv_smul_me.code:

Ideal.mem_pointwise_smul_iff_inv_smul_me.description: An element belongs to the pointwise action of an ideal if and only if the inverse action of that element on the element belongs to the ideal itself.

Ideal.pointwise_smul_le_pointwise_smul_i.code:
Ideal.pointwise_smul_le_pointwise_smul_iff.{u_1, u_2} {M : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Group M] [CommRing R]
  [MulSemiringAction M R] {a : M} {S T : Ideal R} : a • S ≤ a • T ↔ S ≤ T
Ideal.pointwise_smul_le_pointwise_smul_i.description: The pointwise action of an ideal on one ideal being less than or equal to the pointwise action on another ideal is equivalent to the first ideal being less than or equal to the second ideal.

RingHom.kerLift.code: RingHom.kerLift.{u, v} {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [Semiring S] (f : R →+* S) : R ⧸ ker f →+* S
RingHom.kerLift.comment:
The induced map from the quotient by the kernel to the codomain.

This is an isomorphism if `f` has a right inverse (`quotientKerEquivOfRightInverse`) /
is surjective (`quotientKerEquivOfSurjective`).

explanatories.Ideal.Quotient.lift: A ring homomorphism that maps all elements of an ideal to zero can be extended to a homomorphism from the quotient of the ring by that ideal.
explanatories.RingHom.mem_ker: An element belongs to the kernel of a ring homomorphism if and only if it maps to zero under that homomorphism.

  (f : R →+* S) :
  [IsLocalRingHom f, ⇑f '' ↑(maximalIdeal R).toAddSubmonoid ⊆ ↑(maximalIdeal S),
      Ideal.map f (maximalIdeal R) ≤ maximalIdeal S, maximalIdeal R ≤ Ideal.comap f (maximalIdeal S),

explanatories.Ideal.Cotangent: The cotangent of an ideal is defined as the quotient of the ideal by its square.
explanatories.Ideal.toCotangent: This definition describes a linear map that takes elements from an ideal and maps them to their corresponding classes in the cotangent space of that ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.toCotangent_eq: The theorem states that two elements in an ideal yield the same image in the cotangent space if and only if their difference belongs to the square of that ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.toCotangent_surjective: The cotangent map of an ideal is surjective, meaning that every class in the cotangent space can be represented by some element from the ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.cotangentToQuotientSquare: The cotangent of an ideal defines a linear map that sends elements from the cotangent space to the quotient of the ring by the square of the ideal.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.Ideal.toCotangent_to_quotient_square: The theorem states that mapping an element of an ideal to the cotangent space and then to the quotient by the ideal's square gives a specific representation of that element in terms of the ideal's structure.
explanatories.Ideal.cotangentIdeal: The cotangent ideal of an ideal in a commutative ring is defined as the ideal formed by its equivalence classes in the quotient of the ring modulo the square of the ideal.
explanatories.Submodule.Quotient.eq: This theorem states that two elements in a module are equivalent in the quotient structure if and only if their difference is an element of the associated submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.restrictScalars: This definition describes the process of forming an S-submodule from an R-submodule by restricting the scalar multiplication from the semiring R to the semiring S.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Ideal.to_quotient_square_range: The theorem demonstrates that the range of the linear map from the cotangent space of an ideal to the quotient by the square of that ideal is equivalent to the submodule formed by restricting scalars to the ideal's cotangent.
explanatories.LinearMap.codRestrict: This definition describes a linear map that restricts the codomain of a given linear map to a specified submodule, ensuring that all outputs lie within that submodule.
explanatories.LinearMap.mem_range_self: This theorem states that the image of an element under a linear map is always contained in the range of that linear map.
explanatories.Equiv.ofBijective: This definition states that if a function is bijective, then there exists an equivalence relationship between its domain and codomain.
explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element from the base type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.Submodule.mkQ_apply: This theorem verifies that applying the construction of a specific submodule to an element results in the same equivalence class as directly taking the equivalence class of that element in the quotient module formed by the submodule.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.

Ideal.cotangentEquivIdeal.fullDefinition: noncomputable def cotangentEquivIdeal : I.Cotangent ≃ₗ[R] I.cotangentIdeal := by   refine   { LinearMap.codRestrict (I.cotangentIdeal.restrictScalars R) I.cotangentToQuotientSquare       fun x => by { rw [← to_quotient_square_range]; exact LinearMap.mem_range_self _ _ },     Equiv.ofBijective _ ⟨?_, ?_⟩ with }   · rintro x y e     replace e := congr_arg Subtype.val e     obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := I.toCotangent_surjective x     obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := I.toCotangent_surjective y     rw [I.toCotangent_eq]     dsimp only [toCotangent_to_quotient_square, Submodule.mkQ_apply] at e     rwa [Submodule.Quotient.eq] at e   · rintro ⟨_, x, hx, rfl⟩     exact ⟨I.toCotangent ⟨x, hx⟩, Subtype.ext rfl⟩
Ideal.cotangentEquivIdeal.description: The definition establishes a linear equivalence between the cotangent space of an ideal and the ideal formed from the quotient of the ring by the square of that ideal.

explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.Ideal.pow_le_self: The n-th power of an ideal in a semiring is contained within the ideal itself when n is a positive integer.
explanatories.two_ne_zero: This theorem asserts that the number two is not equal to zero in any type that permits both zero and the natural representation of two, assuming two is non-zero.
explanatories.Subsingleton.intro: A type is a subsingleton if it can be shown that all of its elements are equal to each other.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgHom.toRingHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebra homomorphism as a ring homomorphism, preserving the algebraic structures involved.
explanatories.Ideal.Quotient.lift: A ring homomorphism that maps all elements of an ideal to zero can be extended to a homomorphism from the quotient of the ring by that ideal.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply: This theorem shows that in a scalar tower involving two commutative semirings and an algebra, applying the algebra map from the first semiring to the algebra equals applying the algebra map from the second semiring to the algebra after first applying the algebra map from the first semiring to the second semiring.
explanatories.RingHom.toFun_eq_coe: This theorem establishes that the function associated with a ring homomorphism, when viewed as a monoid homomorphism, is equal to the original function defined by that ring homomorphism.

explanatories.AlgHom.map_algebraMap: An algebra homomorphism from one algebra to another preserves the image of the algebra map from a commutative semiring to the respective algebras in a scalar tower.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

AlgHom.kerSquareLift.fullDefinition: def _root_.AlgHom.kerSquareLift (f : A →ₐ[R] B) : A ⧸ RingHom.ker f.toRingHom ^ 2 →ₐ[R] B := by   refine { Ideal.Quotient.lift (RingHom.ker f.toRingHom ^ 2) f.toRingHom ?_ with commutes' := ?_ }   · intro a ha; exact Ideal.pow_le_self two_ne_zero ha   · intro r     rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply R A, RingHom.toFun_eq_coe, Ideal.Quotient.algebraMap_eq,       Ideal.Quotient.lift_mk]     exact f.map_algebraMap r
AlgHom.kerSquareLift.description: The definition establishes a homomorphism from the quotient of a ring by the square of the kernel of a homomorphism to another ring, extending the original mapping to this larger structure.

Ideal.mapCotangent.fullDefinition: def mapCotangent (I₁ : Ideal A) (I₂ : Ideal B) (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (h : I₁ ≤ I₂.comap f) :     I₁.Cotangent →ₗ[R] I₂.Cotangent := by   refine Submodule.mapQ ((I₁ • ⊤ : Submodule A I₁).restrictScalars R)     ((I₂ • ⊤ : Submodule B I₂).restrictScalars R) ?_ ?_   · exact f.toLinearMap.restrict (p := I₁.restrictScalars R) (q := I₂.restrictScalars R) h   · intro x hx     refine Submodule.smul_induction_on hx ?_ (fun _ _ ↦ add_mem)     rintro a ha ⟨b, hb⟩ -     simp only [SetLike.mk_smul_mk, smul_eq_mul, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.restrictScalars_mem]     convert (Submodule.smul_mem_smul (M := I₂) (r := f a)       (n := ⟨f b, h hb⟩) (h ha) (Submodule.mem_top)) using 1     ext     exact _root_.map_mul f a b

Ideal.quotient_mk_maps_eq.comment:
The identity in this lemma asserts that the "obvious" square
```
    R    → (R / (P ∩ R))

R[x] / P → (R / (P ∩ R))[x] / (P / (P ∩ R))
```
commutes.  It is used, for instance, in the proof of `quotient_mk_comp_C_is_integral_of_jacobson`,
in the file `RingTheory.Jacobson`.

IsLocalization.surj.description: The theorem establishes that for any element in the target commutative semiring, there exists an element from a specific submonoid such that their product corresponds to the image of a related element from the source semiring under the algebra map.

explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.eq_iff_exists: This theorem asserts that two elements in a commutative monoid are equal under a localization map if and only if there exists an element in the submonoid such that multiplying it by both elements results in the same product.

IsLocalization.map.comment:
Map a homomorphism `g : R →+* P` to `S →+* Q`, where `S` and `Q` are
localizations of `R` and `P` at `M` and `T` respectively,
such that `g(M) ⊆ T`.

We send `z : S` to `algebraMap P Q (g x) * (algebraMap P Q (g y))⁻¹`, where
`(x, y) : R × M` are such that `z = f x * (f y)⁻¹`.

IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ringEquivOfRingEquiv (h : R ≃+* P) (H : M.map h.toMonoidHom = T) : S ≃+* Q :=   have H' : T.map h.symm.toMonoidHom = M := by     rw [← M.map_id, ← H, Submonoid.map_map]     congr     ext     apply h.symm_apply_apply   { map Q (h : R →+* P) (M.le_comap_of_map_le (le_of_eq H)) with     toFun := map Q (h : R →+* P) (M.le_comap_of_map_le (le_of_eq H))     invFun := map S (h.symm : P →+* R) (T.le_comap_of_map_le (le_of_eq H'))     left_inv := fun x => by       rw [map_map, map_unique _ (RingHom.id _), RingHom.id_apply]       simp     right_inv := fun x => by       rw [map_map, map_unique _ (RingHom.id _), RingHom.id_apply]       simp }
IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv.description: The definition illustrates that if two localizations of a commutative semiring are related by an isomorphism of their original semirings, while preserving the structure of their associated submonoids, then there exists an induced isomorphism between those localizations.

IsLocalization.atUnits.fullDefinition: noncomputable def atUnits (H : M ≤ IsUnit.submonoid R) : R ≃ₐ[R] S := by   refine AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId R S) ⟨?_, ?_⟩   · intro x y hxy     obtain ⟨c, eq⟩ := (IsLocalization.eq_iff_exists M S).mp hxy     obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H c.prop     rwa [← hu, Units.mul_right_inj] at eq   · intro y     obtain ⟨⟨x, s⟩, eq⟩ := IsLocalization.surj M y     obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H s.prop     use x * u.inv     dsimp [Algebra.ofId, RingHom.toFun_eq_coe, AlgHom.coe_mks]     rw [RingHom.map_mul, ← eq, ← hu, mul_assoc, ← RingHom.map_mul]     simp

localizationAlgebra.code:
localizationAlgebra.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (M : Submonoid R) (S : Type u_2) [CommRing S]
  [Algebra R S] {Rₘ : Type u_4} {Sₘ : Type u_5} [CommRing Rₘ] [CommRing Sₘ] [Algebra R Rₘ] [IsLocalization M Rₘ]
  [Algebra S Sₘ] [i : IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S M) Sₘ] : Algebra Rₘ Sₘ
localizationAlgebra.comment:
Definition of the natural algebra induced by the localization of an algebra.
Given an algebra `R → S`, a submonoid `R` of `M`, and a localization `Rₘ` for `M`,
let `Sₘ` be the localization of `S` to the image of `M` under `algebraMap R S`.
Then this is the natural algebra structure on `Rₘ → Sₘ`, such that the entire square commutes,
where `localization_map.map_comp` gives the commutativity of the underlying maps.

This instance can be helpful if you define `Sₘ := Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S M)`,
however we will instead use the hypotheses `[Algebra Rₘ Sₘ] [IsScalarTower R Rₘ Sₘ]` in lemmas
since the algebra structure may arise in different ways.

explanatories.Submonoid.comap: The preimage of a submonoid under a monoid homomorphism constitutes a valid submonoid in the source algebraic structure.
explanatories.Submonoid.le_comap_map: The inclusion of a submonoid in the comap of its image under a homomorphism holds true.
explanatories.IsUnit.map: An additive homomorphism defined on units can be derived from an additive homomorphism operating between two additive monoids.
explanatories.RingHom.toAlgebra: This definition provides a way to construct an algebra over a commutative semiring from a ring homomorphism to another commutative semiring.
explanatories.Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid: This definition provides a way to construct a submonoid in a semiring from a submonoid in a commutative semiring when considering their algebraic relationship.

localizationAlgebra.fullDefinition: noncomputable def localizationAlgebra : Algebra Rₘ Sₘ :=   (map Sₘ (algebraMap R S)         (show _ ≤ (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S M).comap _ from M.le_comap_map) :       Rₘ →+* Sₘ).toAlgebra
localizationAlgebra.description: This definition establishes the natural algebra structure induced by the localization of an algebra over a commutative ring and a submonoid, ensuring compatibility between the localizations of both the algebra and the elements involved.

IsLocalization.algebraMap_eq_map_map_sub.comment:
If the square below commutes, the bottom map is uniquely specified:

  [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [CommRing K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] [CommRing L] [Algebra B L]
  [IsFractionRing B L] {j : A →+* B} (hj : Injective ⇑j) : K →+* L
is_fraction_ring.map.comment:
Given integral domains `A, B` with fields of fractions `K`, `L`
and an injective ring hom `j : A →+* B`, we get a field hom
sending `z : K` to `g (j x) * (g (j y))⁻¹`, where `(x, y) : A × (NonZeroDivisors A)` are
such that `z = f x * (f y)⁻¹`.

explanatories.nonZeroDivisors: This definition denotes the submonoid of a monoid with zero consisting of all non-zero divisors.
explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.IsLocalization.map: This definition outlines a way to map a homomorphism from one localized semiring to another while ensuring that the image of the submonoid under the first semiring is contained within the submonoid of the second semiring.
explanatories.Submonoid.comap: The preimage of a submonoid under a monoid homomorphism constitutes a valid submonoid in the source algebraic structure.
explanatories.nonZeroDivisors_le_comap_nonZeroDivisors: In the context of monoids with zero, the theorem states that when an injective homomorphism is applied, the non-zero divisors of the first monoid are included in the image of the non-zero divisors of the second monoid.

is_fraction_ring.map.fullDefinition: noncomputable def map {A B K L : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [CommRing K]     [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] [CommRing L] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L] {j : A →+* B}     (hj : Injective j) : K →+* L :=   IsLocalization.map L j     (show nonZeroDivisors A ≤ (nonZeroDivisors B).comap j from       nonZeroDivisors_le_comap_nonZeroDivisors_of_injective j hj)
is_fraction_ring.map.description: This definition describes a function that maps elements from the field of fractions of one integral domain to the field of fractions of another integral domain, preserving structure through an injective ring homomorphism between the two domains.

IsFractionRing.fieldEquivOfRingEquiv.comment:
Given integral domains `A, B` and localization maps to their fields of fractions
`f : A →+* K, g : B →+* L`, an isomorphism `j : A ≃+* B` induces an isomorphism of
fields of fractions `K ≃+* L`.

explanatories.mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero: In a monoid with zero, a non-zero element is characterized as being a member of the non-zero divisors if and only if it is not equal to zero.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv: The definition illustrates that if two localizations of a commutative semiring are related by an isomorphism of their original semirings, while preserving the structure of their associated submonoids, then there exists an induced isomorphism between those localizations.
explanatories.RingEquiv.toEquiv: This defines the underlying type equivalence associated with the equivalence of semirings.
explanatories.Equiv.image_eq_preimage: The theorem shows that the image of a set under an equivalence relation is equal to the preimage of that set under the inverse of the same equivalence relation.
explanatories.Set.preimage: The preimage of a set under a function consists of all elements that map into the set when the function is applied.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.RingEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff: A ring isomorphism preserves non-zero elements by ensuring that an element is non-zero in one ring if and only if its image is non-zero in the other ring.

IsFractionRing.fieldEquivOfRingEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def fieldEquivOfRingEquiv [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L] (h : A ≃+* B) :     K ≃+* L :=   ringEquivOfRingEquiv K L h     (by       ext b       show b ∈ h.toEquiv '' _ ↔ _       erw [h.toEquiv.image_eq_preimage, Set.preimage, Set.mem_setOf_eq,         mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero, mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero]       exact h.symm.map_ne_zero_iff)
IsFractionRing.fieldEquivOfRingEquiv.description: This definition states that an isomorphism between two integral domains induces an isomorphism between their corresponding fields of fractions.

FractionRing.comment:
The fraction ring of a commutative ring `R` as a quotient type.

We instantiate this definition as generally as possible, and assume that the
commutative ring `R` is an integral domain only when this is needed for proving.

In this generality, this construction is also known as the *total fraction ring* of `R`.

explanatories.Localization: This definition introduces the concept of the localization of a commutative monoid at a submonoid, represented as a quotient type.

FractionRing.description: This definition introduces the fraction ring of a commutative ring as a type that represents the formal quotients of elements from that ring.

If `A` has an `R`-basis, then localizing `A` at `S` has a basis over `R` localized at `S`.

A suitable instance for `[Algebra A Aₛ]` is `localizationAlgebra`.

explanatories.Basis.ofIsLocalizedModule: The definition describes a construction that allows a basis of a module over a commutative semiring to be extended to a basis of the localized module over that semiring, thereby preserving the basis structure during localization.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.toLinearMap: This definition constructs a linear map from one module to another using a linear equivalence that relates the two modules through compatible ring homomorphisms.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.toAlgHom: This definition states that in a scalar tower, there exists a canonical algebra homomorphism from the middle element to the top element that respects the structure of the bottom element.
explanatories.AlgHom.toLinearMap: This definition establishes a conversion from an algebra homomorphism to a linear map, facilitating the transition between algebraic structures over a commutative semiring and linear mappings.

LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization.comment: An `R`-linear map between two `S⁻¹R`-modules is actually `S⁻¹R`-linear.

explanatories.algebraMap_smul: This theorem states that the action of an element from a commutative semiring on a module through the algebra map is equivalent to the action of that element directly on the module.
explanatories.smul_assoc: This theorem states that in a scalar tower structure involving multiple scalar multiplications, applying the scalars in succession produces the same result as applying the first scalar and then multiplying the outcome by the second scalar.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.IsLocalization.mk'_surjective: The theorem states that every element in the localized structure can be represented as the localization of some pair of elements from the original commutative semiring and its submonoid.
explanatories.IsLocalization.mk': This definition describes a surjective function that maps pairs of an element from a commutative semiring and an element from a submonoid to the target commutative semiring by taking their product and inverting the latter element.
explanatories.SMulCommClass.smul_comm: This theorem states that in the presence of a commutative scalar multiplication structure, the order of multiplying two elements with a third remains unchanged when using scalar multiplication.

LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization.fullDefinition: def LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : M →ₗ[A] N where   toFun := f   map_add' := f.map_add   map_smul' := by     intro r m     simp only [RingHom.id_apply]     rcases mk'_surjective S r with ⟨r, s, rfl⟩     calc f (mk' A r s • m)         = ((s : R) • mk' A 1 s) • f (mk' A r s • m) := by simp       _ = (mk' A 1 s) • (s : R) • f (mk' A r s • m) := by rw [smul_comm, smul_assoc]       _ = (mk' A 1 s) • f ((s : R) • mk' A r s • m) := by simp       _ = (mk' A 1 s) • f (r • m) := by rw [← smul_assoc, smul_mk'_self, algebraMap_smul]       _ = (mk' A 1 s) • r • f m := by simp       _ = mk' A r s • f m := by rw [smul_comm, ← smul_assoc, smul_mk'_one]
LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization.description: This definition specifies a construction for extending a linear map from one module over a commutative semiring to another module over a localized version of that semiring, ensuring that the map retains its linearity in the new algebraic context.

  [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization M S] (I : Ideal R) : Ideal S
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.comment:
Explicit characterization of the ideal given by `Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) I`.
In practice, this ideal differs only in that the carrier set is defined explicitly.
This definition is only meant to be used in proving `mem_map_algebraMap_iff`,
and any proof that needs to refer to the explicit carrier set should use that theorem.

explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.
explanatories.Ideal.add_mem: The sum of any two elements in an ideal of a semiring is also contained within that ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.mul_mem_left: Multiplying an element of an ideal by any other element results in an element that is also within the ideal.
explanatories.RingHom.map_add: This theorem indicates that a ring homomorphism maintains the property of addition by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.Submodule.coe_mk: This theorem states that for an element of a submodule, the natural embedding of that element into the submodule corresponds exactly to the element itself.
explanatories.Submonoid.coe_mul: The product of two elements from a submonoid is equal to the product of their images in the larger monoid.
explanatories.RingHom.map_mul: This theorem states that ring homomorphisms maintain the multiplication structure by ensuring the image of a product equals the product of the images.
explanatories.add_mul: This theorem defines the right distributive property of multiplication over addition in a specific algebraic structure.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.IsLocalization.surj: The theorem establishes that for any element in the target commutative semiring, there exists an element from a specific submonoid such that their product corresponds to the image of a related element from the source semiring under the algebra map.
explanatories.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of two elements is equivalent to their multiplication in a type that has a multiplication operation.
explanatories.map_mul: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def map_ideal (I : Ideal R) : Ideal S where   carrier := { z : S | ∃ x : I × M, z * algebraMap R S x.2 = algebraMap R S x.1 }   zero_mem' := ⟨⟨0, 1⟩, by simp⟩   add_mem' := by     rintro a b ⟨a', ha⟩ ⟨b', hb⟩     let Z : { x // x ∈ I } := ⟨(a'.2 : R) * (b'.1 : R) + (b'.2 : R) * (a'.1 : R),       I.add_mem (I.mul_mem_left _ b'.1.2) (I.mul_mem_left _ a'.1.2)⟩     use ⟨Z, a'.2 * b'.2⟩     simp only [RingHom.map_add, Submodule.coe_mk, Submonoid.coe_mul, RingHom.map_mul]     rw [add_mul, ← mul_assoc a, ha, mul_comm (algebraMap R S a'.2) (algebraMap R S b'.2), ←       mul_assoc b, hb]     ring   smul_mem' := by     rintro c x ⟨x', hx⟩     obtain ⟨c', hc⟩ := IsLocalization.surj M c     let Z : { x // x ∈ I } := ⟨c'.1 * x'.1, I.mul_mem_left c'.1 x'.1.2⟩     use ⟨Z, c'.2 * x'.2⟩     simp only [← hx, ← hc, smul_eq_mul, Submodule.coe_mk, Submonoid.coe_mul, RingHom.map_mul]     ring -- Porting note: removed #align declaration since it is a private def
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: This definition specifies an ideal in a localization of a commutative semiring formed by mapping an ideal from the original ring through the localization process.

  [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization M S] {I : Ideal R} {z : S} :

explanatories.Ideal: An ideal in a semiring is an additive submonoid that is closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring.
explanatories.Ideal.map: The image of an ideal under a function from one semiring to another is defined as the span of the images of the elements in the ideal.

correspond to prime ideals in the original ring `R` that are disjoint from `M`.
This lemma gives the particular case for an ideal and its comap,
see `le_rel_iso_of_prime` for the more general relation isomorphism

IsLocalization.orderIsoOfPrime.description: This definition establishes an order isomorphism between prime ideals in a localization of a ring and the prime ideals in the original ring that are disjoint from a specified submonoid.

IsLocalization.surjective_quotientMap_of.code:
IsLocalization.surjective_quotientMap_of_maximal_of_localization.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R]
  (M : Submonoid R) (S : Type u_2) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization M S] {I : Ideal S} [I.IsPrime]
  {J : Ideal R} {H : J ≤ Ideal.comap (algebraMap R S) I} (hI : (Ideal.comap (algebraMap R S) I).IsMaximal) :
  Function.Surjective ⇑(Ideal.quotientMap I (algebraMap R S) H)
IsLocalization.surjective_quotientMap_of.comment:
`quotientMap` applied to maximal ideals of a localization is `surjective`.
The quotient by a maximal ideal is a field, so inverses to elements already exist,
and the localization necessarily maps the equivalence class of the inverse in the localization

explanatories.AdjoinRoot.algHom_subsingleton: There is only one unique algebra homomorphism from the adjoined root of a polynomial in the form of a constant multiplied by the variable minus one to any commutative ring.
explanatories.Localization.Away: This definition specifies the localization of a commutative monoid at the submonoid generated by a given element.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot: The adjoin of a root of a polynomial to a commutative ring is defined as the quotient of the polynomial ring by the ideal generated by that polynomial.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom: This definition asserts that if there exists an algebra homomorphism between two algebras and its inverse, then the two algebras are isomorphic as algebras over the given commutative semiring.
explanatories.Localization.awayLift: The definition describes a homomorphism from a localization of a commutative semiring, indexed by an invertible element under a specific map, to another commutative semiring.
explanatories.isUnit_of_mul_eq_one: In a commutative monoid, if the product of two elements equals one, then at least one of those elements is a unit.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.root_isInv: The theorem states that for any element in a commutative ring, the product of a specific polynomial evaluated at a root results in one, confirming that the root is indeed an inverse of the polynomial at that point.
explanatories.IsLocalization.Away.AwayMap.lift_eq: The theorem demonstrates that the image of an element under a localization lift map is equal to the image of that element under a given ring homomorphism, provided the image of the specific element is a unit.
explanatories.IsLocalization.Away.invSelf: The property defines a function that returns the inverse of the image of a given element under a localization map associated with a specific element of a commutative semiring.
explanatories.map_sub: The theorem states that additive group homomorphisms maintain the result of subtraction between elements.
explanatories.map_mul: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.

explanatories.Polynomial.aeval_X: This theorem states that evaluating the polynomial variable at a specified element in an R-algebra results in that same element.
explanatories.IsLocalization.Away.mul_invSelf: The theorem establishes that the product of the image of a specific element under a localization map and its associated inverse is equal to one, confirming the inverse relationship in the localization context.
explanatories.Polynomial.aeval_one: This theorem states that evaluating the constant polynomial equal to one at any point in an algebra results in one.
explanatories.sub_self: In an additive group, subtracting an element from itself results in the identity element.
explanatories.Subsingleton.elim: In a subsingleton type, any two elements are equal, demonstrating the uniqueness of elements in such types.
explanatories.IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton: The theorem asserts that when there is a localization of a commutative semiring, any algebra homomorphism from the localized semiring to another commutative semiring is uniquely determined, indicating that there is only one such homomorphism.

Localization.awayEquivAdjoin.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Localization.awayEquivAdjoin (r : R) : Away r ≃ₐ[R] AdjoinRoot (C r * X - 1) :=   AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom     { awayLift _ r       -- Porting note: This argument used to be found automatically, i.e. `_`       (isUnit_of_mul_eq_one ((algebraMap R (AdjoinRoot (C r * X - 1))) r) (root (C r * X - 1))         (root_isInv r)) with       commutes' :=         IsLocalization.Away.AwayMap.lift_eq r (isUnit_of_mul_eq_one _ _ <| root_isInv r) }     (liftHom _ (IsLocalization.Away.invSelf r) <| by       simp only [map_sub, map_mul, aeval_C, aeval_X, IsLocalization.Away.mul_invSelf, aeval_one,         sub_self])     (Subsingleton.elim _ _)     -- Porting note: fix since `IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton` is no local instance anymore     (Subsingleton.elim (h := IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton (Submonoid.powers r)) _ _)

  [hI : I.IsPrime] (J : Ideal P) [J.IsPrime] (f : R →+* P) (hIJ : I = Ideal.comap f J) :
  Localization.AtPrime I →+* Localization.AtPrime J
Localization.localRingHom.comment:
For a ring hom `f : R →+* S` and a prime ideal `J` in `S`, the induced ring hom from the
localization of `R` at `J.comap f` to the localization of `S` at `J`.

To make this definition more flexible, we allow any ideal `I` of `R` as input, together with a proof
that `I = J.comap f`. This can be useful when `I` is not definitionally equal to `J.comap f`.

explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofBijective: A bijective algebra homomorphism can be elevated to an algebra equivalence, establishing a strong correspondence between the two algebras.
explanatories.AlgHom.rangeRestrict: The range restriction of an algebra homomorphism adjusts its codomain to only include the image of the original mapping.
explanatories.Set.surjective_onto_range: The range factorization of a function is surjective, meaning it covers all elements in the range.
explanatories.IsLocalization.lift_injective_iff: The theorem establishes that the injectivity of the lifting operation induced by a localization map is equivalent to the condition that two elements in the source space produce the same image under the algebra map if and only if they yield the same image in the target space through a specified homomorphism.
explanatories.Subtype.ext_iff: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their corresponding values in the underlying set are equal.
explanatories.IsLocalization.injective: The theorem asserts that the algebra homomorphism from a commutative ring to its localization is injective when the submonoid of non-zero divisors is contained in the ring.

Given a commutative ring `A` with fraction ring `K`, and a submonoid `S` of `A` which
contains no zero divisor, this is the localization of `A` at `S`, considered as
a subalgebra of `K` over `A`.

The carrier of this subalgebra is defined as the set of all `x : K` of the form
`IsLocalization.mk' K a ⟨s, _⟩`, where `s ∈ S`.

  [CommRing A] (S : Submonoid A) (hS : S ≤ A⁰) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (B : Type u_3) [CommRing B]

localization.subalgebra.mem_range_map_to.description: The theorem establishes a condition for an element of a field to be in the range of the canonical map from the localization of a commutative ring to its fraction ring, stating that it can be expressed as the quotient of two elements from the ring, with the denominator coming from a specified submonoid.

Localization.subalgebra.ofField.code:
Localization.subalgebra.ofField.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} (K : Type u_2) [CommRing A] (S : Submonoid A) (hS : S ≤ A⁰)
  [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] : Subalgebra A K
Localization.subalgebra.ofField.comment:
Given a domain `A` with fraction field `K`, and a submonoid `S` of `A` which
contains no zero divisor, this is the localization of `A` at `S`, considered as
a subalgebra of `K` over `A`.

The carrier of this subalgebra is defined as the set of all `x : K` of the form
`algebraMap A K a * (algebraMap A K s)⁻¹` where `a s : A` and `s ∈ S`.

explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.
explanatories.Subalgebra.copy: This definition creates a copy of a subalgebra using a new carrier that is equal to the original, facilitating adjustments for definitional equalities.
explanatories.Localization.subalgebra.mem_range_mapToF: The theorem establishes a condition for an element of a field to be in the range of the canonical map from the localization of a commutative ring to its fraction ring, stating that it can be expressed as the quotient of two elements from the ring, with the denominator coming from a specified submonoid.

Localization.subalgebra.ofField.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofField : Subalgebra A K :=   (mapToFractionRing K S (Localization S) hS).range.copy       { x | ∃ (a s : A) (_ : s ∈ S), x = algebraMap A K a * (algebraMap A K s)⁻¹ } <| by     ext     symm     apply mem_range_mapToFractionRing_iff_ofField
Localization.subalgebra.ofField.description: This definition describes the localization of a domain at a submonoid as a subalgebra of its fraction field, consisting of elements represented as the products of images from the ring and the inverses of images from the submonoid.

Module.Finite.of_localizationSpan_finite.code:
Module.Finite.of_localizationSpan_finite'.{u, w, u_1} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M]
  [Module R M] (t : Finset R) (ht : Ideal.span ↑t = ⊤) {Mₚ : { x // x ∈ t } → Type u_1}
  [(g : { x // x ∈ t }) → AddCommMonoid (Mₚ g)] [(g : { x // x ∈ t }) → Module R (Mₚ g)] {Rₚ : { x // x ∈ t } → Type u}
  [(g : { x // x ∈ t }) → CommRing (Rₚ g)] [(g : { x // x ∈ t }) → Algebra R (Rₚ g)]
  [∀ (g : { x // x ∈ t }), IsLocalization.Away (↑g) (Rₚ g)] [(g : { x // x ∈ t }) → Module (Rₚ g) (Mₚ g)]
  [∀ (g : { x // x ∈ t }), IsScalarTower R (Rₚ g) (Mₚ g)] (f : (g : { x // x ∈ t }) → M →ₗ[R] Mₚ g)
  [∀ (g : { x // x ∈ t }), IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers ↑g) (f g)]
  (H : ∀ (g : { x // x ∈ t }), Finite (Rₚ g) (Mₚ g)) : Finite R M
Module.Finite.of_localizationSpan_finite.comment:
If there exists a finite set `{ r }` of `R` such that `Mᵣ` is `Rᵣ`-finite for each `r`,
then `M` is a finite `R`-module.

General version for any modules `Mᵣ` and rings `Rᵣ` satisfying the correct universal properties.
See `Module.Finite.of_localizationSpan_finite` for the specialized version.

See `of_localizationSpan'` for a version without the finite set assumption.

explanatories.Localization.Away: This definition specifies the localization of a commutative monoid at the submonoid generated by a given element.
