  [Algebra R S] {Rₘ : Type u_4} {Sₘ : Type u_5} [CommRing Rₘ] [CommRing Sₘ] [Algebra R Rₘ] [IsLocalization M Rₘ]
  [Algebra S Sₘ] [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S M) Sₘ] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] :
  (IsLocalization.map Sₘ (algebraMap R S) ⋯).IsIntegral
isIntegral_localization.comment:
If `R → S` is an integral extension, `M` is a submonoid of `R`,
`Rₘ` is the localization of `R` at `M`,
and `Sₘ` is the localization of `S` at the image of `M` under the extension map,
then the induced map `Rₘ → Sₘ` is also an integral extension

explanatories.map_one: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.map_update_zero: This theorem states that the output of a multilinear map is zero when one of its input vectors is updated to be zero at any specific coordinate.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a multilinear map preserves addition when one of its inputs is updated with the sum of two elements.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.tprodCoeff: This definition outlines a method for constructing the tensor product of a collection of vectors scaled by a coefficient from a commutative semiring, facilitating specific operations within that context.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.smul_tprodCoeff: This theorem states that scaling an element in a collection of modules followed by an update maintains the equivalence of the tensor product coefficient, appropriately modified by the scaling factor applied to the original coefficient.
explanatories.Commute.tprod: The theorem indicates that if two elements commute in a given structure, then their corresponding tensor products also commute.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.lift.tprod: This theorem establishes that the lift of a multilinear map applied to the tensor product of a collection of modules equals the application of the multilinear map to the collection itself.

PiTensorProduct.singleAlgHom.fullDefinition: def singleAlgHom [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) : A i →ₐ[R] ⨂[R] i, A i where   toFun a := tprod R (MonoidHom.mulSingle _ i a)   map_one' := by simp only [_root_.map_one]; rfl   map_mul' a a' := by simp   map_zero' := MultilinearMap.map_update_zero _ _ _   map_add' _ _ := MultilinearMap.map_add _ _ _ _ _   commutes' r := show tprodCoeff R _ _ = r • tprodCoeff R _ _ by     rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one]     erw [smul_tprodCoeff]     rfl
PiTensorProduct.singleAlgHom.description: This definition provides a homomorphism from an element in a module associated with a specific index to the tensor product of a family of such modules, embedding the element within the tensor product structure.

explanatories.PiTensorProduct.instNonUnitalSemiring: This definition establishes that the tensor product of a family of modules over a commutative semiring possesses the structure of a non-unital semiring.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.instNonAssocSemiring: This definition establishes that the tensor product of a family of modules over a commutative semiring has the properties of a non-associative semiring.

PiTensorProduct.instSemiring.fullDefinition: instance instSemiring : Semiring (⨂[R] i, A i) where   __ := instNonUnitalSemiring   __ := instNonAssocSemiring
PiTensorProduct.instSemiring.description: This definition establishes that the tensor product of a family of algebras over a commutative semiring is itself a semiring.

PiTensorProduct.mul_comm.description: The theorem states that the multiplication in the tensor product of two families of elements over a commutative semiring is commutative.

explanatories.PiTensorProduct.tprod: This definition introduces a multilinear map that constructs the tensor product of a family of modules over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.tprod_mul_tprod: The theorem asserts that the tensor product of two families of elements from a non-unital, non-associative semiring over a commutative semiring corresponds to the multiplication of their respective tensor products.
explanatories.SemiconjBy.tprod: The theorem demonstrates that if one family of elements is semiconjugate to another in a structure, their corresponding tensor products retain this semiconjugate relationship.
explanatories.AlgHom.ofLinearMap: This definition introduces a method to construct an algebra homomorphism from a linear map by proving its behavior with respect to the multiplicative identity and multiplication.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.lift: This definition establishes a linear isomorphism between multilinear maps from a family of modules to an additive commutative monoid and linear maps from the tensor product of those modules to the monoid.
explanatories.Commute.tprod: The theorem indicates that if two elements commute in a given structure, then their corresponding tensor products also commute.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.ext: This theorem establishes that two linear maps from the tensor product of a family of modules to an additive commutative monoid are equal if their compositions with a specific multilinear map are identical.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.ext: This theorem establishes that if two multilinear maps produce the same output for all inputs, then they are equal as maps.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra: This definition specifies a multilinear map that takes a function producing values in a commutative algebra and outputs the product of these values across a finite index set.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom: This definition asserts that if there exists an algebra homomorphism between two algebras and its inverse, then the two algebras are isomorphic as algebras over the given commutative semiring.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.lift.tprod: This theorem establishes that the lift of a multilinear map applied to the tensor product of a collection of modules equals the application of the multilinear map to the collection itself.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Finset.prod_const_one: The product of the constant value one over the elements of any finite set equals one.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra_apply: This theorem states that evaluating a specific type of multilinear map associated with a finite type at a collection of inputs gives the product of the evaluations of those inputs at each index.
explanatories.Pi.mul_apply: There is no content to summarize.
explanatories.Finset.prod_mul_distrib: The product of two functions evaluated over a finite set is equal to the product of the individual products of each function evaluated over the same set.
explanatories.Algebra.ofId: This definition describes a function that represents the algebra map from a commutative semiring to an algebra over that semiring.

PiTensorProduct.constantBaseRingEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def constantBaseRingEquiv : (⨂[R] _ : ι, R) ≃ₐ[R] R :=   letI toFun := lift (MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra R ι R)   AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom     (AlgHom.ofLinearMap       toFun       ((lift.tprod _).trans Finset.prod_const_one)       (by         rw [LinearMap.map_mul_iff]         ext x y         show toFun (tprod R x * tprod R y) = toFun (tprod R x) * toFun (tprod R y)         simp_rw [tprod_mul_tprod, toFun, lift.tprod, MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra_apply,           Pi.mul_apply, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]))     (Algebra.ofId _ _)     (by ext)     (by classical ext)
PiTensorProduct.constantBaseRingEquiv.description: This definition establishes an algebraic equivalence between the tensor product of a finite collection of copies of a commutative semiring and the semiring itself.

  [Semiring A] [Algebra R S] [Algebra S A] [Algebra R A] [IsScalarTower R S A] (r : R)
  [Invertible ((algebraMap R S) r)] : Invertible ((algebraMap R A) r)
IsScalarTower.Invertible.algebraTower.comment:
Suppose that `R → S → A` is a tower of algebras.
If an element `r : R` is invertible in `S`, then it is invertible in `A`.

explanatories.Invertible.copy: This definition states that if an element is invertible and another element is equal to it, then the second element is also invertible.
explanatories.Invertible.map: This definition asserts that monoid homomorphisms maintain the property of invertibility among elements.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply: This theorem shows that in a scalar tower involving two commutative semirings and an algebra, applying the algebra map from the first semiring to the algebra equals applying the algebra map from the second semiring to the algebra after first applying the algebra map from the first semiring to the second semiring.

IsScalarTower.Invertible.algebraTower.fullDefinition: def Invertible.algebraTower (r : R) [Invertible (algebraMap R S r)] :     Invertible (algebraMap R A r) :=   Invertible.copy (Invertible.map (algebraMap S A) (algebraMap R S r)) (algebraMap R A r)     (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply R S A r)
IsScalarTower.Invertible.algebraTower.description: If there is a tower of algebras from one structure to another, and an element is invertible in the second structure, then it is also invertible in the third structure.

Basis.algebraMapCoeffs.{u, w, u_1, u_2} {R : Type u} (A : Type w) {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R]
  [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid M] [Algebra R A] [Module A M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R A M] (b : Basis ι R M)
  (h : Function.Bijective ⇑(algebraMap R A)) : Basis ι A M
Basis.algebraMapCoeffs.comment:
If `R` and `A` have a bijective `algebraMap R A` and act identically on `M`,
then a basis for `M` as `R`-module is also a basis for `M` as `R'`-module.

explanatories.Basis.mapCoeffs: This definition states that if two rings are isomorphic and act identically on a module, then a basis of that module with respect to one ring also serves as a basis with respect to the other ring.
explanatories.RingEquiv.ofBijective: This constructs a ring isomorphism between two non-unital non-associative semirings from a bijective ring homomorphism between them.

Basis.algebraMapCoeffs.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Basis.algebraMapCoeffs : Basis ι A M :=   b.mapCoeffs (RingEquiv.ofBijective _ h) fun c x => by simp
Basis.algebraMapCoeffs.description: If there is a bijective map between two algebras and they act the same way on a module, then a basis for that module over the first algebra serves as a basis over the second algebra as well.

Polynomial.mul_scaleRoots.code:
Polynomial.mul_scaleRoots.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] (p q : R[X]) (r : R) :
  r ^ (p.natDegree + q.natDegree - (p * q).natDegree) • (p * q).scaleRoots r = p.scaleRoots r * q.scaleRoots r
Polynomial.mul_scaleRoots.comment:
Multiplication and `scaleRoots` commute up to a power of `r`. The factor disappears if we
assume that the product of the leading coeffs does not vanish. See `Polynomial.mul_scaleRoots'`.

bernsteinPolynomial.linearIndependent.comment:
The Bernstein polynomials are linearly independent.

We prove by induction that the collection of `bernsteinPolynomial n ν` for `ν = 0, ..., k`
are linearly independent.
The inductive step relies on the observation that the `(n-k)`-th derivative, evaluated at 1,
annihilates `bernsteinPolynomial n ν` for `ν < k`, but has a nonzero value at `ν = k`.

Polynomial.normalizedGcdMonoid.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance (priority := 100) normalizedGcdMonoid : NormalizedGCDMonoid R[X] :=   letI := Classical.decEq R   normalizedGCDMonoidOfExistsLCM fun p q => by     rcases exists_primitive_lcm_of_isPrimitive p.isPrimitive_primPart         q.isPrimitive_primPart with       ⟨r, rprim, hr⟩     refine ⟨C (lcm p.content q.content) * r, fun s => ?_⟩     by_cases hs : s = 0     · simp [hs]     by_cases hpq : C (lcm p.content q.content) = 0     · rw [C_eq_zero, lcm_eq_zero_iff, content_eq_zero_iff, content_eq_zero_iff] at hpq       rcases hpq with (hpq | hpq) <;> simp [hpq, hs]     iterate 3 rw [dvd_iff_content_dvd_content_and_primPart_dvd_primPart hs]     rw [content_mul, rprim.content_eq_one, mul_one, content_C, normalize_lcm, lcm_dvd_iff,       primPart_mul (mul_ne_zero hpq rprim.ne_zero), rprim.primPart_eq,       (isUnit_primPart_C (lcm p.content q.content)).mul_left_dvd, ← hr s.primPart]     tauto

Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv.fullDefinition: def degreeLTEquiv (R) [Semiring R] (n : ℕ) : degreeLT R n ≃ₗ[R] Fin n → R where   toFun p n := (↑p : R[X]).coeff n   invFun f :=     ⟨∑ i : Fin n, monomial i (f i),       (degreeLT R n).sum_mem fun i _ =>         mem_degreeLT.mpr           (lt_of_le_of_lt (degree_monomial_le i (f i)) (WithBot.coe_lt_coe.mpr i.is_lt))⟩   map_add' p q := by     ext     dsimp     rw [coeff_add]   map_smul' x p := by     ext     dsimp     rw [coeff_smul]     rfl   left_inv := by     rintro ⟨p, hp⟩     ext1     simp only [Submodule.coe_mk]     by_cases hp0 : p = 0     · subst hp0       simp only [coeff_zero, LinearMap.map_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero]     rw [mem_degreeLT, degree_eq_natDegree hp0, Nat.cast_lt] at hp     conv_rhs => rw [p.as_sum_range' n hp, ← Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range]   right_inv f := by     ext i     simp only [finset_sum_coeff, Submodule.coe_mk]     rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i, coeff_monomial, if_pos rfl]     · rintro j - hji       rw [coeff_monomial, if_neg]       rwa [← Fin.ext_iff]     · intro h       exact (h (Finset.mem_univ _)).elim
Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv.description: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between the first n coefficients of polynomials with degree less than n and functions that map elements from a finite set of size n to a semiring.

polynomial.degree_lt_equiv.comment: The first `n` coefficients on `degreeLT n` form a linear equivalence with `Fin n → R`.

Multiset.prod_X_add_C_eq_sum_esymm.code:
Multiset.prod_X_add_C_eq_sum_esymm.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] (s : Multiset R) :
  (map (fun r => X + C r) s).prod = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (card s + 1), C (s.esymm j) * X ^ (card s - j)
Multiset.prod_X_add_C_eq_sum_esymm.comment:
A sum version of **Vieta's formula** for `Multiset`: the product of the linear terms `X + λ`
where `λ` runs through a multiset `s` is equal to a linear combination of the symmetric functions
`esymm s` of the `λ`'s .

the product of linear terms `λ + X i` is equal to a linear combination of
the symmetric polynomials `esymm σ R j`.

Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux1.code:
Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux1.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (x : R) :
  (R[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {X - C x}) ≃ₐ[R] R[X] ⧸ RingHom.ker (aeval x).toRingHom

explanatories.Ideal: An ideal in a semiring is an additive submonoid that is closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring.
explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgHom.toRingHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebra homomorphism as a ring homomorphism, preserving the algebraic structures involved.
explanatories.Polynomial.C: This definition specifies a ring homomorphism that maps a constant from a semiring to the corresponding constant polynomial in a polynomial ring.
explanatories.Ideal.span: The ideal generated by a subset of a ring is called the span of that subset.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq: The definition states that two quotient algebras formed by equivalent ideals are isomorphic as algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.ker_evalRingHom: This theorem establishes that the kernel of the evaluation homomorphism at a specific value corresponds to the ideal generated by the polynomial formed by subtracting that value from the indeterminate.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.symm: This definition indicates that every algebra equivalence has a corresponding inverse that switches the roles of the two algebras involved.
explanatories.RingEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a ring isomorphism as another ring isomorphism between the respective rings.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.C: This definition defines a function that takes a value from a commutative semiring and returns the corresponding constant polynomial in the multivariate polynomial type, effectively creating a mapping from the semiring to constant polynomials.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.X: This definition introduces a function that constructs a degree one monomial corresponding to a specific variable in the multivariate polynomial context.

Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux1.fullDefinition: noncomputable def quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux1 (x : R) :     (R[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {X - C x}) ≃ₐ[R] (R[X] ⧸ (RingHom.ker (aeval x).toRingHom : Ideal R[X])) :=   @Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq R R[X] _ _ _ _ _ (ker_evalRingHom x).symm
Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux1.description: There is an algebraic isomorphism between the quotient of the polynomial ring by the ideal generated by the polynomial evaluated at a specific point and the quotient of the polynomial ring by the kernel of the associated evaluation homomorphism.

Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux2.code:
Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux2.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (x : R) :
  (R[X] ⧸ RingHom.ker (aeval x).toRingHom) ≃ₐ[R] R

explanatories.Ideal: An ideal in a semiring is an additive submonoid that is closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring.
explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgHom.toRingHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebra homomorphism as a ring homomorphism, preserving the algebraic structures involved.
explanatories.RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfRightInverse: The definition establishes an isomorphism between the quotient of a ring by the kernel of a homomorphism and the codomain of the homomorphism when there is a right inverse to the homomorphism.
explanatories.Function.RightInverse: This definition describes a relationship where one function serves as a right inverse to another by ensuring the composition of the two produces the identity function.
explanatories.Polynomial.eval_C: This theorem asserts that evaluating the constant polynomial at any point results in the constant value itself.
explanatories.RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply: This theorem shows that applying a ring isomorphism to an element and then its inverse returns the original element.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.X: This definition introduces a function that constructs a degree one monomial corresponding to a specific variable in the multivariate polynomial context.
explanatories.AlgHom.commutes': This theorem states that for an algebra homomorphism between two algebras over a commutative semiring, applying the ring homomorphism form of the algebra homomorphism to an element mapped from the semiring reproduces the mapping of that element in the target algebra.

Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux2.fullDefinition: noncomputable def quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux2 (x : R) :     (R[X] ⧸ (RingHom.ker (aeval x).toRingHom : Ideal R[X])) ≃ₐ[R] R :=   let e := RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfRightInverse (fun x => by     exact eval_C : Function.RightInverse (fun a : R => (C a : R[X])) (@aeval R R _ _ _ x))   { e with commutes' := fun r => e.apply_symm_apply r }
Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquivAux2.description: There is an algebraic isomorphism between the quotient of the polynomial ring by the kernel of the evaluation homomorphism at a specific point and the field of constants represented by that point.

Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquiv.code: Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquiv.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (x : R) : (R[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {X - C x}) ≃ₐ[R] R
Polynomial.quotientSpanXSubCAlgEquiv.comment:

isomorphism of $R$-algebras $R[X] / \langle X - x \rangle \cong R$.

Ideal.eq_zero_of_polynomial_mem_map_range.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R[X])
  (x : ↥((Quotient.mk I).comp C).range) (hx : C x ∈ map (mapRingHom ((Quotient.mk I).comp C).rangeRestrict) I) : x = 0
Ideal.eq_zero_of_polynomial_mem_map_rang.comment:
Given any ring `R` and an ideal `I` of `R[X]`, we get a map `R → R[x] → R[x]/I`.
If we let `R` be the image of `R` in `R[x]/I` then we also have a map `R[x] → R'[x]`.
In particular we can map `I` across this map, to get `I'` and a new map `R' → R'[x] → R'[x]/I`.
This theorem shows `I'` will not contain any non-zero constant polynomials.

dvd_coeff_zero_of_aeval_eq_prime_smul_of.comment:
Let `K` be the field of fraction of an integrally closed domain `R` and let `L` be a separable
extension of `K`, generated by an integral power basis `B` such that the minimal polynomial of
`B.gen` is Eisenstein at `p`. Given `z : L` integral over `R`, if `Q : R[X]` is such that
`aeval B.gen Q = p • z`, then `p ∣ Q.coeff 0`.

explanatories.Submodule.span: This defines the smallest submodule of a module that contains a given set of vectors.
explanatories.Nat.Prime: This definition specifies the criterion for a natural number to be classified as prime, requiring it to be at least two and have only one and itself as divisors.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.IsFractionRing: This definition indicates that a specific structure is recognized as the field of fractions corresponding to a given integral domain.
explanatories.IsIntegrallyClosed: A ring is integrally closed if every element in its field of fractions that satisfies a specific integral condition is also contained within the ring itself.
explanatories.Prime: This definition characterizes an element in a commutative monoid with zero as prime if it is non-zero, not a unit, and divides the product of any two elements if and only if it divides at least one of them.
explanatories.IsIntegral: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is defined as integral if it can be expressed as a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients from that ring.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff: This definition identifies a function that retrieves the coefficient of a specified power in a polynomial over a semiring.
explanatories.minpoly.aeval: An element in an algebra is a root of its minimal polynomial when evaluated at that element.

dvd_coeff_zero_of_aeval_eq_prime_smul_of.description: If a polynomial evaluated at a generator of an integral power basis equals a scalar multiple of an integral element, and the minimal polynomial of that generator is Eisenstein at a prime, then the prime divides the constant term of the polynomial.

explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff: This definition identifies a function that retrieves the coefficient of a specified power in a polynomial over a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.natDegree: This definition assigns a natural number as the degree of a polynomial, explicitly defining the degree of the zero polynomial as zero.
explanatories.minpoly.aeval: An element in an algebra is a root of its minimal polynomial when evaluated at that element.
explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.

mem_adjoin_of_dvd_coeff_of_dvd_aeval.description: If a non-zero polynomial has coefficients divisible by a given non-zero element and evaluates to that element multiplied by another element, then the latter element belongs to the subalgebra generated by the first element.

mem_adjoin_of_smul_prime_smul_of_minpoly.comment:
Let `K` be the field of fraction of an integrally closed domain `R` and let `L` be a separable
extension of `K`, generated by an integral power basis `B` such that the minimal polynomial of
`B.gen` is Eisenstein at `p`. Given `z : L` integral over `R`, if `p • z ∈ adjoin R {B.gen}`, then
`z ∈ adjoin R {B.gen}`.

mem_adjoin_of_smul_prime_pow_smul_of_min.comment:
Let `K` be the field of fraction of an integrally closed domain `R` and let `L` be a separable
extension of `K`, generated by an integral power basis `B` such that the minimal polynomial of
`B.gen` is Eisenstein at `p`. Given `z : L` integral over `R`, if `p ^ n • z ∈ adjoin R {B.gen}`,
then `z ∈ adjoin R {B.gen}`. Together with `Algebra.discr_mul_isIntegral_mem_adjoin` this result
often allows to compute the ring of integers of `L`.

valuation.integer.fullDefinition: def integer : Subring R where   carrier := { x | v x ≤ 1 }   one_mem' := le_of_eq v.map_one   mul_mem' {x y} hx hy := by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, _root_.map_mul, mul_le_one' hx hy]   zero_mem' := by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, _root_.map_zero, zero_le']   add_mem' {x y} hx hy := le_trans (v.map_add x y) (max_le hx hy)   neg_mem' {x} hx := by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx; simpa only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, map_neg]

explanatories.multiplicity.one_right: If an element is not a unit in a commutative monoid, then its multiplicity in one is zero.

  (v : Valuation R Γ₀) {J : Ideal R} (hJ : J ≤ v.supp) : R ⧸ J → Γ₀
Valuation.onQuotVal.comment:
If `hJ : J ⊆ supp v` then `onQuotVal hJ` is the induced function on `R / J` as a function.
Note: it's just the function; the valuation is `onQuot hJ`.

explanatories.Ideal: An ideal in a semiring is an additive submonoid that is closed under multiplication by elements from the semiring.
explanatories.Valuation.supp: The support of a valuation is defined as the ideal in a ring consisting of elements where the valuation evaluates to zero.
explanatories.Quotient.liftOn': This definition describes a variant of a function that processes elements from a quotient type, where the setoid is provided as an implicit argument instead of being an instance.
explanatories.Valuation.map_add_supp: If an element is within the support of a valuation, then adding that element to another does not change the value assigned by the valuation to the second element.
explanatories.Ideal.neg_mem_iff: The membership of the negation of an element in an ideal of a ring is equivalent to the membership of the element itself in that ideal.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.leftRel_apply: This theorem asserts that two elements are equivalent in the quotient group if and only if the product of the inverse of one element and the other element belongs to the corresponding subgroup.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.AddValuation.supp: The support of an additive valuation identifies the ideal in the ring where the valuation takes the maximum value.

Valuation.onQuotVal.fullDefinition: def onQuotVal {J : Ideal R} (hJ : J ≤ supp v) : R ⧸ J → Γ₀ := fun q =>   Quotient.liftOn' q v fun a b h =>     calc       v a = v (b + -(-a + b)) := by simp       _ = v b :=         v.map_add_supp b <| (Ideal.neg_mem_iff _).2 <| hJ <| QuotientAddGroup.leftRel_apply.mp h
Valuation.onQuotVal.description: The induced function on the quotient of a commutative ring by an ideal, under a given valuation, maps elements from the quotient to the valuation's codomain if the ideal is contained within the support of the valuation.

explanatories.Nat.add_sub_of_le: The sum of a natural number and the difference between two natural numbers, where the first is less than or equal to the second, equals the larger number.

valuation_ring.of_discrete_valuation_rin.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) of_discreteValuationRing : ValuationRing A := by   constructor   intro a b   by_cases ha : a = 0; · use 0; right; simp [ha]   by_cases hb : b = 0; · use 0; left; simp [hb]   obtain ⟨ϖ, hϖ⟩ := DiscreteValuationRing.exists_irreducible A   obtain ⟨m, u, rfl⟩ := DiscreteValuationRing.eq_unit_mul_pow_irreducible ha hϖ   obtain ⟨n, v, rfl⟩ := DiscreteValuationRing.eq_unit_mul_pow_irreducible hb hϖ   rcases le_total m n with h | h   · use (u⁻¹ * v : Aˣ) * ϖ ^ (n - m); left     simp_rw [mul_comm (u : A), Units.val_mul, ← mul_assoc, mul_assoc _ (u : A)]     simp only [Units.mul_inv, mul_one, mul_comm _ (v : A), mul_assoc, ← pow_add]     congr 2     exact Nat.add_sub_of_le h   · use (v⁻¹ * u : Aˣ) * ϖ ^ (m - n); right     simp_rw [mul_comm (v : A), Units.val_mul, ← mul_assoc, mul_assoc _ (v : A)]     simp only [Units.mul_inv, mul_one, mul_comm _ (u : A), mul_assoc, ← pow_add]     congr 2     exact Nat.add_sub_of_le h

explanatories.IsLocalization.toLocalizationMap: This definition establishes a mapping that relates a semiring localized at a submonoid to a localization map, confirming that the target semiring reflects the properties of the original semiring under the localization process.
explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.
explanatories.MonoidWithZeroHom.toMonoidHom: This definition describes a way to convert a zero-preserving monoid homomorphism into a standard monoid homomorphism between two monoids.
explanatories.isUnit_iff_ne_zero: This theorem states that in a group with zero, an element is a unit if and only if it is not equal to zero.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift: This definition establishes a method to induce a homomorphism from a localized structure to another commutative monoid, contingent on having an invertible image for every element from the submonoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift_eq: This theorem asserts that if a localization map is lifted under a specific condition that makes the images of elements from a submonoid into another commutative monoid units, then this lifted map evaluates to the same value as a given monoid homomorphism when applied to the original elements of the monoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mk': This definition describes a specific construction of a localized element within a commutative monoid using a localization map by taking an element from the monoid and a corresponding element from a submonoid.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mk'_surjective: This theorem asserts that for any element in the target commutative monoid, there exist corresponding elements in the original monoid and the submonoid that map to it under the specified construction defined by a localization map.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.mk'_eq_iff_eq: This theorem establishes a condition for the equality of two localized elements in terms of the equality of their corresponding images under a localization map applied to products of their components.
explanatories.Submonoid.coe_mul: The product of two elements from a submonoid is equal to the product of their images in the larger monoid.
explanatories.Max.max: A function computes the maximum of two elements from a specified type.
explanatories.IsLocalization.eq_mk'_iff_mul_eq: The theorem establishes that an element from a localized semiring is equivalent to a specific construction if and only if multiplying it by the image of an element from the submonoid equals the image of the original element from the base semiring.
explanatories.add_mul: This theorem defines the right distributive property of multiplication over addition in a specific algebraic structure.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.IsLocalization.mk'_spec: The theorem establishes that when using a specific construction in localization, multiplying the mapped element from the semiring by an element from the submonoid results in the same output as mapping the original element directly.
explanatories.Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift_mk': This theorem demonstrates that the induced homomorphism from the localization of one commutative monoid to another transforms the localized form of a product of elements into a product of their corresponding images under a second homomorphism, while accounting for the inverses of localized units.
explanatories.max_mul_mul_right: This theorem states that the maximum value of two products, formed by multiplying each of two values by a third, is equal to the product of the maximum of the two original values and that third value.
explanatories.mul_le_mul_right': This theorem asserts that if an order relation is preserved under multiplication, then multiplying both sides of an inequality by a common element on the right maintains that inequality.
explanatories.Valuation.map_add: The valuation of the sum of two elements is less than or equal to the maximum of their individual valuations.

Valuation.extendToLocalization.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Valuation.extendToLocalization : Valuation B Γ :=   let f := IsLocalization.toLocalizationMap S B   let h : ∀ s : S, IsUnit (v.1.toMonoidHom s) := fun s => isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 (hS s.2)   { f.lift h with     map_zero' := by convert f.lift_eq (P := Γ) _ 0 <;> simp [f]     map_add_le_max' := fun x y => by       obtain ⟨a, b, s, rfl, rfl⟩ : ∃ (a b : A) (s : S), f.mk' a s = x ∧ f.mk' b s = y := by         obtain ⟨a, s, rfl⟩ := f.mk'_surjective x         obtain ⟨b, t, rfl⟩ := f.mk'_surjective y         use a * t, b * s, s * t         constructor <;>           · rw [f.mk'_eq_iff_eq, Submonoid.coe_mul]             ring_nf       convert_to f.lift h (f.mk' (a + b) s) ≤ max (f.lift h _) (f.lift h _)       · refine congr_arg (f.lift h) (IsLocalization.eq_mk'_iff_mul_eq.2 ?_)         rw [add_mul, _root_.map_add]         iterate 2 erw [IsLocalization.mk'_spec]       iterate 3 rw [f.lift_mk']       rw [max_mul_mul_right]       apply mul_le_mul_right' (v.map_add a b) }

Algebra.adjoinCommSemiringOfComm.fullDefinition: def adjoinCommSemiringOfComm {s : Set A} (hcomm : ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a * b = b * a) :     CommSemiring (adjoin R s) :=   { (adjoin R s).toSemiring with     mul_comm := fun x y => by       ext       simp only [Subalgebra.coe_mul]       exact adjoin_induction₂ x.prop y.prop hcomm (fun _ _ => by rw [commutes])         (fun r x _hx => commutes r x) (fun r x _hx => (commutes r x).symm)         (fun _ _ _ h₁ h₂ => by simp only [add_mul, mul_add, h₁, h₂])         (fun _ _ _ h₁ h₂ => by simp only [add_mul, mul_add, h₁, h₂])         (fun x₁ x₂ y₁ h₁ h₂ => by rw [mul_assoc, h₂, ← mul_assoc y₁, ← h₁, mul_assoc x₁])         fun x₁ x₂ y₁ h₁ h₂ => by rw [mul_assoc x₂, ← h₂, ← mul_assoc x₂, ← h₁, ← mul_assoc] }

fg_of_fg_of_fg.comment:
**Artin--Tate lemma**: if A ⊆ B ⊆ C is a chain of subrings of commutative rings, and
A is noetherian, and C is algebra-finite over A, and C is module-finite over B,
then B is algebra-finite over A.

References: Atiyah--Macdonald Proposition 7.8; Stacks 00IS; Altman--Kleiman 16.17.

explanatories.IsIntegral: An element of an algebra over a commutative ring is defined as integral if it can be expressed as a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients from that ring.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_injective: This theorem states that the mapping from a subtype to its underlying type is injective, meaning that distinct elements in the subtype correspond to distinct elements in the underlying type.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.Algebra.subset_adjoin: The theorem states that any set of elements is contained within the subalgebra generated by that set over a given ring.
explanatories.Set.mem_singleton: An element is a member of the singleton set that contains only that element.
explanatories.isIntegral_algebraMap_iff: An element in an algebra over a commutative ring is integral over that ring if and only if its image under the algebra map to another algebra is also integral over the same ring, provided the algebra map is injective.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Basis.mk: This definition states that a family of vectors is a basis for a module if it is linearly independent and spans the entire module.
explanatories.LinearIndependent: This definition characterizes a family of vectors as linearly independent over a specified ring if no vector in the family can be expressed as a linear combination of the others.
explanatories.linearIndependent_pow: The powers of an element in an algebra, each evaluated at increasing integers, are linearly independent as long as they are less than the degree of the element's minimal polynomial.
explanatories.Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton: The theorem asserts that any element is contained within the subalgebra generated by itself.
explanatories.IsIntegral.mem_span_pow: An integral element in an algebra over a commutative ring belongs to the span of powers of itself if there exists a polynomial for which it can be expressed as the evaluation of that element.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval: This theorem establishes that the smallest subalgebra generated by a single element in an algebra is the same as the range of the evaluation homomorphism at that element.
explanatories.AlgHom.mem_range: An element in the range of an algebra homomorphism corresponds to the existence of a preimage in the domain that maps to it under that homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.aeval_algebraMap_apply: The theorem establishes that evaluating a polynomial at the image of an element under an algebra homomorphism equals applying the homomorphism to the result of evaluating the polynomial at that element.

Algebra.adjoin.powerBasisAux.fullDefinition: noncomputable def adjoin.powerBasisAux {x : S} (hx : IsIntegral K x) :     Basis (Fin (minpoly K x).natDegree) K (adjoin K ({x} : Set S)) := by   have hST : Function.Injective (algebraMap (adjoin K ({x} : Set S)) S) := Subtype.coe_injective   have hx' :     IsIntegral K (⟨x, subset_adjoin (Set.mem_singleton x)⟩ : adjoin K ({x} : Set S)) := by     apply (isIntegral_algebraMap_iff hST).mp     convert hx   apply     @Basis.mk (Fin (minpoly K x).natDegree) _ (adjoin K {x}) fun i =>       ⟨x, subset_adjoin (Set.mem_singleton x)⟩ ^ (i : ℕ)   · have : LinearIndependent K _ := linearIndependent_pow       (⟨x, self_mem_adjoin_singleton _ _⟩ : adjoin K {x})     rwa [← minpoly.algebraMap_eq hST] at this   · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩ _     have := hx'.mem_span_pow (y := ⟨y, hy⟩)     rw [← minpoly.algebraMap_eq hST] at this     apply this     rw [adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval] at hy     obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := (aeval x).mem_range.mp hy     use f     ext     exact aeval_algebraMap_apply S (⟨x, _⟩ : adjoin K {x}) _

explanatories.Subtype.coe_injective: This theorem states that the mapping from a subtype to its underlying type is injective, meaning that distinct elements in the subtype correspond to distinct elements in the underlying type.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.

explanatories.linearIndependent_pow: The powers of an element in an algebra, each evaluated at increasing integers, are linearly independent as long as they are less than the degree of the element's minimal polynomial.

explanatories.Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval: This theorem establishes that the smallest subalgebra generated by a single element in an algebra is the same as the range of the evaluation homomorphism at that element.
explanatories.AlgHom.mem_range: An element in the range of an algebra homomorphism corresponds to the existence of a preimage in the domain that maps to it under that homomorphism.
explanatories.Polynomial.aeval_algebraMap_apply: The theorem establishes that evaluating a polynomial at the image of an element under an algebra homomorphism equals applying the homomorphism to the result of evaluating the polynomial at that element.

PowerBasis.repr_gen_pow_isIntegral.code:
PowerBasis.repr_gen_pow_isIntegral.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {S : Type u_2} [CommRing S] {R : Type u_3} [CommRing R] [Algebra R S]
  {A : Type u_4} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] {B : PowerBasis S A}
  (hB : IsIntegral R B.gen) [IsDomain S] (hmin : minpoly S B.gen = Polynomial.map (algebraMap R S) (minpoly R B.gen))
  (n : ℕ) (i : Fin B.dim) : IsIntegral R ((B.basis.repr (B.gen ^ n)) i)
PowerBasis.repr_gen_pow_isIntegral.comment:
If `B : PowerBasis S A` is such that `IsIntegral R B.gen`, then
`IsIntegral R (B.basis.repr (B.gen ^ n) i)` for all `i` if
`minpoly S B.gen = (minpoly R B.gen).map (algebraMap R S)`. This is the case if `R` is a GCD domain
and `S` is its fraction ring.

explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.symm: This definition indicates that every algebra equivalence has a corresponding inverse that switches the roles of the two algebras involved.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofBijective: A bijective algebra homomorphism can be elevated to an algebra equivalence, establishing a strong correspondence between the two algebras.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.Minpoly.toAdjoin: A surjective algebra morphism is established from the quotient of polynomials by the minimal polynomial of an element to the adjoin of that element over a given ring.
explanatories.injective_iff_map_eq_zero: This theorem asserts that a homomorphism from an additive group to an additive monoid is injective if and only if its kernel contains only the zero element.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.Minpoly.toAdjoin.surjective: The theorem confirms that the map from the minimal polynomial to its adjoin is surjective, meaning every element in the algebra can be reached by applying this map to some polynomial.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.mk_surjective: The theorem asserts that the function mapping elements of the adjoined polynomial structure to its underlying polynomial is surjective.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.mk_eq_zero: The theorem states that the image of an adjoined root is zero if and only if the polynomial divides another polynomial.
explanatories.minpoly.dvd: If an element is a root of a polynomial, then its minimal polynomial divides that polynomial.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.Minpoly.toAdjoin_apply': The theorem demonstrates that the application of the minimal polynomial to an element in an adjoined structure corresponds to the image of that element under a specific homomorphism linked to the minimal polynomial.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.liftHom_mk: The theorem demonstrates that when a polynomial evaluates to zero at a certain point, the homomorphism lifted from that polynomial maps a specific polynomial expression to the evaluation of that expression at the same point.
explanatories.Subalgebra.coe_eq_zero: An element from a subalgebra is equal to zero if and only if its image in the larger algebraic structure is also equal to zero.
explanatories.Polynomial.aeval_subalgebra_coe: This theorem states that evaluating a polynomial within a subalgebra is equivalent to evaluating it after promoting the subalgebra element to the larger algebra.

AlgEquiv.adjoinSingletonEquivAdjoinRootM.fullDefinition: def AlgEquiv.adjoinSingletonEquivAdjoinRootMinpoly {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Algebra F R] (x : R) :     Algebra.adjoin F ({x} : Set R) ≃ₐ[F] AdjoinRoot (minpoly F x) :=   AlgEquiv.symm <| AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Minpoly.toAdjoin F x) <| by     refine ⟨(injective_iff_map_eq_zero _).2 fun P₁ hP₁ ↦ ?_, Minpoly.toAdjoin.surjective F x⟩     obtain ⟨P, rfl⟩ := mk_surjective P₁     refine AdjoinRoot.mk_eq_zero.mpr (minpoly.dvd F x ?_)     rwa [Minpoly.toAdjoin_apply', liftHom_mk, ← Subalgebra.coe_eq_zero, aeval_subalgebra_coe] at hP₁
AlgEquiv.adjoinSingletonEquivAdjoinRootM.description: This definition establishes an algebraic equivalence between the algebra adjoined by a single element and the algebra obtained by adjoining the root of the minimal polynomial of that element.

explanatories.Submodule.subtype: This definition describes a natural linear map that embeds a submodule into the ambient module while retaining the elements' structure.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.

GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [DecidableEq ι] [AddMonoid ι]
  [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] (𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A) [SetLike.GradedMonoid 𝒜]
  (decompose : A →ₐ[R] ⨁ (i : ι), ↥(𝒜 i)) (right_inv : (coeAlgHom 𝒜).comp decompose = AlgHom.id R A)

GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom.comment:
A helper to construct a `GradedAlgebra` when the `SetLike.GradedMonoid` structure is already
available. This makes the `left_inv` condition easier to prove, and phrases the `right_inv`
condition in a way that allows custom `@[ext]` lemmas to apply.

See note [reducible non-instances].

explanatories.DirectSum.decompose: The operation defines an isomorphism between a graded monoid and the direct sum of its components corresponding to specified indices.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.comp: This definition states that the composition of morphisms between additive monoids results in a morphism that also operates within the framework of additive monoids.
explanatories.DirectSum.of: This definition describes the natural inclusion map that embeds an element of an additive commutative monoid into the direct sum of a family of such monoids.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.DirectSum.coeAlgHom: This definition establishes a canonical algebra homomorphism from a direct sum of submodules associated with an indexing set to a semiring.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.AlgHom.id: This definition specifies the identity algebra homomorphism from an algebra to itself over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.AlgHom.congr_fun: This theorem asserts that if two algebra homomorphisms are equal, then they yield the same result when applied to any element from the source algebra.
explanatories.AlgHom.congr_arg: This theorem states that if two elements in an algebra are equal, then the image of these elements under an algebra homomorphism will also be equal.
explanatories.DirectSum.coeAlgHom_of: This theorem asserts that the canonical homomorphism associated with a graded structure and a specific index acts as the identity on elements of the graded component at that index.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.

GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom.fullDefinition: abbrev GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom [SetLike.GradedMonoid 𝒜] (decompose : A →ₐ[R] ⨁ i, 𝒜 i)     (right_inv : (DirectSum.coeAlgHom 𝒜).comp decompose = AlgHom.id R A)     (left_inv : ∀ i (x : 𝒜 i), decompose (x : A) = DirectSum.of (fun i => ↥(𝒜 i)) i x) :     GradedAlgebra 𝒜 where   decompose' := decompose   left_inv := AlgHom.congr_fun right_inv   right_inv := by     suffices decompose.comp (DirectSum.coeAlgHom 𝒜) = AlgHom.id _ _ from AlgHom.congr_fun this     ext i x : 2     exact (decompose.congr_arg <| DirectSum.coeAlgHom_of _ _ _).trans (left_inv i x)
GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom.description: This definition provides a way to construct a graded algebra from a given algebra homomorphism that respects the graded structure, ensuring both left and right inverse properties for decomposition.

explanatories.add_eq_zero_iff: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, the sum of two elements equals zero if and only if both elements are individually zero.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.DirectSum.decompose_of_mem_ne: If an element belongs to one specific submonoid of a direct sum, it must yield zero when projected onto any other submonoid in that sum.
explanatories.not_and_or: This theorem demonstrates that the negation of a conjunction is logically equivalent to the disjunction of the negations of the individual propositions.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.DirectSum.decompose_add: The decomposition operation preserves addition, meaning that the decomposition of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their individual decompositions.
explanatories.DirectSum.add_apply: This theorem establishes that the sum of two elements in the direct sum of additive commutative monoids can be computed component-wise.
explanatories.AddMemClass.coe_add: This theorem demonstrates that the sum of two elements within a set is equal to the sum of their corresponding representations in the additive structure.
explanatories.add_mul: This theorem defines the right distributive property of multiplication over addition in a specific algebraic structure.

GradedRing.projZeroRingHom.fullDefinition: def GradedRing.projZeroRingHom : A →+* A where   toFun a := decompose 𝒜 a 0   map_one' :=     -- Porting note: qualified `one_mem`     decompose_of_mem_same 𝒜 SetLike.GradedOne.one_mem   map_zero' := by     simp only -- Porting note: added     rw [decompose_zero]     rfl   map_add' _ _ := by     simp only -- Porting note: added     rw [decompose_add]     rfl   map_mul' := by     refine DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn 𝒜 (fun x => ?_) ?_ ?_     · simp only [zero_mul, decompose_zero, zero_apply, ZeroMemClass.coe_zero]     · rintro i ⟨c, hc⟩       refine DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn 𝒜 ?_ ?_ ?_       · simp only [mul_zero, decompose_zero, zero_apply, ZeroMemClass.coe_zero]       · rintro j ⟨c', hc'⟩         simp only [Subtype.coe_mk]         by_cases h : i + j = 0         · rw [decompose_of_mem_same 𝒜               (show c * c' ∈ 𝒜 0 from h ▸ SetLike.GradedMul.mul_mem hc hc'),             decompose_of_mem_same 𝒜 (show c ∈ 𝒜 0 from (add_eq_zero_iff.mp h).1 ▸ hc),             decompose_of_mem_same 𝒜 (show c' ∈ 𝒜 0 from (add_eq_zero_iff.mp h).2 ▸ hc')]         · rw [decompose_of_mem_ne 𝒜 (SetLike.GradedMul.mul_mem hc hc') h]           cases' show i ≠ 0 ∨ j ≠ 0 by rwa [add_eq_zero_iff, not_and_or] at h with h' h'           · simp only [decompose_of_mem_ne 𝒜 hc h', zero_mul]           · simp only [decompose_of_mem_ne 𝒜 hc' h', mul_zero]       · intro _ _ hd he         simp only at hd he -- Porting note: added         simp only [mul_add, decompose_add, add_apply, AddMemClass.coe_add, hd, he]     · rintro _ _ ha hb _       simp only at ha hb -- Porting note: added       simp only [add_mul, decompose_add, add_apply, AddMemClass.coe_add, ha, hb]

Ideal.IsHomogeneous.comment:
An `I : Ideal A` is homogeneous if for every `r ∈ I`, all homogeneous components
of `r` are in `I`.

explanatories.DirectSum.decompose: The operation defines an isomorphism between a graded monoid and the direct sum of its components corresponding to specified indices.

Ideal.IsHomogeneous.fullDefinition: def Ideal.IsHomogeneous : Prop :=   ∀ (i : ι) ⦃r : A⦄, r ∈ I → (DirectSum.decompose 𝒜 r i : A) ∈ I
Ideal.IsHomogeneous.description: An ideal is considered homogeneous if it contains all the homogeneous components of its elements.

HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant.code:
HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {A : Type u_4} [Semiring A] [DecidableEq ι]
  [CanonicallyOrderedAddCommMonoid ι] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubmonoidClass σ A] (𝒜 : ι → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] :
  HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜
HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant.comment:
For a graded ring `⨁ᵢ 𝒜ᵢ` graded by a `CanonicallyOrderedAddCommMonoid ι`, the irrelevant ideal
refers to `⨁_{i>0} 𝒜ᵢ`, or equivalently `{a | a₀ = 0}`. This definition is used in `Proj`
construction where `ι` is always `ℕ` so the irrelevant ideal is simply elements with `0` as
0-th coordinate.

# Future work
Here in the definition, `ι` is assumed to be `CanonicallyOrderedAddCommMonoid`. However, the notion
of irrelevant ideal makes sense in a more general setting by defining it as the ideal of elements
with `0` as i-th coordinate for all `i ≤ 0`, i.e. `{a | ∀ (i : ι), i ≤ 0 → aᵢ = 0}`.

explanatories.DirectSum.decompose_zero: The theorem establishes that the decomposition of the zero element in a graded monoid corresponds to the zero element in the direct sum of its components.
explanatories.DirectSum.zero_apply: This theorem establishes that the zero element of the direct sum of additive commutative monoids is equal to the zero element of each individual monoid.

explanatories.GradedRing.projZeroRingHom: This definition establishes a ring homomorphism for the projection of elements from a graded ring to its zeroth component when the grading is defined by a canonically ordered additive monoid.
explanatories.ZeroMemClass.coe_zero: The zero element of a type related to a zero-enabled structure is represented by the zero element itself.
explanatories.DirectSum.decompose_of_mem_ne: If an element belongs to one specific submonoid of a direct sum, it must yield zero when projected onto any other submonoid in that sum.

HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant.fullDefinition: def HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant : HomogeneousIdeal 𝒜 :=   ⟨RingHom.ker (GradedRing.projZeroRingHom 𝒜), fun i r (hr : (decompose 𝒜 r 0 : A) = 0) => by     change (decompose 𝒜 (decompose 𝒜 r _ : A) 0 : A) = 0     by_cases h : i = 0     · rw [h, hr, decompose_zero, zero_apply, ZeroMemClass.coe_zero]     · rw [decompose_of_mem_ne 𝒜 (SetLike.coe_mem _) h]⟩

HomogeneousLocalization.map.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [AddCommMonoid ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] {B : Type u_4}
  [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] (ℬ : ι → Submodule R B) [GradedAlgebra ℬ] {P : Submonoid A} {Q : Submonoid B} (g : A →+* B)
  (comap_le : P ≤ Submonoid.comap g Q) (hg : ∀ (i : ι), ∀ a ∈ 𝒜 i, g a ∈ ℬ i) :
  HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 P →+* HomogeneousLocalization ℬ Q
HomogeneousLocalization.map.comment:
Let `A, B` be two graded algebras with the same indexing set and `g : A → B` be a graded algebra
homomorphism (i.e. `g(Aₘ) ⊆ Bₘ`). Let `P ≤ A` be a submonoid and `Q ≤ B` be a submonoid such that
`P ≤ g⁻¹ Q`, then `g` induce a map from the homogeneous localizations `A⁰_P` to the homogeneous
localizations `B⁰_Q`.

HomogeneousLocalization.map.fullDefinition: def map (g : A →+* B)     (comap_le : P ≤ Q.comap g) (hg : ∀ i, ∀ a ∈ 𝒜 i, g a ∈ ℬ i) :     HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 P →+* HomogeneousLocalization ℬ Q where   toFun := Quotient.map'     (fun x ↦ ⟨x.1, ⟨_, hg _ _ x.2.2⟩, ⟨_, hg _ _ x.3.2⟩, comap_le x.4⟩)     fun x y (e : x.embedding = y.embedding) ↦ by       apply_fun IsLocalization.map (Localization Q) g comap_le at e       simp_rw [HomogeneousLocalization.NumDenSameDeg.embedding, Localization.mk_eq_mk',         IsLocalization.map_mk', ← Localization.mk_eq_mk'] at e       exact e   map_add' := Quotient.ind₂' fun x y ↦ by     simp only [← mk_add, Quotient.map'_mk'', num_add, map_add, map_mul, den_add]; rfl   map_mul' := Quotient.ind₂' fun x y ↦ by     simp only [← mk_mul, Quotient.map'_mk'', num_mul, map_mul, den_mul]; rfl   map_zero' := by simp only [← mk_zero (𝒜 := 𝒜), Quotient.map'_mk'', deg_zero,     num_zero, ZeroMemClass.coe_zero, map_zero, den_zero, map_one]; rfl   map_one' := by simp only [← mk_one (𝒜 := 𝒜), Quotient.map'_mk'', deg_zero,     num_one, ZeroMemClass.coe_zero, map_zero, den_one, map_one]; rfl
HomogeneousLocalization.map.description: This definition describes a process that allows the construction of a homomorphism between two homogeneous localizations of graded algebras that are related through a graded algebra homomorphism and compatible submonoids.

explanatories.Submodule.span: This defines the smallest submodule of a module that contains a given set of vectors.
explanatories.Set.Finite: A set is considered finite if there exists a natural number that demonstrates its equivalence to a finite set of natural numbers.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.Ideal.zero_mem: The zero element belongs to any ideal in a semiring.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.Ideal.add_mem: The sum of any two elements in an ideal of a semiring is also contained within that ideal.
explanatories.AddMemClass.add_mem: This theorem states that a set defined by an addition property is closed under the operation of addition.
explanatories.Submodule.smul_mem: This theorem demonstrates that if an element belongs to a submodule, then its scalar multiplication by any element from the semiring also lies within the same submodule, thereby confirming closure under scalar multiplication.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Set.Finite.image: The image of a finite set under a function is also a finite set.
explanatories.Submodule.span_image: The span of the image of a set under a semilinear map is equal to the image of the span of the original set under that map.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_coe: This theorem states that the range of a linear map can be identified with the set of its output values when applied to its input domain.
explanatories.Submodule.map_top: This theorem establishes that the image of the entire module under a semilinear map is equal to the range of that map.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.range: This theorem establishes that the range of a semilinear equivalence between two modules is the entire target module.
explanatories.Submodule.subset_span: The elements of any set are included in the span of that set's vectors, which is the smallest submodule containing them.
explanatories.Finset.image: This definition specifies a way to obtain the image of a finite set under a given function, producing a new finite set consisting of the outputs of the function applied to each element of the original set.
explanatories.Finset.coe_image: This theorem states that the image of a finite set under a function is equal to the set of images of its elements, as represented by the function application.
explanatories.Inhabited.mk: Any type that has a default element is considered inhabited.
explanatories.Finset.induction: This theorem establishes that a property holds for all finite sets if it holds for the empty set and for any set obtained by inserting an element into another set for which the property already holds.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul: This definition introduces a canonical function that maps elements from two modules over a commutative semiring to their tensor product.
explanatories.Ideal.span: The ideal generated by a subset of a ring is called the span of that subset.
explanatories.Ideal.subset_span: Any set of elements in a semiring is contained within the ideal generated by its span.
explanatories.Module.Finite.out: A module over a semiring is finitely generated if and only if the entire module can be generated by a finite set of elements.
explanatories.Module.Finite.mk: If a module is finitely generated, then it is considered finite as a module over a semiring.
explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.Module.Finite.range: The range of a linear map from a finite module is itself a finite module.
explanatories.eq_top_iff: An element in a partially ordered set is equal to the maximum element if and only if the maximum element is less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.mk: This definition describes a canonical bilinear map that takes an element from one module and another from a second module and produces an element in their tensor product.
explanatories.ZeroMemClass.zero_mem: Any element of a set that belongs to a zero-member class contains the zero element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.isScalarTower_left: This definition asserts that if a scalar tower structure holds for a module, it also holds for the tensor product of that module with another module over a common semiring.
explanatories.Submodule.span_span_of_tower: Taking the span of a set with respect to a larger ring is equivalent to taking the span of the set with respect to the smaller ring and then the larger ring.
explanatories.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of two elements is equivalent to their multiplication in a type that has a multiplication operation.
explanatories.TensorProduct.smul_tmul': This theorem demonstrates that scaling an element from one module before taking its tensor product with an element from another module is equivalent to taking the tensor product first and then scaling, provided both modules are appropriately structured.
explanatories.Set.mem_range_self: An element obtained by applying a function to an index is guaranteed to be part of the range of that function.
explanatories.Submodule.add_mem: This theorem asserts that the sum of two elements from a submodule of a module is also an element of that submodule.

Module.Finite.base_change.fullDefinition: instance Module.Finite.base_change [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommMonoid M]     [Module R M] [h : Module.Finite R M] : Module.Finite A (TensorProduct R A M) := by   classical     obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := h.out     refine ⟨⟨s.image (TensorProduct.mk R A M 1), eq_top_iff.mpr ?_⟩⟩     rintro x -     induction x with     | zero => exact zero_mem _     | tmul x y =>       -- Porting note: new TC reminder       haveI : IsScalarTower R A (TensorProduct R A M) := TensorProduct.isScalarTower_left       rw [Finset.coe_image, ← Submodule.span_span_of_tower R, Submodule.span_image, hs,         Submodule.map_top, LinearMap.range_coe]       change _ ∈ Submodule.span A (Set.range <| TensorProduct.mk R A M 1)       rw [← mul_one x, ← smul_eq_mul, ← TensorProduct.smul_tmul']       exact Submodule.smul_mem _ x (Submodule.subset_span <| Set.mem_range_self y)     | add x y hx hy => exact Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy
Module.Finite.base_change.description: If a module is finitely generated over a commutative ring, then its tensor product with another ring also results in a finitely generated module.

explanatories.MvPolynomial.coeff_add: This theorem asserts that the coefficient of a specific monomial in the sum of two multivariate polynomials is equal to the sum of the coefficients of that monomial in each individual polynomial.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.False.elim: From a contradiction, any proposition can be inferred, illustrating that if something is false, anything follows.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.coeff_zero: This theorem states that the coefficient of the zero polynomial in a multivariate polynomial is zero regardless of the configuration of variables.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.coeff_smul: This theorem states that the coefficient of a specific monomial in a scalar multiplication of a multivariate polynomial is equal to the scalar multiplied by the coefficient of that monomial in the polynomial itself.
explanatories.right_ne_zero_of_mul: This theorem states that in a multiplication structure with zero, if the product of two elements is nonzero, then the second element must also be nonzero.

MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodul.fullDefinition: def weightedHomogeneousSubmodule (w : σ → M) (m : M) : Submodule R (MvPolynomial σ R) where   carrier := { x | x.IsWeightedHomogeneous w m }   smul_mem' r a ha c hc := by     rw [coeff_smul] at hc     exact ha (right_ne_zero_of_mul hc)   zero_mem' d hd := False.elim (hd <| coeff_zero _)   add_mem' {a} {b} ha hb c hc := by     rw [coeff_add] at hc     obtain h | h : coeff c a ≠ 0 ∨ coeff c b ≠ 0 := by       contrapose! hc       simp only [hc, add_zero]     · exact ha h     · exact hb h
MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodul.description: The weighted homogeneous submodule consists of all multivariate polynomials of a specified weighted degree.

explanatories.right_ne_zero_of_mul: This theorem states that in a multiplication structure with zero, if the product of two elements is nonzero, then the second element must also be nonzero.

mv_polynomial.weighted_homogeneous_submo.fullDefinition: def weightedHomogeneousSubmodule (w : σ → M) (m : M) : Submodule R (MvPolynomial σ R) where   carrier := { x | x.IsWeightedHomogeneous w m }   smul_mem' r a ha c hc := by     rw [coeff_smul] at hc     exact ha (right_ne_zero_of_mul hc)   zero_mem' d hd := False.elim (hd <| coeff_zero _)   add_mem' {a} {b} ha hb c hc := by     rw [coeff_add] at hc     obtain h | h : coeff c a ≠ 0 ∨ coeff c b ≠ 0 := by       contrapose! hc       simp only [hc, add_zero]     · exact ha h     · exact hb h

MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodul.comment:
The submodule `weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w m` of homogeneous `MvPolynomial`s of
degree `n` is equal to the `R`-submodule of all `p : (σ →₀ ℕ) →₀ R` such that
`p.support ⊆ {d | weightedDegree w d = m}`. While equal, the former has a
convenient definitional reduction.

explanatories.MvPolynomial.weightedDegree: The weighted degree of a finitely supported function is a linear map that assigns to the function the sum of its weights multiplied by the values according to a specified weight function.
explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.Submodule.subtype: This definition describes a natural linear map that embeds a submodule into the ambient module while retaining the elements' structure.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.Finsupp.restrictDom: This definition describes a linear map that restricts a finitely supported function to only consider values from a specified subset of its domain.

divides the monomial corresponding to `xi`.

of the canonical map `A →ₐ[R] B ⧸ I` corresponds to an `R`-derivation from `A` to `I`.

explanatories.Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ: This defines a canonical algebra morphism from an algebra to its quotient by an ideal.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.diffToIdealOfQuotientCompEq: The difference between two algebra homomorphisms that coincide after quotienting by an ideal can be represented as a linear map from the algebra to the ideal itself.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.diffToIdealOfQuotientCompEq_apply: The application of the defined map for the difference between two algebra homomorphisms that agree when quotiented by an ideal yields the same result as subtracting the outputs of those homomorphisms evaluated at any element of the algebra.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.toAlgHom: This definition states that in a scalar tower, there exists a canonical algebra homomorphism from the middle element to the top element that respects the structure of the bottom element.
explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.

explanatories.sub_self: In an additive group, subtracting an element from itself results in the identity element.
explanatories.Ideal.mem_bot: An element is in the zero ideal if and only if it equals zero.
explanatories.pow_two: This theorem states that in a monoid, the square of an element is equal to the element multiplied by itself.
explanatories.Ideal.mul_mem_mul: The product of any element from one ideal and any element from another ideal is contained in the product of those ideals.
explanatories.Submodule.coe_add: This theorem demonstrates that the operation of addition in a submodule corresponds to the addition in the larger module, ensuring that the sum of two elements from the submodule also belongs to that submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.coe_mk: This theorem states that for an element of a submodule, the natural embedding of that element into the submodule corresponds exactly to the element itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_mk: This theorem asserts that the coercion of a specific additive homomorphism into a linear map retains the property of ensuring the scaling operation is consistently applied to both the original and the resulting functions.
explanatories.Submodule.coe_smul_of_tower: This theorem asserts that when an element from a submodule is scaled by a scalar from a larger structure that acts as a scalar tower, the result remains consistent when viewed in both the submodule and the original module.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom': This theorem asserts that the action of a scalar homomorphism from one commutative semiring to another within a scalar tower is equal to the algebra map from the intermediate semiring to the algebra.
explanatories.LinearMap.toFun_eq_coe: This theorem demonstrates that the function associated with a semilinear map can be represented directly by its lifted form.

explanatories.mul_sub: This theorem expresses the distributive property of multiplication over subtraction in a non-unital non-associative ring.
explanatories.Algebra.smul_def: This theorem asserts that the scalar multiplication of an element in an algebra by a scalar from a commutative semiring can be expressed as the product of the image of that scalar under the algebra map and the algebra element.
explanatories.sub_eq_iff_eq_add: The difference between two elements in an additive group is equal to a third element if and only if the first element is equal to the sum of the second and the third elements.

derivationToSquareZeroOfLift.fullDefinition: def derivationToSquareZeroOfLift (f : A →ₐ[R] B)     (e : (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp f = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A (B ⧸ I)) :     Derivation R A I := by   refine     { diffToIdealOfQuotientCompEq I f (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A B) ?_ with       map_one_eq_zero' := ?_       leibniz' := ?_ }   · rw [e]; ext; rfl   · ext; change f 1 - algebraMap A B 1 = 0; rw [map_one, map_one, sub_self]   · intro x y     let F := diffToIdealOfQuotientCompEq I f (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A B) (by rw [e]; ext; rfl)     have : (f x - algebraMap A B x) * (f y - algebraMap A B y) = 0 := by       rw [← Ideal.mem_bot, ← hI, pow_two]       convert Ideal.mul_mem_mul (F x).2 (F y).2 using 1     ext     dsimp only [Submodule.coe_add, Submodule.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk,       diffToIdealOfQuotientCompEq_apply, Submodule.coe_smul_of_tower, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom',       LinearMap.toFun_eq_coe]     simp only [map_mul, sub_mul, mul_sub, Algebra.smul_def] at this ⊢     rw [sub_eq_iff_eq_add, sub_eq_iff_eq_add] at this     simp only [LinearMap.coe_toAddHom, diffToIdealOfQuotientCompEq_apply, map_mul, this,       IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom']     ring
derivationToSquareZeroOfLift.description: The definition shows that given a tower of algebras with a square-zero ideal, each lift of a canonical algebra map corresponds to a derivation from the base algebra to the ideal.

liftOfDerivationToSquareZero.fullDefinition: def liftOfDerivationToSquareZero (f : Derivation R A I) : A →ₐ[R] B :=   { ((I.restrictScalars R).subtype.comp f.toLinearMap + (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A B).toLinearMap :       A →ₗ[R] B) with     toFun := fun x => f x + algebraMap A B x     map_one' := by       dsimp       -- Note: added the `(algebraMap _ _)` hint because otherwise it would match `f 1`       rw [map_one (algebraMap _ _), f.map_one_eq_zero, Submodule.coe_zero, zero_add]     map_mul' := fun x y => by       have : (f x : B) * f y = 0 := by         rw [← Ideal.mem_bot, ← hI, pow_two]         convert Ideal.mul_mem_mul (f x).2 (f y).2 using 1       simp only [map_mul, f.leibniz, add_mul, mul_add, Submodule.coe_add,         Submodule.coe_smul_of_tower, Algebra.smul_def, this]       ring     commutes' := fun r => by       simp only [Derivation.map_algebraMap, eq_self_iff_true, zero_add, Submodule.coe_zero, ←         IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply R A B r]     map_zero' := ((I.restrictScalars R).subtype.comp f.toLinearMap +       (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A B).toLinearMap).map_zero }

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.MvPowerSeries.coeff_one: The coefficient of the constant multivariate formal power series is one if the multi-index is zero and zero otherwise.
explanatories.Finset.sum_congr: If two finite sets are equal and their corresponding functions yield the same values for all elements, then the sums of those function values over the sets are also equal.

MvPowerSeries.map.fullDefinition: def map : MvPowerSeries σ R →+* MvPowerSeries σ S where   toFun φ n := f <| coeff R n φ   map_zero' := ext fun _n => f.map_zero   map_one' :=     ext fun n =>       show f ((coeff R n) 1) = (coeff S n) 1 by         classical         rw [coeff_one, coeff_one]         split_ifs with h         · simp only [RingHom.map_ite_one_zero, ite_true, map_one, h]         · simp only [RingHom.map_ite_one_zero, ite_false, map_zero, h]   map_add' φ ψ :=     ext fun n => show f ((coeff R n) (φ + ψ)) = f ((coeff R n) φ) + f ((coeff R n) ψ) by simp   map_mul' φ ψ :=     ext fun n =>       show f _ = _ by         classical         rw [coeff_mul, map_sum, coeff_mul]         apply Finset.sum_congr rfl         rintro ⟨i, j⟩ _; rw [f.map_mul]; rfl
MvPowerSeries.map.description: A mapping from multivariate power series over one semiring to another is established through a homomorphism that adjusts their coefficients according to a given function.

MvPowerSeries.coeff_invOfUnit.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Ring R] [DecidableEq σ] (n : σ →₀ ℕ)
  (φ : MvPowerSeries σ R) (u : Rˣ) :
  (coeff R n) (φ.invOfUnit u) =
    if n = 0 then ↑u⁻¹
    else -↑u⁻¹ * ∑ x ∈ antidiagonal n, if x.2 < n then (coeff R x.1) φ * (coeff R x.2) (φ.invOfUnit u) else 0

MvPowerSeries.map.isLocalRingHom.fullDefinition: instance map.isLocalRingHom : IsLocalRingHom (map σ f) :=   ⟨by     rintro φ ⟨ψ, h⟩     replace h := congr_arg (constantCoeff σ S) h     rw [constantCoeff_map] at h     have : IsUnit (constantCoeff σ S ↑ψ) := isUnit_constantCoeff (↑ψ) ψ.isUnit     rw [h] at this     rcases isUnit_of_map_unit f _ this with ⟨c, hc⟩     exact isUnit_of_mul_eq_one φ (invOfUnit φ c) (mul_invOfUnit φ c hc.symm)⟩

IsNoetherian.injective_of_surjective_of_injective.{w, u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type w} [Ring R]
  [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [IsNoetherian R M] (i f : N →ₗ[R] M) (hi : Injective ⇑i)
  (hf : Surjective ⇑f) : Injective ⇑f
IsNoetherian.injective_of_surjective_of_.comment:
**Orzech's theorem** for Noetherian module: if `R` is a ring (not necessarily commutative),
`M` and `N` are `R`-modules, `M` is Noetherian, `i : N →ₗ[R] M` is injective,
`f : N →ₗ[R] M` is surjective, then `f` is also injective. The proof here is adapted from
Djoković's paper *Epimorphisms of modules which must be isomorphisms* [djokovic1973],
utilizing `LinearMap.iterateMapComap`.
See also Orzech's original paper: *Onto endomorphisms are isomorphisms* [orzech1971].

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

IsNoetherian.injective_of_surjective_of_.description: If a linear map from one Noetherian module onto another is surjective and another map from the second module to the first is injective, then the surjective map is also injective.
