PowerSeries.mk_one_pow_eq_mk_choose_add.code:
PowerSeries.mk_one_pow_eq_mk_choose_add.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [CommRing S] (d : ℕ) :
  mk 1 ^ (d + 1) = mk fun n => ↑((d + n).choose d)
PowerSeries.mk_one_pow_eq_mk_choose_add.comment:
Note that `mk 1` is the constant function `1` so the power series `1 + X + X^2 + ...`. This theorem
states that for any `d : ℕ`, `(1 + X + X^2 + ... : S⟦X⟧) ^ (d + 1)` is equal to the power series
`mk fun n => Nat.choose (d + n) d : S⟦X⟧`.

explanatories.Nat.choose: The definition specifies a function that calculates the number of subsets containing a certain number of elements from a set with a specified total number of elements, commonly referred to as binomial coefficients.

PowerSeries.mk_one_pow_eq_mk_choose_add.description: This theorem establishes that raising the power series representing the infinite sum of one and powers of a variable to the power of one more than a natural number produces a new power series whose coefficients correspond to the binomial coefficients from a combinatorial selection.

PowerSeries.mk_one_mul_one_sub_eq_one.comment:
(1 + X + X^2 + ...) * (1 - X) = 1.

Note that the power series `1 + X + X^2 + ...` is written as `mk 1` where `1` is the constant
function so that `mk 1` is the power series with all coefficients equal to one.
PowerSeries.mk_one_mul_one_sub_eq_one.description: This theorem demonstrates that the product of the power series representing the infinite sum of one and powers of a variable with the series that subtracts the variable from one equals one.

PowerSeries.invOneSubPow.comment:
The power series `mk fun n => Nat.choose (d + n) d`, whose multiplicative inverse is
`(1 - X) ^ (d + 1)`.

PowerSeries.firstUnitCoeff.fullDefinition: def firstUnitCoeff {f : k⟦X⟧} (hf : f ≠ 0) : kˣ :=   let d := f.order.get (order_finite_iff_ne_zero.mpr hf)   have f_const : coeff k d f ≠ 0 := by apply coeff_order   have : Invertible (constantCoeff k (divided_by_X_pow_order hf)) := by     apply invertibleOfNonzero     convert f_const using 1     rw [← coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, ← zero_add d]     convert (coeff_X_pow_mul (exists_eq_mul_right_of_dvd (X_pow_order_dvd       (order_finite_iff_ne_zero.mpr hf))).choose d 0).symm     exact (self_eq_X_pow_order_mul_divided_by_X_pow_order hf).symm   unitOfInvertible (constantCoeff k (divided_by_X_pow_order hf))
PowerSeries.firstUnitCoeff.description: This defines a function that retrieves the non-zero coefficient of a power series with the smallest index, treating it as a unit in the field.

UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizationM.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def normalizationMonoid : NormalizationMonoid α :=   normalizationMonoidOfMonoidHomRightInverse     { toFun := fun a : Associates α =>         if a = 0 then 0         else           ((normalizedFactors a).map               (Classical.choose mk_surjective.hasRightInverse : Associates α → α)).prod       map_one' := by nontriviality α; simp       map_mul' := fun x y => by         by_cases hx : x = 0         · simp [hx]         by_cases hy : y = 0         · simp [hy]         simp [hx, hy] }     (by       intro x       dsimp       by_cases hx : x = 0       · simp [hx]       have h : Associates.mkMonoidHom ∘ Classical.choose mk_surjective.hasRightInverse =           (id : Associates α → Associates α) := by         ext x         rw [Function.comp_apply, mkMonoidHom_apply,           Classical.choose_spec mk_surjective.hasRightInverse x]         rfl       rw [if_neg hx, ← mkMonoidHom_apply, MonoidHom.map_multiset_prod, map_map, h, map_id, ←         associated_iff_eq]       apply normalizedFactors_prod hx)
UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizationM.description: The definition introduces a normalization monoid structure for unique factorization monoids within the context of a commutative monoid with zero.

UniqueFactorizationMonoid.dvd_of_dvd_mul.comment:
Euclid's lemma: if `a ∣ b * c` and `a` and `c` have no common prime factors, `a ∣ b`.
Compare `IsCoprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left`.
UniqueFactorizationMonoid.dvd_of_dvd_mul.description: If an element divides the product of two other elements and shares no common prime factors with one of them, then it must also divide the other element.

is multiplicative on coprime elements, then `f` is multiplicative on all products of primes.

Associates.FactorSet.code: Associates.FactorSet.{u} (α : Type u) [CancelCommMonoidWithZero α] : Type u
Associates.FactorSet.comment:
`FactorSet α` representation elements of unique factorization domain as multisets.
`Multiset α` produced by `normalizedFactors` are only unique up to associated elements, while the
multisets in `FactorSet α` are unique by equality and restricted to irreducible elements. This
gives us a representation of each element as a unique multisets (or the added ⊤ for 0), which has a
complete lattice structure. Infimum is the greatest common divisor and supremum is the least common
multiple.

explanatories.WithTop: This definition creates a new type that extends a given type by adding a greatest element.

Associates.FactorSet.description: This definition describes a type that represents the set of irreducible elements in a unique factorization domain as unique multisets, enabling a complete lattice structure where the greatest common divisor and least common multiple correspond to the infimum and supremum, respectively.

UniqueFactorizationMonoid.fintypeSubtype.fullDefinition: noncomputable def fintypeSubtypeDvd {M : Type*} [CancelCommMonoidWithZero M]     [UniqueFactorizationMonoid M] [Fintype Mˣ] (y : M) (hy : y ≠ 0) : Fintype { x // x ∣ y } := by   haveI : Nontrivial M := ⟨⟨y, 0, hy⟩⟩   haveI : NormalizationMonoid M := UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizationMonoid   haveI := Classical.decEq M   haveI := Classical.decEq (Associates M)   -- We'll show `λ (u : Mˣ) (f ⊆ factors y) → u * Π f` is injective   -- and has image exactly the divisors of `y`.   refine     Fintype.ofFinset       (((normalizedFactors y).powerset.toFinset ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset Mˣ)).image fun s =>         (s.snd : M) * s.fst.prod)       fun x => ?_   simp only [exists_prop, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_univ, and_true_iff,     Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_powerset, exists_eq_right, Multiset.mem_map]   constructor   · rintro ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩     show (s.snd : M) * s.fst.prod ∣ y     rw [(unit_associated_one.mul_right s.fst.prod).dvd_iff_dvd_left, one_mul,       ← (normalizedFactors_prod hy).dvd_iff_dvd_right]     exact Multiset.prod_dvd_prod_of_le hs   · rintro (h : x ∣ y)     have hx : x ≠ 0 := by       refine mt (fun hx => ?_) hy       rwa [hx, zero_dvd_iff] at h     obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := normalizedFactors_prod hx     refine ⟨⟨normalizedFactors x, u⟩, ?_, (mul_comm _ _).trans hu⟩     exact (dvd_iff_normalizedFactors_le_normalizedFactors hx hy).mp h
UniqueFactorizationMonoid.fintypeSubtype.description: If an element in a unique factorization monoid is nonzero and has finitely many units, then it has a finite number of divisors.

PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus.code: PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus.{u} {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (s : Set R) : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)
PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus.comment:
The zero locus of a set `s` of elements of a commutative (semi)ring `R` is the set of all
prime ideals of the ring that contain the set `s`.

An element `f` of `R` can be thought of as a dependent function on the prime spectrum of `R`.
At a point `x` (a prime ideal) the function (i.e., element) `f` takes values in the quotient ring
`R` modulo the prime ideal `x`. In this manner, `zeroLocus s` is exactly the subset of
`PrimeSpectrum R` where all "functions" in `s` vanish simultaneously.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

consisting of all "functions" that vanish on all of `t`.

FractionalIdeal.code:
FractionalIdeal.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R) (P : Type u_2) [CommRing P] [Algebra R P] :
  Type u_2
FractionalIdeal.comment:
The fractional ideals of a domain `R` are ideals of `R` divided by some `a ∈ R`.

More precisely, let `P` be a localization of `R` at some submonoid `S`,
then a fractional ideal `I ⊆ P` is an `R`-submodule of `P`,
such that there is a nonzero `a : R` with `a I ⊆ R`.

explanatories.IsFractional: A submodule is considered a fractional ideal if it can be contained within the ring when multiplied by a non-zero element from the ring's submonoid.

FractionalIdeal.fullDefinition: def FractionalIdeal :=   { I : Submodule R P // IsFractional S I }
FractionalIdeal.description: A fractional ideal of a domain is an ideal in its localization that can be multiplied by a non-zero element from the ring to be contained within the original ring.

FractionalIdeal.equivNum.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equivNum [Nontrivial P] [NoZeroSMulDivisors R P]     {I : FractionalIdeal S P} (h_nz : (I.den : R) ≠ 0) : I ≃ₗ[R] I.num := by   refine LinearEquiv.trans     (LinearEquiv.ofBijective ((DistribMulAction.toLinearMap R P I.den).restrict fun _ hx ↦ ?_)       ⟨fun _ _ hxy ↦ ?_, fun ⟨y, hy⟩ ↦ ?_⟩)     (Submodule.equivMapOfInjective (Algebra.linearMap R P)       (NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective R P) (num I)).symm   · rw [← den_mul_self_eq_num]     exact Submodule.smul_mem_pointwise_smul _ _ _ hx   · simp_rw [LinearMap.restrict_apply, DistribMulAction.toLinearMap_apply, Subtype.mk.injEq] at hxy     rwa [Submonoid.smul_def, Submonoid.smul_def, smul_right_inj h_nz, SetCoe.ext_iff] at hxy   · rw [← den_mul_self_eq_num] at hy     obtain ⟨x, hx, hxy⟩ := hy     exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, by simp_rw [LinearMap.restrict_apply, Subtype.ext_iff, ← hxy]; rfl⟩

`FractionalIdeal.mul` is the product of two fractional ideals,
used to define the `Mul` instance.

This is only an auxiliary definition: the preferred way of writing `I.mul J` is `I * J`.

Elaborated terms involving `FractionalIdeal` tend to grow quite large,
so by making definitions irreducible, we hope to avoid deep unfolds.

explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

explanatories.Submodule.span_induction: If a property holds for zero and all elements of a set, and is preserved under addition and scalar multiplication, then it also holds for all elements in the span of that set.
explanatories.IsLocalization.isInteger_zero: The theorem asserts that zero in a localization of a commutative semiring is considered an integer from the original ring.
explanatories.IsLocalization.isInteger_add: The theorem states that the sum of two elements in a localization of a commutative semiring, both of which are considered integers from the original ring, is also regarded as an integer in that ring.
explanatories.SMulCommClass.smul_comm: This theorem states that in the presence of a commutative scalar multiplication structure, the order of multiplying two elements with a third remains unchanged when using scalar multiplication.
explanatories.IsLocalization.isInteger_smul: The theorem demonstrates that the product of an integer from the original ring with an element of a localization of that ring is also regarded as an integer in the original ring.
explanatories.IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples: The theorem asserts that for a finite set of fractions indexed by a finite set, there exists a common multiple in the original ring such that all fractions can be expressed as integers when multiplied by this common multiple.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

EuclideanDomain.to_principal_ideal_domai.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) EuclideanDomain.to_principal_ideal_domain : IsPrincipalIdealRing R where   principal S := by classical exact     ⟨if h : { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 }.Nonempty then         have wf : WellFounded (EuclideanDomain.r : R → R → Prop) := EuclideanDomain.r_wellFounded         have hmin : WellFounded.min wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h ∈ S ∧             WellFounded.min wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h ≠ 0 :=           WellFounded.min_mem wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h         ⟨WellFounded.min wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h,           Submodule.ext fun x => ⟨fun hx =>             div_add_mod x (WellFounded.min wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h) ▸               (Ideal.mem_span_singleton.2 <| dvd_add (dvd_mul_right _ _) <| by                 have : x % WellFounded.min wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h ∉                     { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } :=                   fun h₁ => WellFounded.not_lt_min wf _ h h₁ (mod_lt x hmin.2)                 have : x % WellFounded.min wf { x : R | x ∈ S ∧ x ≠ 0 } h = 0 := by                   simp only [not_and_or, Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_ne_iff] at this                   exact this.neg_resolve_left <| (mod_mem_iff hmin.1).2 hx                 simp [*]),               fun hx =>                 let ⟨y, hy⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton.1 hx                 hy.symm ▸ S.mul_mem_right _ hmin.1⟩⟩       else ⟨0, Submodule.ext fun a => by             rw [← @Submodule.bot_coe R R _ _ _, span_eq, Submodule.mem_bot]             exact ⟨fun haS => by_contra fun ha0 => h ⟨a, ⟨haS, ha0⟩⟩,               fun h₁ => h₁.symm ▸ S.zero_mem⟩⟩⟩

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def liftToMultiset : (α → R) ≃ (Multiplicative (Multiset α) →* R) where   toFun f :=     { toFun := fun s => (s.toAdd.map f).prod       map_mul' := fun x y =>         calc           _ = Multiset.prod (Multiset.map f x + Multiset.map f y) := by             rw [← Multiset.map_add]             rfl           _ = _ := Multiset.prod_add _ _       map_one' := rfl }   invFun F x := F (Multiplicative.ofAdd ({x} : Multiset α))   left_inv f := funext fun x => show (Multiset.map f {x}).prod = _ by simp   right_inv F := MonoidHom.ext fun x =>     let F' := MonoidHom.toAdditive'' F     let x' := Multiplicative.toAdd x     show (Multiset.map (fun a => F' {a}) x').sum = F' x' by       erw [← Multiset.map_map (fun x => F' x) (fun x => {x}), ← AddMonoidHom.map_multiset_sum]       exact DFunLike.congr_arg F (Multiset.sum_map_singleton x')

wittPolynomial.code: wittPolynomial.{u_1} (p : ℕ) (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial ℕ R
wittPolynomial.comment:
`wittPolynomial p R n` is the `n`-th Witt polynomial
with respect to a prime `p` with coefficients in a commutative ring `R`.
It is defined as:

`∑_{i ≤ n} p^i X_i^{p^{n-i}} ∈ R[X_0, X_1, X_2, …]`.

explanatories.MvPolynomial: This definition introduces a type representing multivariate polynomials characterized by an index set for the variables and a commutative semiring for the coefficients.
explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.monomial: This definition describes a function that generates a monomial in a multivariate polynomial, characterized by a coefficient and a specified set of exponent values.

wittPolynomial.fullDefinition: noncomputable def wittPolynomial (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial ℕ R :=   ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), monomial (single i (p ^ (n - i))) ((p : R) ^ i)
wittPolynomial.description: The Witt polynomial for a prime number with coefficients in a commutative ring is defined as a specific polynomial that involves a summation of terms including powers of the prime and indeterminate variables.

wittStructureRat.code:
wittStructureRat.{u_2} (p : ℕ) {idx : Type u_2} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (Φ : MvPolynomial idx ℚ) (n : ℕ) :
  MvPolynomial (idx × ℕ) ℚ
wittStructureRat.comment:
`wittStructureRat Φ` is a family of polynomials `ℕ → MvPolynomial (idx × ℕ) ℚ`
that are uniquely characterised by the property that
```
bind₁ (wittStructureRat p Φ) (wittPolynomial p ℚ n) =
bind₁ (fun i ↦ (rename (prod.mk i) (wittPolynomial p ℚ n))) Φ
```
In other words: evaluating the `n`-th Witt polynomial on the family `wittStructureRat Φ`
is the same as evaluating `Φ` on the (appropriately renamed) `n`-th Witt polynomials.

See `wittStructureRat_prop` for this property,
and `wittStructureRat_existsUnique` for the fact that `wittStructureRat`
gives the unique family of polynomials with this property.

These polynomials turn out to have integral coefficients,
but it requires some effort to show this.
See `wittStructureInt` for the version with integral coefficients,
and `map_wittStructureInt` for the fact that it is equal to `wittStructureRat`
when mapped to polynomials over the rationals.

  MvPolynomial (idx × ℕ) ℤ
wittStructureInt.comment:
`wittStructureInt Φ` is a family of polynomials `ℕ → MvPolynomial (idx × ℕ) ℤ`
that are uniquely characterised by the property that
```
bind₁ (wittStructureInt p Φ) (wittPolynomial p ℤ n) =
bind₁ (fun i ↦ (rename (prod.mk i) (wittPolynomial p ℤ n))) Φ
```
In other words: evaluating the `n`-th Witt polynomial on the family `wittStructureInt Φ`
is the same as evaluating `Φ` on the (appropriately renamed) `n`-th Witt polynomials.

See `wittStructureInt_prop` for this property,
and `wittStructureInt_existsUnique` for the fact that `wittStructureInt`
gives the unique family of polynomials with this property.

WittVector.eval.code:
WittVector.eval.{u_1} {p : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {k : ℕ} (φ : ℕ → MvPolynomial (Fin k × ℕ) ℤ)
  (x : Fin k → 𝕎 R) : 𝕎 R
WittVector.eval.comment:
Let `φ` be a family of polynomials, indexed by natural numbers, whose variables come from the
disjoint union of `k` copies of `ℕ`, and let `xᵢ` be a Witt vector for `0 ≤ i < k`.

`eval φ x` evaluates `φ` mapping the variable `X_(i, n)` to the `n`th coefficient of `xᵢ`.

Instantiating `φ` with certain polynomials defined in
`Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/StructurePolynomial.lean` establishes the
ring operations on `𝕎 R`. For example, `WittVector.wittAdd` is such a `φ` with `k = 2`;
evaluating this at `(x₀, x₁)` gives us the sum of two Witt vectors `x₀ + x₁`.

explanatories.WittVector.zero_coeff: The theorem asserts that the coefficient of the constant term in a polynomial corresponding to a prime number and a ring is equal to zero for any given natural number.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.WittVector.add_coeff: This theorem states that the coefficient of the sum of two Witt vectors is equal to the evaluation of a particular polynomial at the coefficients of the individual vectors, given that the prime number and ring conditions are satisfied.
explanatories.WittVector.sub_coeff: This theorem states that the coefficient of the difference of two Witt vectors is equal to the evaluation of a specific polynomial at the coefficients of the individual vectors, assuming the conditions for the prime number and commutative ring are satisfied.
explanatories.WittVector.mul_coeff: This theorem asserts that the coefficient of the product of two Witt vectors at a given index is equal to the evaluation of a polynomial constructed from their coefficients using a specified multiplication rule.
explanatories.WittVector.neg_coeff: This theorem establishes that the coefficient of the negation of a Witt vector at any index is equal to the evaluation of a specific polynomial associated with the Witt negation at the coefficients of the original Witt vector.
explanatories.WittVector.nsmul_coeff: This theorem establishes a relationship between the coefficient of a scaled Witt vector and the evaluation of a specific polynomial defined for that scaling.
explanatories.WittVector.zsmul_coeff: This theorem establishes a relationship between the coefficient of a Witt vector multiplied by an integer and a polynomial evaluation involving the Witt scalar multiplication with a specified prime number.
explanatories.WittVector.pow_coeff: This theorem asserts that the coefficient of the m-th power of a Witt vector at a given index is equal to the evaluation of a polynomial derived from its coefficients using a specific power rule.
explanatories.WittVector.peval: This definition provides a method to evaluate a multivariate polynomial with variables sourced from multiple copies of natural numbers, using a specific evaluation function.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.map_aeval: This theorem shows that the application of a polynomial to an evaluation map can be expressed equivalently in terms of a composition of ring homomorphisms and the evaluation of the polynomial at substituted values.
explanatories.algebraMap_int_eq: This theorem states that the algebra map from the integers to any ring is equal to the canonical ring homomorphism that embeds the integers into that ring.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.coe_eval₂Hom: This theorem establishes that the evaluation homomorphism applied to a multivariate polynomial is equivalent to the direct evaluation of the polynomial using the specified algebra homomorphism and function.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_congr: This theorem asserts that when two homomorphisms and two polynomials are equal, the evaluation of those polynomials under their respective homomorphisms will also be equal.
explanatories.RingHom.ext_int: This theorem states that two ring homomorphisms from integers to a non-associative semiring are equal if they define the same mappings.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

WittVector.«tacticGhost_fun_tac_,_».fullDefinition: elab "ghost_fun_tac" φ:term "," fn:term : tactic => do   evalTactic (← `(tactic| (   ext n   have := congr_fun (congr_arg (@peval R _ _) (wittStructureInt_prop p $φ n)) $fn   simp only [wittZero, OfNat.ofNat, Zero.zero, wittOne, One.one,     HAdd.hAdd, Add.add, HSub.hSub, Sub.sub, Neg.neg, HMul.hMul, Mul.mul,HPow.hPow, Pow.pow,     wittNSMul, wittZSMul, HSMul.hSMul, SMul.smul]   simpa (config := { unfoldPartialApp := true }) [WittVector.ghostFun, aeval_rename, aeval_bind₁,     comp, uncurry, peval, eval] using this   )))

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code: WittVector.ghostFun.{u_1} {p : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] : 𝕎 R → ℕ → R
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.comment:
Evaluates the `n`th Witt polynomial on the first `n` coefficients of `x`,
producing a value in `R`.
This function will be bundled as the ring homomorphism `WittVector.ghostMap`
once the ring structure is available,
but we rely on it to set up the ring structure in the first place.

WittVector.IsPoly.comp.comment: The composition of polynomial functions is polynomial.

explanatories.MvPolynomial.bind₁: This definition describes an operation that transforms a multivariate polynomial in one variable type into another polynomial by replacing each variable with a corresponding polynomial defined by a mapping, while preserving the original coefficient type.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.aeval_bind₁: The theorem states that evaluating a multivariate polynomial formed by binding a mapping to another polynomial is equivalent to evaluating the original polynomial with the applied mapping for each variable.

WittVector.IsPoly.comp.fullDefinition: instance comp {g f} [hg : IsPoly p g] [hf : IsPoly p f] :     IsPoly p fun R _Rcr => @g R _Rcr ∘ @f R _Rcr := by   obtain ⟨φ, hf⟩ := hf   obtain ⟨ψ, hg⟩ := hg   use fun n => bind₁ φ (ψ n)   intros   simp only [aeval_bind₁, Function.comp, hg, hf]
WittVector.IsPoly.comp.description: The composition of two polynomial functions is also classified as a polynomial function of the same degree.

WittVector.IsPoly₂.mk'.code:

WittVector.IsPoly₂.comp.fullDefinition: instance IsPoly₂.comp {h f g} [hh : IsPoly₂ p h] [hf : IsPoly p f] [hg : IsPoly p g] :     IsPoly₂ p fun R _Rcr x y => h (f x) (g y) := by   obtain ⟨φ, hf⟩ := hf   obtain ⟨ψ, hg⟩ := hg   obtain ⟨χ, hh⟩ := hh   refine ⟨⟨fun n ↦ bind₁ (uncurry <|     ![fun k ↦ rename (Prod.mk (0 : Fin 2)) (φ k),       fun k ↦ rename (Prod.mk (1 : Fin 2)) (ψ k)]) (χ n), ?_⟩⟩   intros   funext n   simp (config := { unfoldPartialApp := true }) only [peval, aeval_bind₁, Function.comp, hh, hf, hg,     uncurry]   apply eval₂Hom_congr rfl _ rfl   ext ⟨i, n⟩   fin_cases i <;> simp [aeval_eq_eval₂Hom, eval₂Hom_rename, Function.comp]

WittVector.Tactic.ghostCalc.comment:
`ghost_calc` is a tactic for proving identities between polynomial functions.
Typically, when faced with a goal like
```lean
∀ (x y : 𝕎 R), verschiebung (x * frobenius y) = verschiebung x * y
```
you can
1. call `ghost_calc`
2. do a small amount of manual work -- maybe nothing, maybe `rintro`, etc
3. call `ghost_simp`

and this will close the goal.

`ghost_calc` cannot detect whether you are dealing with unary or binary polynomial functions.
You must give it arguments to determine this.
If you are proving a universally quantified goal like the above,
call `ghost_calc _ _`.
If the variables are introduced already, call `ghost_calc x y`.
In the unary case, use `ghost_calc _` or `ghost_calc x`.

`ghost_calc` is a light wrapper around type class inference.
All it does is apply the appropriate extensionality lemma and try to infer the resulting goals.
This is subtle and Lean's elaborator doesn't like it because of the HO unification involved,
so it is easier (and prettier) to put it in a tactic script.

WittVector.wittMulN.code: WittVector.wittMulN (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] : ℕ → ℕ → MvPolynomial ℕ ℤ
WittVector.wittMulN.comment:
`wittMulN p n` is the family of polynomials that computes
the coefficients of `x * n` in terms of the coefficients of the Witt vector `x`.

explanatories.MvPolynomial: This definition introduces a type representing multivariate polynomials characterized by an index set for the variables and a commutative semiring for the coefficients.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.bind₁: This definition describes an operation that transforms a multivariate polynomial in one variable type into another polynomial by replacing each variable with a corresponding polynomial defined by a mapping, while preserving the original coefficient type.
explanatories.Function.uncurry: This definition describes a way to transform a function that takes two arguments into a single function that takes a pair of values instead.
explanatories.MvPolynomial.X: This definition introduces a function that constructs a degree one monomial corresponding to a specific variable in the multivariate polynomial context.

WittVector.wittMulN.fullDefinition: noncomputable def wittMulN : ℕ → ℕ → MvPolynomial ℕ ℤ   | 0 => 0   | n + 1 => fun k => bind₁ (Function.uncurry <| ![wittMulN n, X]) (wittAdd p k)
WittVector.wittMulN.description: This defines a family of polynomials that computes the coefficients of the product of a given natural number and a Witt vector based on a specified prime number.

WittVector.verschiebungFun.code: WittVector.verschiebungFun.{u_1} {p : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (x : 𝕎 R) : 𝕎 R
WittVector.verschiebungFun.comment:
`verschiebungFun x` shifts the coefficients of `x` up by one,
by inserting 0 as the 0th coefficient.
`x.coeff i` then becomes `(verchiebungFun x).coeff (i + 1)`.

`verschiebungFun` is the underlying function of the additive monoid hom `WittVector.verschiebung`.

explanatories.WittVector.mk': This theorem defines a method to construct a Witt vector over a specified prime number and a given type of coefficients.
explanatories.WittVector.coeff: This definition specifies a function that retrieves the nth coefficient from a given Witt vector.

WittVector.verschiebungFun.description: The definition describes a function that shifts the coefficients of a Witt vector up by one position, inserting a zero as the new leading coefficient.

WittVector.verschiebung.comment:
`verschiebung x` shifts the coefficients of `x` up by one, by inserting 0 as the 0th coefficient.
`x.coeff i` then becomes `(verchiebung x).coeff (i + 1)`.

This is an additive monoid hom with underlying function `verschiebung_fun`.

explanatories.WittVector.verschiebungFun: The definition describes a function that shifts the coefficients of a Witt vector up by one position, inserting a zero as the new leading coefficient.
explanatories.WittVector.verschiebungFun_coeff: The theorem establishes that the nth coefficient of a shifted Witt vector is zero if n is zero, and corresponds to the (n-1)th coefficient of the original Witt vector otherwise.
explanatories.Nat.zero_eq: Zero is equal to the natural number zero.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.
explanatories.if_true: This theorem asserts that when the condition is always true, the result of a conditional expression will equal the first option unconditionally.
explanatories.WittVector.zero_coeff: The theorem asserts that the coefficient of the constant term in a polynomial corresponding to a prime number and a ring is equal to zero for any given natural number.
explanatories.ite_self: The theorem states that if a proposition is true or false, then choosing the same value in both branches of a conditional yields that value.
explanatories.WittVector.IsPoly₂.ext: If two polynomial functions yield the same values at all ghost components across Witt vectors, then they are equal.

An auxiliary polynomial over the integers, that satisfies
`p * (frobeniusPolyAux p n) + X n ^ p = frobeniusPoly p n`.

modulo `p`.

WittVector.frobeniusPolyAux.eq_1 (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] :
  ∀ (x : ℕ),
    frobeniusPolyAux p x =
      X (x + 1) -
        ∑ i : Fin x,
          let_fun x_1 := ⋯;
          ∑ j ∈ range (p ^ (x - ↑i)),
            (X ↑i ^ p) ^ (p ^ (x - ↑i) - (j + 1)) * frobeniusPolyAux p ↑i ^ (j + 1) *
              C ↑((p ^ (x - ↑i)).choose (j + 1) / p ^ (x - ↑i - v p ⟨j + 1, ⋯⟩) * p ^ (j - v p ⟨j + 1, ⋯⟩))

WittVector.frobenius.code: WittVector.frobenius.{u_1} {p : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CommRing R] : 𝕎 R →+* 𝕎 R
WittVector.frobenius.comment:
If `R` has characteristic `p`, then there is a ring endomorphism
that raises `r : R` to the power `p`.
By applying `WittVector.map` to this endomorphism,
we obtain a ring endomorphism `frobenius R p : 𝕎 R →+* 𝕎 R`.

The underlying function of this morphism is `WittVector.frobeniusFun`.

witt_vector.frobenius_equiv.fullDefinition: def frobeniusEquiv [PerfectRing R p] : WittVector p R ≃+* WittVector p R :=   { (WittVector.frobenius : WittVector p R →+* WittVector p R) with     toFun := WittVector.frobenius     invFun := map (_root_.frobeniusEquiv R p).symm     left_inv := fun f => ext fun n => by       rw [frobenius_eq_map_frobenius]       exact frobeniusEquiv_symm_apply_frobenius R p _     right_inv := fun f => ext fun n => by       rw [frobenius_eq_map_frobenius]       exact frobenius_apply_frobeniusEquiv_symm R p _ }

TruncatedWittVector.code: TruncatedWittVector.{u_2} : ℕ → ℕ → Type u_2 → Type u_2
TruncatedWittVector.comment:
A truncated Witt vector over `R` is a vector of elements of `R`,
i.e., the first `n` coefficients of a Witt vector.
We will define operations on this type that are compatible with the (untruncated) Witt
vector operations.

`TruncatedWittVector p n R` takes a parameter `p : ℕ` that is not used in the definition.
In practice, this number `p` is assumed to be a prime number,
and under this assumption we construct a ring structure on `TruncatedWittVector p n R`.
(`TruncatedWittVector p₁ n R` and `TruncatedWittVector p₂ n R` are definitionally
equal as types but will have different ring operations.)
TruncatedWittVector.fullDefinition: def TruncatedWittVector (_ : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) :=   Fin n → R
TruncatedWittVector.description: This definition establishes a type representing truncated Witt vectors, which consist of the first `n` coefficients from a Witt vector over a ring, allowing for operations that align with the structure of full Witt vectors.

explanatories.TruncatedWittVector.out_injective: This theorem establishes that the function mapping truncated Witt vectors to their outputs is injective, meaning distinct truncated Witt vectors correspond to distinct outputs.

explanatories.Lean.Parser.Category.tactic: The tactic category in Lean represents the syntax for proof tactics that operate on the context of hypotheses to construct terms of the expected type following the `by` keyword in proofs.
explanatories.WittVector.init_add: The theorem asserts that initializing the sum of two Witt vectors with a given number of coefficients is equivalent to independently initializing each vector with the same number of coefficients and then summing the results.
explanatories.WittVector.init_mul: The theorem establishes that initializing the product of two Witt vectors with a given number of coefficients is equivalent to independently initializing each vector with the same number of coefficients and then multiplying the results.
explanatories.WittVector.init_neg: The theorem states that initializing the negation of a Witt vector with a given number of coefficients is equivalent to negating the initialized vector, where the initialization applies to the same number of coefficients.
explanatories.WittVector.init_sub: The theorem establishes that initializing the difference of two Witt vectors with a specified number of coefficients is the same as independently initializing each vector and then taking the difference of the results.
explanatories.WittVector.init_nsmul: The theorem states that initializing a scalar multiplication of a Witt vector with a given number of coefficients is equivalent to performing the scalar multiplication after independently initializing the vector with the same number of coefficients.
explanatories.WittVector.init_zsmul: The theorem states that initializing a scaled Witt vector results in the same vector as scaling the initialized Witt vector by the same factor.
explanatories.WittVector.init_pow: The theorem shows that initializing a power of a Witt vector with a specified number of coefficients is the same as independently initializing the vector and then raising the result to that power.

explanatories.TruncatedWittVector.truncate_comp_wittVe: This theorem asserts that the composition of truncation functions for Witt vectors is associative, showing that truncating a vector first and then applying another truncation results in the same final truncation as performing a single truncation directly.

explanatories.RingHom.comp_assoc: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of semiring homomorphisms is associative, allowing for rearrangement of the composition order without affecting the outcome.

WittVector.liftEquiv.fullDefinition: def liftEquiv : { f : ∀ k, S →+* TruncatedWittVector p k R // ∀ (k₁ k₂) (hk : k₁ ≤ k₂),     (TruncatedWittVector.truncate hk).comp (f k₂) = f k₁ } ≃ (S →+* 𝕎 R) where   toFun f := lift f.1 f.2   invFun g :=     ⟨fun k => (truncate k).comp g, by       intro _ _ h       simp only [← RingHom.comp_assoc, truncate_comp_wittVector_truncate]⟩   left_inv := by rintro ⟨f, hf⟩; simp only [truncate_comp_lift]   right_inv g := lift_unique _ _ fun _ => rfl

Here the vertical arrows are `TruncatedWittVector.zmodEquivTrunc`,
the horizontal arrow at the top is `ZMod.castHom`,
and the horizontal arrow at the bottom is `TruncatedWittVector.truncate`.

WittVector.equiv.comment:
The ring of Witt vectors over `ZMod p` is isomorphic to the ring of `p`-adic integers. This
equivalence is witnessed by `WittVector.toPadicInt` with inverse `WittVector.fromPadicInt`.

explanatories.WittVector.toPadicInt_comp_fromPadicInt_: The composition of the mappings from p-adic integers to themselves via two specific homomorphisms yields the identity mapping, ensuring that the operations are consistent and reversible in this context.

explanatories.RingHom.map_add: This theorem indicates that a ring homomorphism maintains the property of addition by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.

WittVector.mkUnit.fullDefinition: def mkUnit {a : Units k} {A : 𝕎 k} (hA : A.coeff 0 = a) : Units (𝕎 k) :=   Units.mkOfMulEqOne A (@WittVector.mk' p _ (inverseCoeff a A)) (by     ext n     induction' n with n _     · simp [WittVector.mul_coeff_zero, inverseCoeff, hA]     let H_coeff := A.coeff (n + 1) * ↑(a⁻¹ ^ p ^ (n + 1)) +       nthRemainder p n (truncateFun (n + 1) A) fun i : Fin (n + 1) => inverseCoeff a A i     have H := Units.mul_inv (a ^ p ^ (n + 1))     linear_combination (norm := skip) -H_coeff * H     have ha : (a : k) ^ p ^ (n + 1) = ↑(a ^ p ^ (n + 1)) := by norm_cast     have ha_inv : (↑a⁻¹ : k) ^ p ^ (n + 1) = ↑(a ^ p ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ := by norm_cast     simp only [nthRemainder_spec, inverseCoeff, succNthValUnits, hA,       one_coeff_eq_of_pos, Nat.succ_pos', ha_inv, ha, inv_pow]     ring!)

WittVector.RecursionMain.succNthDefining.fullDefinition: def succNthDefiningPoly (n : ℕ) (a₁ a₂ : 𝕎 k) (bs : Fin (n + 1) → k) : Polynomial k :=   X ^ p * C (a₁.coeff 0 ^ p ^ (n + 1)) - X * C (a₂.coeff 0 ^ p ^ (n + 1)) +     C       (a₁.coeff (n + 1) * (bs 0 ^ p) ^ p ^ (n + 1) +             nthRemainder p n (fun v => bs v ^ p) (truncateFun (n + 1) a₁) -           a₂.coeff (n + 1) * bs 0 ^ p ^ (n + 1) -         nthRemainder p n bs (truncateFun (n + 1) a₂))

  [CharP k p] (n : ℕ) (a₁ a₂ : 𝕎 k) (bs : Fin (n + 1) → k) :
  succNthDefiningPoly p n a₁ a₂ bs =
    X ^ p * C (a₁.coeff 0 ^ p ^ (n + 1)) - X * C (a₂.coeff 0 ^ p ^ (n + 1)) +
      C
        (a₁.coeff (n + 1) * (bs 0 ^ p) ^ p ^ (n + 1) + nthRemainder p n (fun v => bs v ^ p) (truncateFun (n + 1) a₁) -
            a₂.coeff (n + 1) * bs 0 ^ p ^ (n + 1) -
          nthRemainder p n bs (truncateFun (n + 1) a₂))

WittVector.exists_frobenius_solution_fractionRing_aux.{u_1} (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {k : Type u_1} [Field k]
  [CharP k p] [IsAlgClosed k] (m n : ℕ) (r' q' : 𝕎 k) (hr' : r'.coeff 0 ≠ 0) (hq' : q'.coeff 0 ≠ 0)
  (hq : ↑p ^ n * q' ∈ nonZeroDivisors (𝕎 k)) :
  let b := frobeniusRotation p hr' hq';
  φ ((algebraMap (𝕎 k) (FractionRing (𝕎 k))) b) * Localization.mk (↑p ^ m * r') ⟨↑p ^ n * q', hq⟩ =
    ↑p ^ (↑m - ↑n) * (algebraMap (𝕎 k) (FractionRing (𝕎 k))) b

Int.multichoose.eq_1.code:

    | -[n+1] => (-1) ^ k * ↑((n + 1).choose k)

Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_cri.comment:
If `f` is a non constant polynomial with coefficients in `R`, and `P` is a prime ideal in `R`,
then if every coefficient in `R` except the leading coefficient is in `P`, and
the trailing coefficient is not in `P^2` and no non units in `R` divide `f`, then `f` is
irreducible.

explanatories.Subalgebra.FG: A subalgebra is considered finitely generated if there exists a finite set of elements such that the subalgebra can be obtained by adjoining those elements.
explanatories.Module.Finite.out: A module over a semiring is finitely generated if and only if the entire module can be generated by a finite set of elements.
explanatories.Algebra.FiniteType.out: A finite type algebra over a commutative semiring can be generated by a finite set of elements.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Algebra.FiniteType.of_surjective: A finite type algebra is established over a commutative semiring when there exists a surjective algebra homomorphism from a finitely generated algebra to it.
explanatories.FreeAlgebra.lift: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the space of functions from a set to an algebra and the space of algebra homomorphisms from the free algebra generated by that set to the algebra, allowing for unique lifting of functions to morphisms.
explanatories.Algebra.FiniteType.freeAlgebra: The free algebra over a finite indexing type is finitely generated over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.RingHom.FiniteType: A ring homomorphism is considered to be of finite type if the codomain is finitely generated as an algebra over the domain.
explanatories.RingHom.FiniteType.of_surjective: A surjective ring homomorphism is of finite type if the codomain is finitely generated as an algebra over the domain.
explanatories.AlgHom.FiniteType: An algebra morphism is classified as being of finite type if the codomain is finitely generated as an algebra over the domain.
explanatories.AlgHom.FiniteType.of_surjective: A surjective algebra homomorphism from one algebra to another over a commutative ring ensures that the target algebra is finitely generated.
explanatories.AddMonoidAlgebra.of': This definition describes a function that embeds elements of a magma, including a zero element, into its corresponding additive monoid algebra representation.
explanatories.AddMonoid.FG.out: Any additive monoid that is finitely generated is trivially considered as finitely generated for the top element.
explanatories.AddMonoidAlgebra.freeAlgebra_lift_of_sur: If a set generates an additive monoid, then the corresponding lift to the free algebra is surjective, meaning it maps onto the entire algebra generated by that monoid.

Module.Finite.injective_of_surjective_en.code:
Module.Finite.injective_of_surjective_endomorphism.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {M : Type u_2}
  [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (f_surj : Surjective ⇑f) : Function.Injective ⇑f
Module.Finite.injective_of_surjective_en.comment:
A theorem by Vasconcelos, given a finite module `M` over a commutative ring, any
surjective endomorphism of `M` is also injective.
It is a consequence of the fact `CommRing.orzechProperty`
that any commutative ring `R` satisfies the `OrzechProperty`;
please use `OrzechProperty.injective_of_surjective_endomorphism` instead.
This is similar to `IsNoetherian.injective_of_surjective_endomorphism` but only applies in the
commutative case, but does not use a Noetherian hypothesis.

explanatories.RingHom.Finite: A ring homomorphism is finite if the target ring is finitely generated as a module over the source ring.
explanatories.AlgHom.Finite: An algebra morphism is finite if the target algebra is finitely generated as a module over the source algebra.
explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.OrzechProperty.injective_of_surjective_e: This theorem establishes that a surjective linear map from a module to itself is also injective.

Module.Finite.injective_of_surjective_en.description: In a finite module over a commutative ring, any surjective endomorphism must also be injective.

explanatories.Submodule.liftQ: This definition describes a linear map from the quotient of a module by a submodule to another module, induced by a linear transformation that vanishes on the submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.ker_mkQ: This theorem states that the kernel of the quotient map associated with a submodule is exactly the submodule itself.
explanatories.Submodule.smul_mono: The image of a submodule under the scalar multiplication of ideals is contained within the image of another submodule if the first ideal is contained in the second and similarly for the submodules.
explanatories.Ideal.pow_le_pow_right: If one ideal raised to a power is contained within another ideal raised to a higher power, then the lower exponent ideal must also be contained within the higher exponent ideal.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.SModEq.def: This theorem establishes an equivalence between two elements of a module being equivalent modulo a submodule and their images being equal in the corresponding quotient module.

AdicCompletion.transitionMap.description: This definition describes a canonical linear map that relates two quotient modules by an ideal for two indices where one is less than or equal to the other, facilitating the process of adic completion.

explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.IsHausdorff.iInf_pow_smul: In a Hausdorff module over a commutative ring, the intersection of all ideals generated by increasingly higher powers of a given ideal is trivial.
explanatories.iInf_le: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a function over an index set is always less than or equal to the function's value at any specific index from that set.
explanatories.Submodule.map_smul'': Mapping a linear function over the product of an ideal and a submodule is equivalent to taking the product of the ideal with the image of the submodule under that linear function.
explanatories.Submodule.map_le_iff_le_comap: The theorem establishes a condition under which the image of a submodule under a semilinear map is contained in another submodule if and only if the original submodule is contained in the preimage of that other submodule.
explanatories.le_iInf: This theorem demonstrates that if an element is less than or equal to all elements produced by a function mapping from an index set, then it is also less than or equal to the infimum of those function values in a complete lattice.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Submodule.map_mono: This theorem establishes that if one submodule is contained within another, then the image of the first under a semilinear map is also contained within the image of the second.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.SModEq.def: This theorem establishes an equivalence between two elements of a module being equivalent modulo a submodule and their images being equal in the corresponding quotient module.

Hausdorffification.lift.fullDefinition: def lift (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : Hausdorffification I M →ₗ[R] N :=   liftQ _ f <| map_le_iff_le_comap.1 <| h.iInf_pow_smul ▸ le_iInf fun n =>     le_trans (map_mono <| iInf_le _ n) <| by       rw [map_smul'']       exact smul_mono le_rfl le_top
Hausdorffification.lift.description: Every linear map to a Hausdorff module can be uniquely extended from the Hausdorffification of another module with respect to an ideal.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private noncomputable def mapPreimage (x : AdicCauchySequence I N) :     (n : ℕ) → f ⁻¹' {x n}   | .zero => ⟨(hf (x 0)).choose, (hf (x 0)).choose_spec⟩   | .succ n =>       let y := (hf (x (n + 1))).choose       have hy := (hf (x (n + 1))).choose_spec       let ⟨yₙ, (hyₙ : f yₙ = x n)⟩ := mapPreimage x n       let ⟨⟨d, _⟩, (p : f d = f (yₙ - y))⟩ := mapPreimageDelta hf x hy hyₙ       ⟨yₙ - d, by simpa [p]⟩

IsPrimitiveRoot.zmodEquivZPowers.fullDefinition: def zmodEquivZPowers (h : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ k) : ZMod k ≃+ Additive (Subgroup.zpowers ζ) :=   AddEquiv.ofBijective     (AddMonoidHom.liftOfRightInverse (Int.castAddHom <| ZMod k) _ ZMod.intCast_rightInverse       ⟨{  toFun := fun i => Additive.ofMul (⟨_, i, rfl⟩ : Subgroup.zpowers ζ)           map_zero' := by simp only [zpow_zero]; rfl           map_add' := by intro i j; simp only [zpow_add]; rfl }, fun i hi => by         simp only [AddMonoidHom.mem_ker, CharP.intCast_eq_zero_iff (ZMod k) k, AddMonoidHom.coe_mk,           Int.coe_castAddHom] at hi ⊢         obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hi         simp [zpow_mul, h.pow_eq_one, one_zpow, zpow_natCast]⟩)     (by       constructor       · rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]         intro i hi         rw [Subtype.ext_iff] at hi         have := (h.zpow_eq_one_iff_dvd _).mp hi         rw [← (CharP.intCast_eq_zero_iff (ZMod k) k _).mpr this, eq_comm]         exact ZMod.intCast_rightInverse i       · rintro ⟨ξ, i, rfl⟩         refine ⟨Int.castAddHom (ZMod k) i, ?_⟩         rw [AddMonoidHom.liftOfRightInverse_comp_apply]         rfl)
IsPrimitiveRoot.zmodEquivZPowers.description: This establishes an additive monoid isomorphism between integers modulo a given positive integer and the subgroup generated by the powers of a primitive root of unity.

IsPrimitiveRoot.zmodEquivZPowers.eq_1.{u_4} {R : Type u_4} {k : ℕ} [CommRing R] {ζ : Rˣ} (h : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ k) :
  h.zmodEquivZPowers =
    AddEquiv.ofBijective
      (((Int.castAddHom (ZMod k)).liftOfRightInverse ZMod.cast ⋯)

rootsOfUnityEquivOfPrimitiveRoots.fullDefinition: def _root_.rootsOfUnityEquivOfPrimitiveRoots {S F} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]     [FunLike F R S] [MonoidHomClass F R S]     {n : ℕ+} {f : F} (hf : Function.Injective f) (hζ : (primitiveRoots n R).Nonempty) :     (rootsOfUnity n R) ≃* rootsOfUnity n S :=   (Subgroup.equivMapOfInjective _ _ (Units.map_injective hf)).trans (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr     (((mem_primitiveRoots (k := n) n.2).mp hζ.choose_spec).map_rootsOfUnity hf))
rootsOfUnityEquivOfPrimitiveRoots.description: If a ring contains at least one primitive n-th root of unity and is extended to another ring, then the n-th roots of unity in both rings are isomorphic as groups.

IsPrimitiveRoot.nthRoots_one_eq_biUnion_.comment:
`nthRoots n` as a `Finset` is equal to the union of `primitiveRoots i R` for `i ∣ n`

explanatories.rootsOfUnity.coe_pow: The power of an element in a subgroup of a commutative monoid can be expressed as the same power applied to the corresponding element of the original set.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.

explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.IsPrimitiveRoot.val_toRootsOfUnity_coe: This converts a primitive root into an element of the subgroup of roots of unity in a commutative monoid.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.pow_one: This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one yields the element itself.
explanatories.IsPrimitiveRoot.orderOf: An element in a commutative monoid is a primitive root if its order equals the value of its order function.
explanatories.IsPrimitiveRoot.eq_orderOf: If an element is a primitive root of unity for a given positive integer, then its order is equal to that integer.
explanatories.SetLike.coe_injective: This theorem demonstrates that the mapping from elements of a structure defined as `SetLike` to their corresponding set representation is a one-to-one function, ensuring that distinct elements produce distinct outputs.
explanatories.Exists.choose_spec: An element chosen from an existence assertion satisfies the property asserted by that existence statement.
explanatories.IsPrimitiveRoot.toRootsOfUnity: This converts a primitive root into an element of the subgroup of roots of unity in a commutative monoid.
explanatories.orderOf_units: This theorem states that the order of a unit in a monoid is equal to the order of the element itself when considered as a group element.
explanatories.Subgroup.orderOf_coe: This theorem states that the order of an element in a subgroup is equal to the order of the same element in the larger group.
explanatories.MonoidHom.toHomUnits: A homomorphism from a group to a monoid can be transformed into a homomorphism from the group to the units of the monoid.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.toAlgHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebraic equivalence between two algebras over a commutative semiring as an algebra homomorphism between them.
explanatories.Exists.choose: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.one_apply: This theorem states that when applying the identity element of an algebra to any element, the output remains unchanged.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.toRingEquiv_eq_coe: This theorem demonstrates that an algebra equivalence can be expressed as a ring equivalence by identifying its underlying structure in a specific manner.
explanatories.RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe: The theorem states that the ring homomorphism associated with a ring equivalence is equal to the equivalence itself considered as a function.
explanatories.RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom: This theorem asserts that the function corresponding to a ring equivalence is equal to the function obtained by considering the ring equivalence as a ring homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.coe_ringEquiv: This theorem shows that the function associated with an algebraic equivalence can be represented equivalently through two notations, confirming their equality.
explanatories.Nat.cast_one: The theorem asserts that the natural number one, when cast into an additive monoid with a unity element, is equal to the identity element of that monoid.
explanatories.ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff: This theorem establishes that two natural numbers are equal when cast to the finite modulo structure if and only if they are congruent modulo a specified integer.
explanatories.pow_eq_pow_iff_modEq: This theorem states that in a left canceling monoid, two powers of an element are equal if and only if the exponents are congruent modulo the order of that element.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.mul_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the application of the product of two algebra equivalences to an element is equal to first applying one equivalence and then the other, preserving the structure of the algebra.

IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow.fullDefinition: noncomputable def autToPow : (S ≃ₐ[R] S) →* (ZMod n)ˣ :=   let μ' := hμ.toRootsOfUnity   have ho : orderOf μ' = n := by     rw [hμ.eq_orderOf, ← hμ.val_toRootsOfUnity_coe, orderOf_units, Subgroup.orderOf_coe]   MonoidHom.toHomUnits     { toFun := fun σ => (map_rootsOfUnity_eq_pow_self σ.toAlgHom μ').choose       map_one' := by         dsimp only         generalize_proofs h1         have h := h1.choose_spec         dsimp only [μ', AlgEquiv.one_apply, AlgEquiv.toRingEquiv_eq_coe, RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe,           RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, AlgEquiv.coe_ringEquiv] at *         replace h : μ' = μ' ^ h1.choose :=           rootsOfUnity.coe_injective (by simpa only [rootsOfUnity.coe_pow] using h)         nth_rw 1 [← pow_one μ'] at h         rw [← Nat.cast_one, ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff, ← ho, ← pow_eq_pow_iff_modEq, h]       map_mul' := by         intro x y         dsimp only         generalize_proofs hxy' hx' hy'         have hxy := hxy'.choose_spec         have hx := hx'.choose_spec         have hy := hy'.choose_spec         dsimp only [μ', AlgEquiv.toRingEquiv_eq_coe, RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe,           RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, AlgEquiv.coe_ringEquiv, AlgEquiv.mul_apply] at *         replace hxy : x (((μ' : Sˣ) : S) ^ hy'.choose) = ((μ' : Sˣ) : S) ^ hxy'.choose := hy ▸ hxy         rw [map_pow] at hxy         replace hxy : (((μ' : Sˣ) : S) ^ hx'.choose) ^ hy'.choose = ((μ' : Sˣ) : S) ^ hxy'.choose :=           hx ▸ hxy         rw [← pow_mul] at hxy         replace hxy : μ' ^ (hx'.choose * hy'.choose) = μ' ^ hxy'.choose :=           rootsOfUnity.coe_injective (by simpa only [rootsOfUnity.coe_pow] using hxy)         rw [← Nat.cast_mul, ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff, ← ho, ← pow_eq_pow_iff_modEq, hxy] }
IsPrimitiveRoot.autToPow.description: This defines a homomorphism from the algebra of automorphisms of a domain to the multiplicative group of units in the finite field modulo a positive integer, which maps each automorphism to the power of an element that it transforms.

explanatories.Polynomial.coeff: This definition identifies a function that retrieves the coefficient of a specified power in a polynomial over a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff_mul: This theorem expresses the coefficient of the product of two polynomials at a specific index as a sum of the products of their coefficients from pairs of indices that add up to that index.
explanatories.Ideal.sum_mem: The sum of elements from a finite set that belong to an ideal also belongs to the same ideal.
explanatories.Finset.HasAntidiagonal.mem_antidiagonal: A pair belongs to the antidiagonal of an element if and only if the sum of its two components equals that element.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.Ideal.mul_mem_mul: The product of any element from one ideal and any element from another ideal is contained in the product of those ideals.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff_one: This theorem states that the coefficient of the constant polynomial one at degree n is one if n is zero and zero otherwise.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff_add: This theorem states that the coefficient of a polynomial sum at a given index is the sum of the coefficients of the individual polynomials at that same index.
explanatories.Ideal.add_mem: The sum of any two elements in an ideal of a semiring is also contained within that ideal.
explanatories.Ideal.zero_mem: The zero element belongs to any ideal in a semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.algebraMap_apply: This theorem states that applying the algebra map from a commutative semiring to polynomials yields a polynomial representation of the image of the element under the algebra map to the base semiring.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff_C: This theorem asserts that the coefficient of a constant polynomial at any degree is equal to the constant itself when the degree is zero, and is zero for all other degrees.

IsAdicComplete.henselianRing.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)     [IsAdicComplete I R] : HenselianRing R I where   jac := IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot _   is_henselian := by     intro f _ a₀ h₁ h₂     classical       let f' := derivative f       -- we define a sequence `c n` by starting at `a₀` and then continually       -- applying the function sending `b` to `b - f(b)/f'(b)` (Newton's method).       -- Note that `f'.eval b` is a unit, because `b` has the same residue as `a₀` modulo `I`.       let c : ℕ → R := fun n => Nat.recOn n a₀ fun _ b => b - f.eval b * Ring.inverse (f'.eval b)       have hc : ∀ n, c (n + 1) = c n - f.eval (c n) * Ring.inverse (f'.eval (c n)) := by         intro n         simp only [c, Nat.rec_add_one]       -- we now spend some time determining properties of the sequence `c : ℕ → R`       -- `hc_mod`: for every `n`, we have `c n ≡ a₀ [SMOD I]`       -- `hf'c`  : for every `n`, `f'.eval (c n)` is a unit       -- `hfcI`  : for every `n`, `f.eval (c n)` is contained in `I ^ (n+1)`       have hc_mod : ∀ n, c n ≡ a₀ [SMOD I] := by         intro n         induction' n with n ih         · rfl         rw [hc, sub_eq_add_neg, ← add_zero a₀]         refine ih.add ?_         rw [SModEq.zero, Ideal.neg_mem_iff]         refine I.mul_mem_right _ ?_         rw [← SModEq.zero] at h₁ ⊢         exact (ih.eval f).trans h₁       have hf'c : ∀ n, IsUnit (f'.eval (c n)) := by         intro n         haveI := isLocalRingHom_of_le_jacobson_bot I (IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot I)         apply isUnit_of_map_unit (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)         convert h₂ using 1         exact SModEq.def.mp ((hc_mod n).eval _)       have hfcI : ∀ n, f.eval (c n) ∈ I ^ (n + 1) := by         intro n         induction' n with n ih         · simpa only [Nat.zero_eq, Nat.rec_zero, zero_add, pow_one] using h₁         rw [← taylor_eval_sub (c n), hc, sub_eq_add_neg, sub_eq_add_neg,           add_neg_cancel_comm]         rw [eval_eq_sum, sum_over_range' _ _ _ (lt_add_of_pos_right _ zero_lt_two), ←           Finset.sum_range_add_sum_Ico _ (Nat.le_add_left _ _)]         swap         · intro i           rw [zero_mul]         refine Ideal.add_mem _ ?_ ?_         · erw [Finset.sum_range_succ]           rw [Finset.range_one, Finset.sum_singleton,             taylor_coeff_zero, taylor_coeff_one, pow_zero, pow_one, mul_one, mul_neg,             mul_left_comm, Ring.mul_inverse_cancel _ (hf'c n), mul_one, add_neg_self]           exact Ideal.zero_mem _         · refine Submodule.sum_mem _ ?_           simp only [Finset.mem_Ico]           rintro i ⟨h2i, _⟩           have aux : n + 2 ≤ i * (n + 1) := by trans 2 * (n + 1) <;> nlinarith only [h2i]           refine Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right aux ?_)           rw [pow_mul']           exact Ideal.pow_mem_pow ((Ideal.neg_mem_iff _).2 <| Ideal.mul_mem_right _ _ ih) _       -- we are now in the position to show that `c : ℕ → R` is a Cauchy sequence       have aux : ∀ m n, m ≤ n → c m ≡ c n [SMOD (I ^ m • ⊤ : Ideal R)] := by         intro m n hmn         rw [← Ideal.one_eq_top, Ideal.smul_eq_mul, mul_one]         obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hmn         clear hmn         induction' k with k ih         · rw [add_zero]         rw [← add_assoc]

tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_localRing_of.code:
tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_localRing_of_isDomain.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [LocalRing R]
  [IsDomain R] :
  [IsPrincipalIdealRing R, ValuationRing R, IsDedekindDomain R,
      IsIntegrallyClosed R ∧ ∀ (P : Ideal R), P ≠ ⊥ → P.IsPrime → P = maximalIdeal R,
      Submodule.IsPrincipal (maximalIdeal R), finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) ≤ 1,
      ∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊥ → ∃ n, I = maximalIdeal R ^ n].TFAE
tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_localRing_of.comment:
Let `(R, m, k)` be a noetherian local domain (possibly a field).
The following are equivalent:
0. `R` is a PID
1. `R` is a valuation ring
2. `R` is a dedekind domain
3. `R` is integrally closed with at most one non-zero prime ideal
4. `m` is principal
5. `dimₖ m/m² ≤ 1`
6. Every nonzero ideal is a power of `m`.

Also see `DiscreteValuationRing.TFAE` for a version assuming `¬ IsField R`.

Algebra.TensorProduct.ext.comment:
A version of `TensorProduct.ext` for `AlgHom`.

Using this as the `@[ext]` lemma instead of `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext'` allows `ext` to apply
lemmas specific to `A →ₐ[S] _` and `B →ₐ[R] _`; notably this allows recursion into nested tensor
products of algebras.

See note [partially-applied ext lemmas].

explanatories.Algebra.TensorProduct.ext: The theorem demonstrates that if two algebra homomorphisms from the tensor product of two algebras to a third algebra yield the same result when composed with the left inclusion or the right restriction of scalars, then these two homomorphisms are identical.
explanatories.AlgHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two algebra homomorphisms are identical if they yield the same output for every element in the source algebra.

explanatories.Basis.ext: This theorem asserts that two linear maps are identical if they produce the same output for every basis vector.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.ext: The theorem asserts that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module produce the same outputs for all combinations of inputs from the first two modules, then those linear maps are identical.

Algebra.TensorProduct.productLeftAlgHom.comment:
If `A`, `B`, `C` are `R`-algebras, `A` and `C` are also `S`-algebras (forming a tower as
`·/S/R`), then the product map of `f : A →ₐ[S] C` and `g : B →ₐ[R] C` is an `S`-algebra
homomorphism.

This is just a special case of `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` for when `C` is commutative.

LinearMap.tensorProduct.comment:
The natural linear map $A ⊗ \text{Hom}_R(M, N) → \text{Hom}_A (M_A, N_A)$,
where $M_A$ and $N_A$ are the respective modules over $A$ obtained by extension of scalars.

See `LinearMap.tensorProductEnd` for this map specialized to endomorphisms,
and bundled as `A`-algebra homomorphism.

module.End.division_ring.description: The endomorphism ring of a simple module is structured as a division ring according to Schur's Lemma.

Algebra.Generators.Hom.comp.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Hom.comp (f : Hom P' P'') (g : Hom P P') : Hom P P'' where   val x := aeval f.val (g.val x)   aeval_val x := by     simp only     rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply S S' S'', ← g.aeval_val]     induction g.val x using MvPolynomial.induction_on with     | h_C r => simp [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]     | h_add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]     | h_X p i hp => simp only [_root_.map_mul, hp, aeval_X, aeval_val]
Algebra.Generators.Hom.comp.description: This defines the composition of two homomorphisms between different generators of commutative rings, resulting in a new homomorphism.

Algebra.Generators.comp.fullDefinition: def comp (Q : Generators S T) (P : Generators R S) : Generators R T where   vars := Q.vars ⊕ P.vars   val := Sum.elim Q.val (algebraMap S T ∘ P.val)   σ' x := (Q.σ x).sum (fun n r ↦ rename Sum.inr (P.σ r) * monomial (n.mapDomain Sum.inl) 1)   aeval_val_σ' s := by     have (x : P.Ring) : aeval (algebraMap S T ∘ P.val) x = algebraMap S T (aeval P.val x) := by       rw [map_aeval, aeval_def, coe_eval₂Hom, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq, Function.comp]     conv_rhs => rw [← Q.aeval_val_σ s, ← (Q.σ s).sum_single]     simp only [map_finsupp_sum, _root_.map_mul, aeval_rename, Sum.elim_comp_inr, this, aeval_val_σ,       aeval_monomial, _root_.map_one, Finsupp.prod_mapDomain_index_inj Sum.inl_injective,       Sum.elim_inl, one_mul, single_eq_monomial]
Algebra.Generators.comp.description: This definition describes a way to combine two generator families from separate algebraic structures to create a new family of generators for a third structure.

Bialgebra.mul_compr₂_counit.code:
Bialgebra.mul_compr₂_counit.{u, v} {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [self : Bialgebra R A] :
  (LinearMap.mul R A).compr₂ counit = (LinearMap.mul R R).compl₁₂ counit counit
Bialgebra.mul_compr₂_counit.comment:
The counit on a bialgebra preserves multiplication. Note that this is written
in a rather obscure way: it says that two bilinear maps `A →ₗ[R] A →ₗ[R]` are equal.
The two corresponding equal linear maps `A ⊗[R] A →ₗ[R]`
are the following: the first factors through `A` and is multiplication on `A` followed
by `counit`. The second factors through `R ⊗[R] R`, and is `counit ⊗ counit` followed by
multiplication on `R`.

See `Bialgebra.mk'` for a constructor for bialgebras which uses
the more familiar but mathematically equivalent `counit (a * b) = counit a * counit b`.

Bialgebra.mul_compr₂_comul.code:
Bialgebra.mul_compr₂_comul.{u, v} {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [self : Bialgebra R A] :
  (LinearMap.mul R A).compr₂ comul = (LinearMap.mul R (A ⊗[R] A)).compl₁₂ comul comul
Bialgebra.mul_compr₂_comul.comment:
The comultiplication on a bialgebra preserves multiplication. This is written in
a rather obscure way: it says that two bilinear maps `A →ₗ[R] A →ₗ[R] (A ⊗[R] A)`
are equal. The corresponding equal linear maps `A ⊗[R] A →ₗ[R] A ⊗[R] A`
are firstly multiplcation followed by `comul`, and secondly `comul ⊗ comul` followed
by multiplication on `A ⊗[R] A`.

See `Bialgebra.mk'` for a constructor for bialgebras which uses the more familiar
but mathematically equivalent `comul (a * b) = comul a * comul b`.

Algebra.pushoutDesc.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Algebra.pushoutDesc [H : Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'] {A : Type*} [Semiring A]     [Algebra R A] (f : S →ₐ[R] A) (g : R' →ₐ[R] A) (hf : ∀ x y, f x * g y = g y * f x) :     S' →ₐ[R] A := by   letI := Module.compHom A f.toRingHom   haveI : IsScalarTower R S A :=     { smul_assoc := fun r s a =>         show f (r • s) * a = r • (f s * a) by rw [map_smul, smul_mul_assoc] }   haveI : IsScalarTower S A A := { smul_assoc := fun r a b => mul_assoc _ _ _ }   have : ∀ x, H.out.lift g.toLinearMap (algebraMap R' S' x) = g x := H.out.lift_eq _   refine AlgHom.ofLinearMap ((H.out.lift g.toLinearMap).restrictScalars R) ?_ ?_   · dsimp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply]     rw [← (algebraMap R' S').map_one, this, _root_.map_one]   · intro x y     refine H.out.inductionOn x ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_     · rw [zero_mul, map_zero, zero_mul]     rotate_left     · intro s s' e       dsimp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply] at e ⊢       rw [LinearMap.map_smul, smul_mul_assoc, LinearMap.map_smul, e, smul_mul_assoc]     · intro s s' e₁ e₂       dsimp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply] at e₁ e₂ ⊢       rw [add_mul, map_add, map_add, add_mul, e₁, e₂]     intro x     dsimp     rw [this]     refine H.out.inductionOn y ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_     · rw [mul_zero, map_zero, mul_zero]     · intro y       dsimp       rw [← _root_.map_mul, this, this, _root_.map_mul]     · intro s s' e       rw [mul_comm, smul_mul_assoc, LinearMap.map_smul, LinearMap.map_smul, mul_comm, e]       change f s * (g x * _) = g x * (f s * _)       rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, hf]     · intro s s' e₁ e₂       rw [mul_add, map_add, map_add, mul_add, e₁, e₂]

algebra.pushout_desc.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Algebra.pushoutDesc [H : Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'] {A : Type*} [Semiring A]     [Algebra R A] (f : S →ₐ[R] A) (g : R' →ₐ[R] A) (hf : ∀ x y, f x * g y = g y * f x) :     S' →ₐ[R] A := by   letI := Module.compHom A f.toRingHom   haveI : IsScalarTower R S A :=     { smul_assoc := fun r s a =>         show f (r • s) * a = r • (f s * a) by rw [map_smul, smul_mul_assoc] }   haveI : IsScalarTower S A A := { smul_assoc := fun r a b => mul_assoc _ _ _ }   have : ∀ x, H.out.lift g.toLinearMap (algebraMap R' S' x) = g x := H.out.lift_eq _   refine AlgHom.ofLinearMap ((H.out.lift g.toLinearMap).restrictScalars R) ?_ ?_   · dsimp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply]     rw [← (algebraMap R' S').map_one, this, _root_.map_one]   · intro x y     refine H.out.inductionOn x ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_     · rw [zero_mul, map_zero, zero_mul]     rotate_left     · intro s s' e       dsimp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply] at e ⊢       rw [LinearMap.map_smul, smul_mul_assoc, LinearMap.map_smul, e, smul_mul_assoc]     · intro s s' e₁ e₂       dsimp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply] at e₁ e₂ ⊢       rw [add_mul, map_add, map_add, add_mul, e₁, e₂]     intro x     dsimp     rw [this]     refine H.out.inductionOn y ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_     · rw [mul_zero, map_zero, mul_zero]     · intro y       dsimp       rw [← _root_.map_mul, this, this, _root_.map_mul]     · intro s s' e       rw [mul_comm, smul_mul_assoc, LinearMap.map_smul, LinearMap.map_smul, mul_comm, e]       change f s * (g x * _) = g x * (f s * _)       rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, hf]     · intro s s' e₁ e₂       rw [mul_add, map_add, map_add, mul_add, e₁, e₂]
algebra.pushout_desc.description: When given compatible algebra homomorphisms from two algebras to another while assuming the target algebra is a pushout of the two, a unique algebra homomorphism can be constructed from their tensor product to that target.

Algebra.Presentation.dimension.comment:
Dimension of a presentation defined as the cardinality of the generators
minus the cardinality of the relations.

even then for this to make sense, you should assume that the presentation
is a complete intersection.

explanatories.Submodule.mapQLinear: This definition describes a linear mapping that translates compatible linear maps between two modules to a linear map between their respective quotient modules formed by their submodules.
explanatories.LinearMap.codRestrict: This definition describes a linear map that restricts the codomain of a given linear map to a specified submodule, ensuring that all outputs lie within that submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.map_le_iff_le_comap: The theorem establishes a condition under which the image of a submodule under a semilinear map is contained in another submodule if and only if the original submodule is contained in the preimage of that other submodule.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.le_of_eq_of_le: If two elements are equal and the second element is less than or equal to a third element, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third element.
explanatories.smul_mono_right: This theorem states that in a structure equipped with a scalar multiplication and a preorder, scalar multiplication by a fixed element preserves the order relation among elements.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.

QuotSMulTop.map.fullDefinition: def map : (M →ₗ[R] M') →ₗ[R] QuotSMulTop r M →ₗ[R] QuotSMulTop r M'  :=   Submodule.mapQLinear _ _ ∘ₗ LinearMap.id.codRestrict _ fun _ =>     map_le_iff_le_comap.mp <| le_of_eq_of_le (map_pointwise_smul _ _ _) <|       smul_mono_right r le_top

QuotSMulTop.equivQuotTensor.comment: Reducing a module modulo `r` is the same as left tensoring with `R/(r)`.

explanatories.Ideal.span: The ideal generated by a subset of a ring is called the span of that subset.
explanatories.Submodule.quotEquivOfEq: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between the quotient spaces of a module by two equal submodules.
explanatories.Submodule.ideal_span_singleton_smul: The scalar multiplication of a submodule by the ideal generated by a single element is equivalent to multiplying the submodule by that element directly.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.

QuotSMulTop.equivQuotTensor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equivQuotTensor :     QuotSMulTop r M ≃ₗ[R] (R ⧸ Ideal.span {r}) ⊗[R] M :=   quotEquivOfEq _ _ (ideal_span_singleton_smul _ _).symm ≪≫ₗ    (quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M _).symm
QuotSMulTop.equivQuotTensor.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the quotient of a module by a submodule generated by a ring element and the tensor product of the field quotient by that element with the module itself.

Derivation.tensorProductTo.comment: For a `R`-derivation `S → M`, this is the map `S ⊗[R] S →ₗ[S] M` sending `s ⊗ₜ t ↦ s • D t`.

explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lift: The definition describes a process for creating a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module based on a specified bilinear map that holds a particular composition property with respect to a canonical bilinear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.lsmul: This definition describes a bilinear map that represents scalar multiplication, taking a scalar from a commutative semiring and an element from a module to produce a resulting element in the module.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip: This definition describes a process that takes a bilinear map and rearranges the order of its variables to form a new linear map.

Derivation.tensorProductTo.description: The map takes elements from the tensor product of two algebras and sends them to a module by multiplying one factor by the derivation applied to the other.

This is implemented as `I / I ^ 2` with `I` the kernel of the multiplication map `S ⊗[R] S →ₐ[R] S`.

KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal.comment:
The `S`-submodule of `S →₀ S` (the direct sum of copies of `S` indexed by `S`) generated by
the relations:
1. `dx + dy = d(x + y)`
2. `x dy + y dx = d(x * y)`
3. `dr = 0` for `r ∈ R`
where `db` is the unit in the copy of `S` with index `b`.

This is the kernel of the surjection `Finsupp.total S Ω[S⁄R] S (KaehlerDifferential.D R S)`.
See `KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal_eq` and `KaehlerDifferential.total_surjective`.

kaehler_differential.quot_ker_total_equi.fullDefinition: noncomputable def KaehlerDifferential.quotKerTotalEquiv :     ((S →₀ S) ⧸ KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal R S) ≃ₗ[S] Ω[S⁄R] :=   { (KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal R S).liftQ       (Finsupp.total S (Ω[S⁄R]) S (KaehlerDifferential.D R S))       (KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal_eq R S).ge with     invFun := (KaehlerDifferential.derivationQuotKerTotal R S).liftKaehlerDifferential     left_inv := by       intro x       obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective _ x       exact         LinearMap.congr_fun (KaehlerDifferential.derivationQuotKerTotal_lift_comp_total R S : _) x     right_inv := by       intro x       obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := KaehlerDifferential.total_surjective R S x       have := LinearMap.congr_fun (KaehlerDifferential.derivationQuotKerTotal_lift_comp_total R S) x       rw [LinearMap.comp_apply] at this       rw [this]       rfl }

KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal_map.code:
KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal_map.{u, v, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  (A : Type u_2) (B : Type u_3) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra S B]
  [IsScalarTower R A B] [IsScalarTower R S B] (h : Function.Surjective ⇑(algebraMap A B)) :
  Submodule.map (Finsupp.mapRange.linearMap (Algebra.linearMap A B) ∘ₗ Finsupp.lmapDomain A A ⇑(algebraMap A B))
        (KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal R A) ⊔
      Submodule.span A (Set.range fun x => Finsupp.single ((algebraMap S B) x) 1) =
    Submodule.restrictScalars A (KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal S B)
KaehlerDifferential.kerTotal_map.comment:
Given the commutative diagram
```
A --→ B
↑     ↑
|     |
R --→ S
```
The kernel of the presentation `⊕ₓ B dx ↠ Ω_{B/S}` is spanned by the image of the
kernel of `⊕ₓ A dx ↠ Ω_{A/R}` and all `ds` with `s : S`.
See `kerTotal_map'` for the special case where `R = S`.

kernel of `⊕ₓ A dx ↠ Ω_{A/R}` and all `da` with `a : A`.

KaehlerDifferential.mvPolynomialEquiv.fullDefinition: def KaehlerDifferential.mvPolynomialEquiv (σ : Type*) :     Ω[MvPolynomial σ R⁄R] ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial σ R] σ →₀ MvPolynomial σ R where   __ := (MvPolynomial.mkDerivation _ (Finsupp.single · 1)).liftKaehlerDifferential   invFun := Finsupp.total σ _ _ (fun x ↦ D _ _ (MvPolynomial.X x))   right_inv := by     intro x     induction' x using Finsupp.induction_linear with _ _ _ _ a b     · simp only [AddHom.toFun_eq_coe, LinearMap.coe_toAddHom]; rw [map_zero, map_zero]     · simp only [AddHom.toFun_eq_coe, LinearMap.coe_toAddHom, map_add] at *; simp only [*]     · simp [LinearMap.map_smul, -map_smul]   left_inv := by     intro x     obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := total_surjective _ _ x     induction' x using Finsupp.induction_linear with _ _ _ _ a b     · simp only [AddHom.toFun_eq_coe, LinearMap.coe_toAddHom]; rw [map_zero, map_zero, map_zero]     · simp only [map_add, AddHom.toFun_eq_coe, LinearMap.coe_toAddHom] at *; simp only [*]     · simp only [AddHom.toFun_eq_coe, LinearMap.coe_toAddHom, Finsupp.total_single,         LinearMap.map_smul, Derivation.liftKaehlerDifferential_comp_D]       congr 1       induction a using MvPolynomial.induction_on       · simp only [MvPolynomial.derivation_C, map_zero]       · simp only [map_add, *]       · simp [*]

  (f : ι → R) (x : ι → M) : Prop
Module.IsTrivialRelation.comment:
The proposition that the relation $\sum_i f_i x_i = 0$ in $M$ is trivial.
That is, there exist a finite index type $\kappa$, elements
$(y_j)_{j \in \kappa}$ of $M$, and elements $(a_{ij})_{i \in \iota, j \in \kappa}$ of $R$
such that for all $i$,
$$x_i = \sum_j a_{ij} y_j$$
and for all $j$,
$$\sum_{i} f_i a_{ij} = 0.$$
By `Module.sum_smul_eq_zero_of_isTrivialRelation`, this condition implies $\sum_i f_i x_i = 0$.
Module.IsTrivialRelation.fullDefinition: abbrev IsTrivialRelation : Prop :=   ∃ (κ : Type u) (_ : Fintype κ) (a : ι → κ → R) (y : κ → M),     (∀ i, x i = ∑ j, a i j • y j) ∧ ∀ j, ∑ i, f i * a i j = 0
Module.IsTrivialRelation.description: This definition describes a condition under which a linear combination of elements in a module sums to zero based on a specific structure relating the coefficients and elements involved.
