explanatories.Polynomial.Monic: This definition characterizes a polynomial as monic if its leading coefficient is equal to one.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.map: The map associated with the property of being an adjoined root allows the transfer of polynomials from a commutative semiring to another algebra while preserving the algebraic structure.
explanatories.Function.Surjective.subsingleton: There is no theorem or definition provided.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.subsingleton: If the base ring is a subsingleton, then the algebra generated by adjoining a root of a polynomial is also a subsingleton.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.RingHom.map_add: This theorem indicates that a ring homomorphism maintains the property of addition by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.repr: A representative polynomial can be chosen for an element in an algebra generated by adjoining a root of a polynomial, ensuring that mapping this representative returns the original element.
explanatories.RingHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two ring homomorphisms are equal if they yield the same output for every input from the domain.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.ext: Two instances of being an adjoined root are equal if they share the same root.
explanatories.RingHom.coe_mk: This theorem establishes that a ring homomorphism can be constructed from its underlying function along with its properties related to zero and addition.
explanatories.AlgHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two algebra homomorphisms are identical if they yield the same output for every element in the source algebra.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRootMonic.Monic: If a polynomial is monic in the context of being an adjoining root, then it retains its monic property.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRootMonic.modByMonicHom: This definition establishes a linear homomorphism that maps elements of a ring, under the condition of being an adjoined monic root, to their equivalence classes based on the polynomial remainder when reduced by another monic polynomial.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRootMonic.modByMonicHom_map: The theorem states that the image of a polynomial under the homomorphism associated with a monic adjoined root is equal to the polynomial's remainder when divided by the corresponding monic polynomial.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_mk: This theorem asserts that the coercion of a specific additive homomorphism into a linear map retains the property of ensuring the scaling operation is consistently applied to both the original and the resulting functions.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRootMonic.map_modByMonicHom: The map associated with the adjoining of a monic polynomial applied to the homomorphism resulting from reducing an element to a monic polynomial yields the original element in the algebra.
explanatories.Polynomial.modByMonic_eq_self_iff: This theorem establishes that a polynomial equals itself when divided by a monic polynomial if and only if its degree is less than that of the monic polynomial.
explanatories.Basis.ofRepr: This definition establishes a linear equivalence that maps a vector to its coordinates with respect to a given basis.
explanatories.Finsupp.comapDomain: The comapDomain function creates a finitely supported function from one type to another by applying an injective mapping to the support of a given finitely supported function.
explanatories.Fin.val_injective: This theorem states that the function mapping finite natural numbers to their integer representations is injective, meaning it assigns distinct integers to distinct finite natural numbers.
explanatories.Function.Injective.injOn: The theorem asserts that if a function is injective, then it is also injective when restricted to a specific subset of its domain.
explanatories.Polynomial.toFinsupp_add: This theorem demonstrates that the conversion of the sum of two polynomials into a finite sums of monomials corresponds to the sum of their individual conversions into that same form.
explanatories.Finsupp.comapDomain_add_of_injective: The image of the sum of two finitely supported functions under an injective function is equal to the sum of their individual images under that function.
explanatories.map_smul: This theorem states that a morphism that is equivariant with respect to the actions of a monoid preserves the action when applied to the product of an element from the monoid and an element from the type.
explanatories.Polynomial.toFinsupp_smul: This theorem shows that the scalar multiplication of a polynomial can be expressed in terms of the scalar multiplication of its finite sum representation.
explanatories.Finsupp.comapDomain_smul_of_injective: The action of scaling a finitely supported function by a scalar in the codomain can be expressed in terms of the original function scaled by the same scalar if the mapping from the domain is injective.
explanatories.Polynomial.ofFinsupp: This theorem demonstrates that any additive monoid algebra can be represented as a polynomial over a semiring.
explanatories.Finsupp.mapDomain: This definition constructs a finitely supported function in the target domain by summing the values of an original finitely supported function over all elements that map to the same target element through a given function.
explanatories.subsingleton_or_nontrivial: Every type is either a subsingleton or nontrivial.
explanatories.Finsupp.mapDomain_comapDomain: The mapping from a domain to another through an injective function correctly recovers the original finitely supported function under certain conditions on the support set.
explanatories.Polynomial.eta: This theorem asserts that a polynomial over a semiring is equivalent to its representation as an additive monoid algebra when transformed back into a polynomial format.
explanatories.Set.mem_range: An element is in the range of a function if and only if there exists an input that maps to it under the function.
explanatories.Polynomial.toFinsupp_apply: This theorem states that the coefficient of a polynomial at a given index is equal to its representation as a finitely supported function at that index.
explanatories.Classical.not_not: The Double Negation Theorem states that the negation of the negation of a proposition is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an element belongs to the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluated at that element is non-zero.
explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.Finset.mem_coe: This theorem establishes that an element is a member of a finite set when considered as a subset of a larger set if and only if it is a member of the finite set itself.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt: This theorem states that if the natural degree of a polynomial is less than a given natural number, then the coefficient of that natural number in the polynomial is zero.
explanatories.lt_of_lt_of_le: This theorem shows that if one element is less than a second element, and the second element is less than or equal to a third element, then the first element is also less than the third element in a preorder.
explanatories.Polynomial.natDegree_lt_natDegree_iff: This theorem establishes that one polynomial has a strictly lower natural degree than another if and only if its degree is also strictly less than the degree of the other polynomial, given that the first polynomial is non-zero.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_modByMonic_lt: This theorem states that the degree of the remainder obtained from dividing a polynomial by a monic polynomial is strictly less than the degree of the monic polynomial.
explanatories.Finsupp.comapDomain_apply: The theorem establishes that the value of a finitely supported function, when mapped through a domain transformation, equals the original function's value at the transformed input under certain conditions on the mapping.
explanatories.Polynomial.coeff: This definition identifies a function that retrieves the coefficient of a specified power in a polynomial over a semiring.
explanatories.Finsupp.mapDomain_apply: The application of a finitely supported function after mapping its domain through an injective function results in the preservation of values at corresponding original inputs.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_eq_natDegree: This theorem states that for a non-zero polynomial, its degree is equal to the natural degree taken as a natural number.
explanatories.Polynomial.Monic.ne_zero: This theorem asserts that a monic polynomial is not equal to zero.
explanatories.Polynomial.degree_lt_iff_coeff_zero: The degree of a polynomial being less than a natural number is equivalent to all coefficients of the polynomial at indices greater than or equal to that number being zero.
explanatories.Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range: If an element is not in the range of a function, then the result of mapping the domain of a finitely supported function through that function to the given element is zero.
explanatories.not_exists: The negation of the existence of an element satisfying a property is equivalent to the property being false for all elements.
explanatories.Fin.prop: This theorem asserts that every finite natural number represented as a finite index is less than the size of that finite set.
explanatories.LT.lt.not_le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then the second element is not less than or equal to the first.
explanatories.Basis.repr: This definition establishes a linear equivalence that maps a vector to its coordinates with respect to a given basis.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.RingHom.map_add': This theorem asserts that a ring homomorphism preserves the operation of addition when applied to the sum of two elements.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.coe_mk: This theorem shows that the function represented by an algebra equivalence constructed from given properties acts as the intended function between the two algebras.

IsAdjoinRootMonic.basis.fullDefinition: def basis (h : IsAdjoinRootMonic S f) : Basis (Fin (natDegree f)) R S :=   Basis.ofRepr     { toFun := fun x => (h.modByMonicHom x).toFinsupp.comapDomain _ Fin.val_injective.injOn       invFun := fun g => h.map (ofFinsupp (g.mapDomain _))       left_inv := fun x => by         cases subsingleton_or_nontrivial R         · subsingleton [h.subsingleton]         simp only         rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_comapDomain, Polynomial.eta, h.map_modByMonicHom x]         · exact Fin.val_injective         intro i hi         refine Set.mem_range.mpr ⟨⟨i, ?_⟩, rfl⟩         contrapose! hi         simp only [Polynomial.toFinsupp_apply, Classical.not_not, Finsupp.mem_support_iff, Ne,           modByMonicHom, LinearMap.coe_mk, Finset.mem_coe]         by_cases hx : h.toIsAdjoinRoot.repr x %ₘ f = 0         · simp [hx]         refine coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt (lt_of_lt_of_le ?_ hi)         dsimp -- Porting note (#11227):added a `dsimp`         rw [natDegree_lt_natDegree_iff hx]         exact degree_modByMonic_lt _ h.Monic       right_inv := fun g => by         nontriviality R         ext i         simp only [h.modByMonicHom_map, Finsupp.comapDomain_apply, Polynomial.toFinsupp_apply]         rw [(Polynomial.modByMonic_eq_self_iff h.Monic).mpr, Polynomial.coeff]         · dsimp only -- Porting note (#10752): added `dsimp only`           rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_apply Fin.val_injective]         rw [degree_eq_natDegree h.Monic.ne_zero, degree_lt_iff_coeff_zero]         intro m hm         rw [Polynomial.coeff]         dsimp only -- Porting note (#10752): added `dsimp only`         rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range]         rw [Set.mem_range, not_exists]         rintro i rfl         exact i.prop.not_le hm       map_add' := fun x y => by         beta_reduce -- Porting note (#12129): additional beta reduction needed         rw [map_add, toFinsupp_add, Finsupp.comapDomain_add_of_injective Fin.val_injective]       -- Porting note: the original simp proof with the same lemmas does not work       -- See https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/issues/5026       -- simp only [map_add, Finsupp.comapDomain_add_of_injective Fin.val_injective, toFinsupp_add]       map_smul' := fun c x => by         dsimp only -- Porting note (#10752): added `dsimp only`         rw [map_smul, toFinsupp_smul, Finsupp.comapDomain_smul_of_injective Fin.val_injective,           RingHom.id_apply] }       -- Porting note: the original simp proof with the same lemmas does not work       -- See https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/issues/5026       -- simp only [map_smul, Finsupp.comapDomain_smul_of_injective Fin.val_injective,       --   RingHom.id_apply, toFinsupp_smul] }

IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv.code:
IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv.{u, v, u_1} {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {f : R[X]}
  {T : Type u_1} [CommRing T] [Algebra R T] (h : IsAdjoinRoot S f) (h' : IsAdjoinRoot T f) : S ≃ₐ[R] T
IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv.comment:
Adjoining a root gives a unique ring up to algebra isomorphism.

This is the converse of `IsAdjoinRoot.ofEquiv`: this turns an `IsAdjoinRoot` into an
`AlgEquiv`, and `IsAdjoinRoot.ofEquiv` turns an `AlgEquiv` into an `IsAdjoinRoot`.

explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.root: The root of a polynomial that is adjoined to a structure generates that structure within the context of the given algebra.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.aeval_eq: The evaluation of a polynomial at the root of the adjoined polynomial is equal to the result of mapping that polynomial through the associated adjoined root map.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.aeval_root: The evaluation of the polynomial at its adjoined root is equal to zero.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.map_repr: The mapping of a chosen representative polynomial for an element in an algebra generated by adjoining a root of a polynomial accurately retrieves the original element.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.liftHom: The definition describes a way to extend an algebra homomorphism from a commutative ring to a larger algebra by incorporating a specific root of a polynomial that defines the adjunction.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.liftHom_map: The theorem asserts that applying a homomorphism to the mapping of a polynomial through an adjoined root yields the same result as evaluating the polynomial at that root.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.root: The definition specifies the adjoined root of a polynomial as an element within the structure created by adjoining that root to the underlying ring.

IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv.fullDefinition: def aequiv (h : IsAdjoinRoot S f) (h' : IsAdjoinRoot T f) : S ≃ₐ[R] T :=   { h.liftHom h'.root h'.aeval_root with     toFun := h.liftHom h'.root h'.aeval_root     invFun := h'.liftHom h.root h.aeval_root     left_inv := fun x => by rw [← h.map_repr x, liftHom_map, aeval_eq, liftHom_map, aeval_eq]     right_inv := fun x => by rw [← h'.map_repr x, liftHom_map, aeval_eq, liftHom_map, aeval_eq] }
IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv.description: The introduction of two algebras generated by adjoining the root of the same polynomial establishes an isomorphism between them.

IsAdjoinRoot.ofEquiv.comment:
Transfer `IsAdjoinRoot` across an algebra isomorphism.

This is the converse of `IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv`: this turns an `AlgEquiv` into an `IsAdjoinRoot`,
and `IsAdjoinRoot.aequiv` turns an `IsAdjoinRoot` into an `AlgEquiv`.

explanatories.RingHom.comp: This definition establishes that the composition of two ring homomorphisms results in another ring homomorphism.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.map: The map associated with the property of being an adjoined root allows the transfer of polynomials from a commutative semiring to another algebra while preserving the algebraic structure.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.map_surjective: The map associated with being an adjoined root is surjective, meaning every element in the target algebra can be reached from some polynomial in the source semiring.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.algebraMap_eq: The algebra map from a commutative semiring to an algebra is equal to the composition of the map from the adjoining property and the constant polynomial function.
explanatories.RingHom.comp_apply: This theorem asserts that the composition of two ring homomorphisms applied to an element is equal to the application of the second homomorphism followed by the application of the first homomorphism.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.algebraMap_apply: The application of the algebra map from the base commutative ring to the algebra generated by adjoining a root of a polynomial is equivalent to mapping the constant polynomial associated with an element of the ring.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.ker_map: The kernel of the map related to being an adjoined root corresponds precisely to the ideal generated by the polynomial defining the adjoined root.
explanatories.RingHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two ring homomorphisms are equal if they yield the same output for every input from the domain.
explanatories.IsAdjoinRoot.ext: Two instances of being an adjoined root are equal if they share the same root.
explanatories.AlgHom.ext: This theorem asserts that two algebra homomorphisms are identical if they yield the same output for every element in the source algebra.
explanatories.AlgHom.commutes: This theorem demonstrates that an algebra homomorphism commutes with the algebra maps from a commutative semiring to its algebras.
explanatories.AdjoinRoot.algebraMap_eq: The theorem states that the algebra map from a commutative ring to the adjoined root of a polynomial is equal to the mapping of the polynomial itself into the adjoined structure.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.surjective: An algebra equivalence is surjective, indicating that every element in the second algebra is the image of some element from the first algebra.
explanatories.Function.Surjective.comp: This statement suggests that function composition involves applying one function to the result of another function, thereby linking their operations together.
explanatories.RingHom.comap_ker: The preimage of the kernel of a ring homomorphism under another ring homomorphism is equal to the kernel of the composition of those two homomorphisms.
explanatories.RingHom.ker_coe_equiv: The kernel of a ring isomorphism between a ring and a semiring is trivial, meaning it contains only the zero element.
explanatories.RingHom.ker_eq_comap_bot: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is equal to the ideal that consists of all elements mapped to zero, represented as the comap of the homomorphism to the zero ideal.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.commutes: An algebra equivalence between two algebras over a commutative semiring commutes with the action of scalars from that semiring.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.coe_ringEquiv: This theorem shows that the function associated with an algebraic equivalence can be represented equivalently through two notations, confirming their equality.
explanatories.RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom: This theorem asserts that the function corresponding to a ring equivalence is equal to the function obtained by considering the ring equivalence as a ring homomorphism.

MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal.fullDefinition: def vanishingIdeal (V : Set (σ → k)) : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ k) where   carrier := {p | ∀ x ∈ V, eval x p = 0}   zero_mem' x _ := RingHom.map_zero _   add_mem' {p q} hp hq x hx := by simp only [hq x hx, hp x hx, add_zero, RingHom.map_add]   smul_mem' p q hq x hx := by     simp only [hq x hx, Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul, mul_zero, RingHom.map_mul]

littleWedderburn.code: littleWedderburn.{u_1} (D : Type u_1) [DivisionRing D] [Finite D] : Field D
littleWedderburn.comment:
A finite division ring is a field. See `Finite.isDomain_to_isField` and
`Fintype.divisionRingOfIsDomain` for more general statements, but these create data, and therefore
may cause diamonds if used improperly.

This theorem asserts that the center of a finite division ring is the entire ring itself.

littleWedderburn.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) littleWedderburn (D : Type*) [DivisionRing D] [Finite D] : Field D :=   { ‹DivisionRing D› with     mul_comm := fun x y ↦ by simp [Subring.mem_center_iff.mp ?_ x, center_eq_top D] }
littleWedderburn.description: This definition establishes that every finite division ring is a field.

  {L : Type v} (E : Type z) [Field K] [Field L] [Field E] [Algebra K L] [Algebra K E] [Module.Finite K L]
  [IsAlgClosed E] (b : ι → L) [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] (e : ι ≃ (L →ₐ[K] E)) :
  (algebraMap K E) (discr K b) = (embeddingsMatrixReindex K E b e).det ^ 2
Algebra.discr_eq_det_embeddingsMatrixRei.comment:
If `L/K` is a field extension and `b : ι → L`, then `discr K b` is the square of the
determinant of the matrix whose `(i, j)` coefficient is `σⱼ (b i)`, where `σⱼ : L →ₐ[K] E` is the
embedding in an algebraically closed field `E` corresponding to `j : ι` via a bijection
`e : ι ≃ (L →ₐ[K] E)`.

explanatories.AlgEquiv.injective: An algebra equivalence is injective, meaning that different elements in the first algebra map to different elements in the second algebra.

galRestrictHom.fullDefinition: def galRestrictHom : (L →ₐ[K] L) ≃* (B →ₐ[A] B) where   toFun := fun f ↦ (IsIntegralClosure.equiv A (integralClosure A L) L B).toAlgHom.comp       (((f.restrictScalars A).comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A B L)).codRestrict         (integralClosure A L) (fun x ↦ IsIntegral.map _ (IsIntegralClosure.isIntegral A L x)))   map_mul' := by     intros σ₁ σ₂     ext x     apply (IsIntegralClosure.equiv A (integralClosure A L) L B).symm.injective     ext     dsimp     simp only [AlgEquiv.symm_apply_apply, AlgHom.coe_codRestrict, AlgHom.coe_comp,       AlgHom.coe_restrictScalars', IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom', Function.comp_apply,       AlgHom.mul_apply, IsIntegralClosure.algebraMap_equiv, Subalgebra.algebraMap_eq]     rfl   invFun := galLift A K L B   left_inv σ :=     have := (IsFractionRing.injective A K).isDomain     have := IsIntegralClosure.isLocalization A K L B     AlgHom.coe_ringHom_injective <| IsLocalization.ringHom_ext (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid B A⁰)       <| RingHom.ext fun x ↦ by simp [Subalgebra.algebraMap_eq, galLift]   right_inv σ :=     have := (IsFractionRing.injective A K).isDomain     have := IsIntegralClosure.isLocalization A K L B     AlgHom.ext fun x ↦       IsIntegralClosure.algebraMap_injective B A L (by simp [Subalgebra.algebraMap_eq, galLift])
